summary: Write, from the code, how a tester reaches each VS Code item, using the cheap model
logs: paths: 791 items returned for 791 asked; 0 areas returned nothing

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud (also the Sign in button in the Settings panel)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Sign In to AGI Cloud" and press Enter.
Finish the approval in the browser page that opens, then return to VS Code.
Look at the AGI panel: the signed-in account state should show, as Expected says.
items.needs: a browser and an AGI account (or a way to create one)

labels.text: Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud

items.note: The browser handoff lives in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/account-auth/deviceAuth.ts; the quoted line in the plan was not found, but the sign-in command and device flow are present.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud, then the browser page > Create account
steps: Sign out of AGI Cloud in VS Code if signed in, then press Cmd+Shift+P and run "Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud".
In the browser page that opens, look for the "Create account" link beside the sign-in link.
Click "Create account" and check that a sign-up page opens, as Expected says.
items.needs: a browser and an email address or a supported provider account; not signed in to AGI Cloud

labels.text: Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud

items.note: The sign-up link is in apps/web/app/auth/device/page.tsx, linked to /signup; the page's condition for showing the link was not traced, so the tester should confirm it appears while signed out.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory (or Get started with AGI Code walkthrough > Decide what AGI remembers > Open Memory)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory" and press Enter.
Read the memory choice shown, then run "Code: Turn Memory On or Off" from the palette to choose whether memory is used.
Run "Code: Turn Memory On or Off" again to change the choice and check the memory state changes, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account

labels.text: Code: Turn Memory On or Off

items.note: The walkthrough step explains memory; the choice is changed through the Memory commands, not a setup screen that asks at first run. The plan's Code line pointed at package.json:878, which holds that step.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Remote Control, then the Pair a phone button
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Remote Control" and press Enter.
In the panel titled "Remote Control", click "Pair a phone".
On the phone, open the AGI Mobile app and pair with the desktop by scanning the Pairing QR code shown (or typing the pairing code).
Check the panel changes to connected for that phone, and that the pairing code expires in a few minutes, as Expected says.
items.needs: a phone with the AGI Mobile app, and an AGI account signed in on both
items.note: The account binding is set in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts, which the tester cannot see; the phone-side wording 'Pair with Desktop' comes from vscode.json remote.howToPair, not verified in the mobile app.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Getting Started (first-run setup screen in the AGI sidebar)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Show Getting Started" and press Enter.
Read the first screen "Work with your code", then click Next to move through the steps.
On the last step click the button shown there ("Open chat" with no runtime, otherwise "Done").
Check that you land on a first chat, as Expected says.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code that runs after the last step (completeOnboarding in ChatStateManager) was not traced to confirm it opens a chat; the first-run screen shows automatically only when it has not been seen before.

items.where: Get started with AGI Code (VS Code walkthrough), and Code: Show Getting Started for the first-run steps
steps: Open the walkthrough "Get started with AGI Code" from VS Code's Welcome or Get Started page.
Complete one step, such as "Decide what AGI remembers" by clicking its Open Memory link, then close VS Code.
Reopen VS Code and the walkthrough, and check the completed step is still ticked, as Expected says.
Optionally, run "Code: Show Getting Started" and click Next once, then close and reopen the window to see whether the screen restarts at its first step.
items.needs: none
items.note: The walkthrough's saved progress is VS Code's own walkthrough state, not code in the extension, and the first-run screen step index is not saved (only the seen flag is), so resuming there is unverified. Opening the walkthrough from the Welcome page was not traced in the code.

items.needs: a Free account or no account

labels.text: Sign in for AGI subscription features. Local and provider BYOK do not require an AGI plan.
Sign in or add a provider key

items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for guest, sign-up, and carry-over wording and found no guest mode or guest-to-account conversion. Only partial evidence: without sign-in, Local and provider BYOK models are shown as usable ('On this device'), and locked cloud models ask for a sign-in or provider key.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > New chat (+ button in the header, tooltip "New chat"); command palette: Code: New Conversation
steps: Sign in, then open AGI Code from the activity bar (or run Code: Open Chat).
Click the + button whose tooltip is "New chat".
Look for an empty chat with a composer that says "Describe a task…" and type a first message to start a new conversation.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: Empty-state and composer exist in code; not run.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > Sessions (history icon in the header) > click a session row; command palette: Code: Open Conversation
steps: Click the history icon with tooltip "Sessions" in the AGI Code header.
Click one session in the list.
Check that its transcript opens and that you can send a new message to continue it.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one past session
items.note: The plan's Code line pointed at commandSetup.ts:1243 (now the sign-out handler). The open-session command is agi-workforce.openConversation at apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1392.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > Sessions (history icon) > Search sessions box; also command palette: Code: Show Sessions History
steps: Click the "Sessions" icon in the AGI Code header.
Click the "Search sessions" box and type a word from a session title.
Clear it and type a word that appears only inside a message body.
Click a matching result and check it opens that session.
items.needs: a signed-in account with several past sessions
items.note: The quick-pick version says "Search sessions by title or message text" (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json). Whether the sheet box matches message text was not verified in code.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > Sessions (history icon) > Archived sessions (archive icon); command palette: Code: Archived Sessions
steps: Click "Sessions" in the AGI Code header.
Click the archive icon labelled "Archived sessions".
Select a session and click the Restore button, or the Delete permanently button.
Confirm the delete prompt if you chose it; check the session is back in the list or gone from the archive.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one archived session

items.where: AGI Code header > More (…) > Projects; command palette: Code: Show Projects
steps: Click the "More" button in the AGI Code header.
Click "Projects".
Check the list opens with the placeholder "Open a project…".
Click the "New project" icon in the list's title bar and check the create flow starts.
items.needs: a signed-in account

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Projects > click a project
steps: Click "More" in the AGI Code header, then "Projects".
Click a project in the list.
Check the project home shows its name, an "About" section with description and instructions, "Knowledge files" and "Recent conversations".
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
items.note: The project home is a quick-pick list, not a full page.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Projects > click a project > "Recent conversations" section > click a conversation
steps: Open a project from More > Projects.
Scroll to the "Recent conversations" section.
Click one conversation.
Check that it opens; the code opens it in the web app in the browser, not inside the editor.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a project that has conversations
items.note: Selecting a conversation calls vscode.env.openExternal, so it opens outside the editor.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Projects > click a project > Edit > Instructions
steps: Open a project from More > Projects.
Under "Edit", click "Instructions".
Change the text in the "Project instructions" box and save.
Reopen the project and check the saved text shows; check it is used in a chat in that project.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a project
items.note: Settings > Instructions & editor holds workspace custom instructions, not per-project ones. The effect on chats was not verified in code.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Work
steps: Click "More" in the AGI Code header, then "Work".
Read the groups "Needs you", "Working", "Ready for review", "Done" and "Stopped".
To hide finished work, type a word in the list's box to narrow it; no separate filter toggle was found.
Compare each task's status text with what is shown on the cloud web app.
items.needs: a signed-in account with cloud tasks
items.note: No dedicated filter for finished tasks was found; finished work sits in the Done and Stopped groups.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Work > click a cloud task row
steps: Click "More", then "Work".
Click a task under any group.
Read the sections "Progress", "Outcome", "Result", "Error", "Outputs" (only those that apply).
Check the "Actions" section for approve or reject when a decision is pending.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a cloud task
items.note: The detail is a quick-pick list. A step-by-step transcript appears only for coding sessions (cloudCodeSessions.ts).

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Work > "Needs you" group; approve or reject on the row, or open the task > Actions
steps: Click "More", then "Work".
Look in the "Needs you" group for tasks waiting on you.
On a row, click the check icon "Approve this run" or the x icon "Reject this run".
Open a task and use "Approve" or "Reject" in its Actions section, then check the row leaves "Needs you".
items.needs: a signed-in account with a cloud task waiting for approval
items.note: "Needs you" acts as the cross-task inbox. "Code: Show Approval History" is a record of past approvals, not the pending list.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Show Schedules; then hover a schedule row, or use its "Show recent runs" icon
steps: Run "Code: Show Schedules" from the command palette.
Hover a schedule row to read its status, cadence, timezone, next run and prompt in the tooltip.
Click the history icon "Show recent runs" on the row.
Check the run list matches Expected: runs with their status and times.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one schedule
items.note: Clicking the row itself opens the schedules page on the web (agi-workforce.openSchedule), not an in-app detail page.

items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No dedicated coding-session home found. Closest: the Sessions sheet with its Local and Cloud tabs plus the + New chat button (webviewContent.ts), and Code: Session Worktrees > New session in a worktree (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/sessionWorktrees.ts). Searched the app folder for a coding home, coding sessions and repository-start screens.

items.where: AGI Code header > Sessions > open a session row (the chat panel is the workspace)
steps: Click "Sessions" in the AGI Code header and open a session.
Read the transcript in the chat panel.
Where a change exists, click "Review changes".
Type your next instruction in the box that says "Describe a task…" and check the reply continues the session.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a coding session that changed files
items.note: No separate workspace screen found; the sidebar chat panel is the workspace. Diff controls are commands such as Code: Accept Diff.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Artifacts; command palette: Code: Show Artifacts
steps: Click "More" in the AGI Code header, then "Artifacts".
Check the list of your artifacts.
Click one artifact and check it opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Skills; also Settings > Integrations > Skills
steps: Click "More", then "Skills".
Check the installed and available lists.
Click "Install a skill" or "Create a skill" from the top of the list.
On a skill row, use the "Turn on" or "Turn off" button and check the state changes.
items.needs: none
items.note: The remove control uses a shared constant; its visible word was not checked.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Plugins; also Settings > Integrations > Plugins
steps: Click "More", then "Plugins".
Check the installed plugins and the "Browse AGI Cloud Marketplace" entry.
Click "Install a plugin" to add one.
On an installed plugin, use "Configure options" or "Update" and check the result.
items.needs: a signed-in account to browse the marketplace
items.note: The remove control is not checked for its visible word.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Account & usage; command palette: Code: Account & usage
steps: Click "More", then the "Account & usage" item (or run the command).
Read "Session usage" and the "<plan> plan usage" rows with their reset times.
Scroll to "Usage history" for recent usage.
items.needs: a paid account to see plan windows (a Free account sees only the Upgrade item)
items.note: Usage is a quick-pick list. Plan windows are session, weekly and credits as the data provides them.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Personalization; command palette: Code: Personalization
steps: Click "More", then "Personalization".
Under "About you", pick "What should AGI call you?" and change it.
Under "Responses", change "Style" or "Length".
Close and reopen Personalization and check the new values are kept.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No profile, appearance or notification sections were found in code; only About you and Responses exist here.

items.where: AGI Code header > More > Help
steps: Click "More", then "Help".
Check the items "Help center", "Service status", "Documentation", "Contact support" open web pages.
Click "Send feedback", then choose "Report a Bug" and check the feedback form opens.
items.needs: a signed-in account to send feedback
items.note: Help menu is in helpMenu.ts; the Code line's submitFeedback.ts was not the menu.

items.where: Sidebar header at the top of the AGI Code panel: "Chat" title, then the Sessions, Settings, New chat and More buttons
steps: Open the AGI Code icon in the VS Code activity bar and sign in if asked.
Look at the top bar of the panel: the "Chat" title is on the left.
Look at the buttons on the right: Sessions (clock icon), Settings (gear), New chat (+) and More (...).
Hover each button to see its tooltip, then compare with Expected: the header shows where you are and the main actions for this view.
items.needs: none
items.note: The header title is always the word "Chat"; the conversation name is not shown there, only a small session identity line when a session is active.

items.where: Sessions (clock icon in the header) > Search sessions
steps: Click the Sessions button (clock icon) in the top-right of the panel.
Click the "Search sessions" box at the top of the Sessions list.
Type part of a conversation title you can see in the list.
Compare with Expected: only matching sessions stay in the list.
items.needs: a few saved sessions in this workspace
items.note: The search box is hidden when the Sessions list is empty, so it only appears once there are sessions.

items.where: Header "+" button, title "New chat"
steps: Send a message in a chat so the conversation has content.
Click the New chat (+) button in the top-right of the panel.
Compare with Expected: the transcript clears and the composer is empty for a fresh conversation.
Optional: press cmd+shift+alt+n (Mac) and check the same result.
items.needs: none
items.note: The shortcut comes from the keybindings in package.json (command "Code: New Conversation").

items.where: Start screen of an empty chat > "Recent chats" section
steps: Make sure you have at least one saved conversation.
Open a new chat with no messages so the start screen shows.
Look for the "Recent chats" heading and its list of rows with titles and ages.
Click a row and compare with Expected: that conversation opens.
items.needs: at least one saved conversation
items.note: When there are more sessions than shown, a "View all" button under the list opens the Sessions list.

items.where: Sessions (clock icon in the header) > any session row
steps: Click the Sessions button (clock icon) in the header.
Look at a row: it shows the title and an age on the right.
Click the row and compare with Expected: the conversation opens.
Look at the list for a marker showing which conversation is the active one.
items.needs: at least two saved sessions
items.note: Rows open on click and show title, age, unread state and metadata, but the session list data has no active flag and the markup shows no active-row marker. I found no active marker, so the active-row part of Expected may not be met.

items.where: More (...) > Projects, then pick a project row
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Projects" in the menu.
A list titled "Code, Projects" opens; pick a project row.
Compare with Expected: the project opens, and the row's rocket button ("Use this project in the chat") is available as a project action.
items.needs: a project in the workspace
items.note: The project list is a VS Code quick pick, not a panel in the sidebar; it also has a command "Code: Show Projects" in the Command Palette.

items.where: More (...) > Work, then the "Cloud tasks" section
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Work" in the menu.
A list titled "Code, Work" opens with the "Cloud tasks" section and the "Schedules" section.
Look at a cloud task row: it shows its title and a description, and it opens when picked. Compare with Expected: tasks look different from chats.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one cloud task
items.note: Cloud tasks show up in a VS Code quick pick, not in the Sessions list. Signed-out users get no cloud rows.

items.where: More (...) > Work, then the "Working" group under "Cloud tasks"
steps: Start a cloud task that is still running.
Click the More (...) button, then "Work".
Look under the "Working" group for the task row; it shows a spinning icon and its state text.
Compare with Expected: a running item is marked. For a chat message, the word "Running" appears on the message while it is sent.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a running cloud task
items.note: The screen reader label is built from the task title and its state description (accessibilityInformation); I did not confirm the spoken output.

items.where: More (...) > Work, then the "Needs you" group
steps: Start a cloud task that will wait for approval or input.
Click the More (...) button, then "Work".
Look for the "Needs you" group and the task row in it.
Click the row's "Approve this run" button if it is shown and compare with Expected: the item is clearly marked as waiting for you.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a cloud task that is waiting for approval or input
items.note: The "Approve this run" button only appears for runs with a pending approval; runs waiting for input show a question icon instead.

items.where: VS Code Command Palette, type "Code:" (for example "Code: Show Cloud Tasks")
steps: Press the Command Palette shortcut (VS Code default, cmd+shift+p on Mac; this extension does not set it).
Type "Code:".
Look at the list of AGI Code commands and pick one, for example "Code: Show Cloud Tasks".
Compare with Expected: the command runs and the matching panel opens.
items.needs: none
items.note: The app has no palette of its own; it uses VS Code's Command Palette. The line numbers in the plan (package.json:627, commandSetup.ts:2309) no longer match; the "Code:" titles are in package.json.

items.where: More (...) > Help > Keyboard shortcuts
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Help" in the menu.
Click "Keyboard shortcuts" in the list titled "Code, Help".
Compare with Expected: VS Code opens its Keyboard Shortcuts tab filtered to this app. Check that shortcuts such as "Code: Open Chat" are listed.
items.needs: none
items.note: The shortcut list is VS Code's own editor, filtered by the word "Code"; it is not a page inside the panel.

items.where: More (...) menu, top account block ("Not signed in" or the account name) with "Sign in" or "Sign out" and "Account & usage"; Settings is the gear in the header
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Read the account block at the top of the menu: the name and a plan line such as "<plan> plan" (or "AGI Cloud account").
Click "Account & usage" and check the plan and usage shown.
Click the More (...) button again and look at the last account action: "Sign out" when signed in, "Sign in" when not. Compare with Expected: settings, plan and sign out are all reachable.
items.needs: none (a signed-in account to see the name and plan)
items.note: This menu does not hold Settings; Settings is the gear button in the header (title "Settings"). The menu is a dropdown, not a separate profile page.

items.where: More (...) > Help, a list titled "Code, Help"
steps: Click the More (...) button in the header.
Click "Help" in the menu.
Look at the list: Documentation, Help center, Keyboard shortcuts, Service status, What's new, Send feedback, Export diagnostics, Contact support.
Pick "Help center" or "Send feedback" and compare with Expected: the help centre, support, feedback and shortcuts are all in this one place.
items.needs: none; a browser for the web pages
items.note: Most items open a web page in the browser; "Keyboard shortcuts" and "Send feedback" run inside VS Code.

items.where: Usage meter banner in the sidebar > "Upgrade" button (shown only in some usage states)
steps: Find the usage meter banner in the panel (it shows the Usage label when collapsed).
Look for an "Upgrade" button; it appears only in some usage states, for example when a plan limit applies.
Click "Upgrade" and compare with Expected: the plan upgrade flow opens (this code opens the web pricing page).
Alternative: Command Palette, type "Code: Upgrade Your Plan" and compare the result.
items.needs: an account whose usage meter shows the Upgrade button (I did not check which plan or state)
items.note: Partial, as the plan file says: the button opens the web pricing page, and checkout sits behind the beta_redemptions waitlist gate. In other states the same button shows "Sign in again" or "Manage billing".

items.where: Status box under the panel header, shown when the developer runtime is not ready: "Try again" (also "Open setup" and "Get help")
steps: Open AGI Code in a state where the developer runtime is not ready (for example, no folder open or the CLI missing).
Look for the status box with the title "Developer runtime needs setup".
Click "Try again" and watch the button read "Checking" and then the result.
Compare with Expected: the box disappears once the runtime is ready, and "Try again" is the reconnect path.
items.needs: a state where the developer runtime is not ready (for example, no workspace folder)
items.note: The box is hidden when the runtime is ready, so there is no separate "connected" indicator. The app-level "Reconnect" action only exists for MCP servers.

items.where: VS Code Command Palette > "Code: Show Session Activity" > "Copy a link to this session"
steps: Open or start a session in the AGI Code panel and send a message.
Press the Command Palette shortcut (VS Code default, cmd+shift+p) and type "Show Session Activity".
Pick "Code: Show Session Activity", then pick "Copy a link to this session".
Paste the link in a text editor and compare with Expected: the link points back to this session in VS Code on this machine.
items.needs: an open or started session

labels.text: Copy a link to this session

items.note: Only sessions get a copy link in the code I read; I found no copy-link action for projects or cloud tasks. Without an open session the command shows a message instead.

items.where: AGI Code panel background, seen through the editor theme
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Open the Command Palette and switch the editor colour theme to a light theme, then to a dark theme.
Check that the panel page background and the raised panels change together with the editor theme.
items.needs: none
items.note: No in-app colour control was found; the colours come from the editor theme.

items.where: The Add context menu surface, opened from the + button
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the + button labelled Attach or use tools under the message box.
Compare the menu surface with the panel page behind it; it should look raised and distinct.
items.needs: none

items.where: Text colours inside the Add context menu
steps: Click the + button labelled Attach or use tools under the message box.
Compare the bold item titles, such as Attach workspace files, with the grey description under each one.
Check that both are easy to read against the menu background.

items.where: Border lines around the message box and menus
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Look at the border around the message box whose placeholder reads Describe a task…
Open the + menu and compare its border with the message box border.
items.needs: none

items.where: Highlight colour of the selected item in the Commands menu
steps: Click the / button labelled Commands under the message box.
Press the Down arrow key once.
Check that the highlighted item has a clear fill and readable text.
items.needs: none
items.note: The highlight is set by the arrow keys in the slash menu code.

items.where: Success, warning, error and info colours on status messages
steps: Trigger an error or warning message in the panel, such as sending a message with no sign-in or API key.
Compare the red or yellow status text and its background with the normal panel text.

items.note: No single fixed control was found that always shows a status message; the tester needs an action that produces one.

items.where: Font family of the panel text, which follows the editor font setting
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Compare the panel text font with the font in an open code editor tab.
Confirm the panel uses the editor's UI font.

items.note: The font comes from the editor setting; the app has no font control of its own.

items.where: Settings button at the top of the AGI Code panel > General
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the gear button titled Settings in the panel header.
Click General in the left list.
Compare the Model and reasoning card heading with the page title Settings and the other card headings.
items.needs: none
items.note: The page title Settings is in the settings page; the heading levels are only partly visible in the settings page.

items.where: Body text size in the panel, which follows the editor font size
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Change the editor font size in the editor settings.
Check that the panel body text grows or shrinks with it.
items.needs: none
items.note: The app reads the editor font size and offers no text-size control of its own; no in-app text-size preference was found.

items.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the + button labelled Attach or use tools under the message box.
Look at the small grey text under each item title, such as the text under Attach workspace files.
Check that the small text is readable and not smaller than about 12 pixels.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Include text files in your next message

items.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a request that gets a code reply
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Type a request that asks for a short code sample and send it.
Look at the code in the reply and compare its font with the normal reply text.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)

items.where: Line spacing inside replies and settings text
steps: Send a request that gets a multi-line reply in AGI Code.
Read the reply and check that the lines are evenly spaced and easy to read.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)

items.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a reply with two paragraphs
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for two short paragraphs.
Check the gap between the two paragraphs in the reply.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)

items.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a bulleted list reply
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for a bulleted list with one nested item.
Check the indent of the list and the step in from the parent item to the nested item.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)

items.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a code block reply
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for a short code block.
Check the space inside the code block between its edge and the code text.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)

items.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send a message that gets a table reply
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….
Send a request that asks for a small table with three columns.
Check the padding inside each table cell and that the cell spacing is even.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account or an API key (the reply needs one)

items.where: Message box (Describe a task…) > send two messages in a row
steps: Click AGI Code in the activity bar.
Click the message box with the placeholder Describe a task….

steps: Open any code file and select a few lines.

Look at the notification titled Code: Running Code Review… in the corner: it should show progress and a cancel option.
Optional: open the settings with Code: Open Settings, click Usage & billing, and look at the Plan usage bar.
items.needs: none; the review may ask for sign-in first (not checked in code)
items.note: The Plan usage bar only shows when the account has plan usage data; that was not verified at runtime.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Reject All Diffs (All Files), then confirm; a notification with a Restore discarded button appears.
steps: Make sure the assistant has a pending change waiting for review in a file.
Open the Command Palette and run Code: Reject All Diffs (All Files).
Confirm the dialog that asks about the reject.
Look for a transient notification with the message about the discarded changes and a Restore discarded button; it should go away on its own and not block the editor.
items.needs: a pending change from the assistant
items.note: The notification text comes from describeDiffScope, whose wording was not read. Whether it auto-dismisses is decided by VS Code, not this code. Another toast (memory off) also exists at commandSetup.ts line 254, not tested.

items.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat > the note above the message box, once a chat is long.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar and open Chat.
Keep sending messages in one chat until it uses a large share of the model's context.
Look just above the message box for the note that starts with: This chat has used N% of the model's context.
Check that the note is announced as a status message (it has role status) and that it disappears when the chat is cleared.
items.needs: a long chat that reaches the context warning level

labels.text: Older messages may be dropped; start a new chat to keep full context.

items.note: The exact warning percent comes from configuration and was not checked; the error block at webviewContent.ts line 4569 is a disclosure inside an error, not this alert.

items.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat > the usage strip with the cloud icon, meter text and an Upgrade button.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar and open Chat.
Find the full-width usage strip with a cloud icon, meter and an Upgrade button.
Check that the strip shows the plan usage text and the Upgrade button, and that its text matches the account's plan state.
Optional: collapse it with its close control and check that it becomes a small pill.
items.needs: an account at its Managed Cloud limit or on a plan without Cloud access
items.note: The strip is hidden unless the plan state triggers it, and the Upgrade button label changes to Manage billing when a paid plan needs attention. The exact trigger was not tested.

items.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat, with no messages in a new chat.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar.
Open Chat with no messages yet (start a new chat).
Look in the message area for the heading Start a conversation.
Read the line under it: Ask about your code or describe a change.
items.needs: none

labels.text: Ask about your code or describe a change.

items.note: A variant class empty-state--has-recents exists for chats with recent history; what it shows was not checked.

items.where: AGI Code (Activity Bar icon) > Chat > send a message while the connection is down; an error block appears in the transcript with a Retry button.
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar and open Chat.
Turn off the Wi-Fi or network connection.
Type a short message and send it.
Look in the transcript for an error block with a headline and a Retry button; turn the network back on, press Retry and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a way to switch off the network connection
items.note: Retry shows only when the error is marked retryable and a send exists; the headline comes from the error type, so its exact wording is not fixed in the code. The view-level Try again button (runtimeRetryBtn in webviewContent.ts) is a separate recovery action.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > click the "Describe a task…" box > type @ and a few letters of a file or symbol name
steps: Sign in, open the AGI Code sidebar and click the "Describe a task…" box.
Type @ followed by part of a file name, for example @app.
Look for a list labelled "Workspace files and symbols" under the box, and check that it narrows as you type more letters.
Clear the text and type a different query; the list should change to match.
Note: the code searches workspace files, folders and symbols. It did not show projects, models or skills in this picker.
items.needs: a workspace folder open in VS Code
items.note: The @ picker lists files, folders and symbols; projects, models and skills are not listed in this picker in the code.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > model button under the chat box (title "Model", shows "Auto" by default) > pick a model in the "Select model" list
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and find the model button under the chat box; it shows "Auto" at first.
Click it to open the "Select model" list grouped by model family.
Pick a different model.
Check that the button now shows the model you picked and that the next reply uses it.
Alternative: open the Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model", then pick a model.
items.needs: none
items.note: If no model is listed the popover shows "No models available".

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Projects" > pick a project > "Use in this chat"
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Projects".
Pick one of your projects from the list.
In the project detail list, choose "Use in this chat".
Open the same project again and check that its row now says "Used in this chat" with a check mark.
Send a message in the chat and check that the project is applied to it.
items.needs: a cloud account with at least one project
items.note: The last step (the chat actually runs in the project) was not traced in the code.

items.where: Two or more folders open in one VS Code window with no file open > an AGI Code action that needs a folder > list "Select a workspace folder for this operation"
steps: Open two folders in one VS Code window (File > Open Folder twice, or add a folder to the workspace).
Close every editor tab so no file is active.
Run an AGI Code command that works on a folder.
Look for the list titled "Select a workspace folder for this operation" and pick a folder; the folder path is shown beside each name.
Check that the command runs in the folder you picked.
items.needs: two folders open in one VS Code window

labels.text: Select a workspace folder for this operation

items.note: The code shows a folder list only. No field for typing a repository URL or path was found for this choice. The exact command that opens this list was not identified.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat asks to run a shell command (approval card "Approval needed") > choose Approve or Deny; or Command Palette > "Code: Permissions" > "Add a rule"
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and send a task that runs a shell command, such as listing files.
When the "Approval needed" card appears, read the action it names.
Compare the choices offered (once, for session, deny) and note what each one covers.
Choose one and check that the run continues or stops as chosen.
Open the Command Palette, run "Code: Permissions" and check the "Add a rule" entry, which lets you pick allow, ask first or block for a site, tool or command.
items.needs: a task that asks for approval (shell commands ask first in the mode described in the Mode list)
items.note: The card's buttons are built from the words Approve and Deny in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts, so the exact button text may read "Approve once" or "Approve for session".

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a task that uses tools > "Activity" summary under the reply > click it to open the list of tool steps
steps: Send a task that makes AGI read or change files so tools run.
Find the "Activity" summary under the reply, which shows a count such as "3 actions".
Click it to open the list of steps.
Check that the steps are in the order they ran, each with its state (running, done or error).
Check that finished steps show a time such as "· 1.2s" after their name.
items.needs: a sign-in or setup that lets AGI run tools
items.note: The time is shown only when the run reports it.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Cloud Tasks"
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks".
Look at the list titled with "Cloud tasks"; tasks are grouped under the headings "Needs you", "Working", "Ready for review", "Done" and "Stopped".
Compare the groups with the task states shown in each row.
Start or wait for a cloud task in another state and check that it moves to the matching group.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one cloud task
items.note: The code shows a grouped list with headings, not a board with a column per status.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for "Step N of", "Step " with a value, "stepper", "step-dot", "steps-indicator" and "wizard". No step indicator or stepper was found; the only related item is onboarding inline actions in the sidebar CSS.

items.needs: none
items.note: The code opens results beside the current editor (showLlmResultInNewTab in apps/extension-vscode/src/platform/applyEdit.ts), but no app control to resize that split was found; the resize is VS Code's own editor divider. Not confirmed that the pane pairing matches Expected.

items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode for docking, left, right, bottom, floating and layout code. The app registers one sidebar view (apps/extension-vscode/package.json, views agi-workforce.sidebar); moving it is done by VS Code, and no layout-saving code was found.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > a reply with a code block > "Apply" button on the block > the editor shows the proposed change with "Accept" and "Reject" links above it
steps: Open a file in the editor and ask AGI in the sidebar to change it, so a reply includes a code block.
Click the "Apply" button on that code block.
Wait for the change to appear in the open file, with removed lines shaded red and added lines marked "+" in the gutter.
Read the line above the change, which starts with "Changes:" and names the file.
Compare with Expected: the lines are readable before you click "Accept" or "Reject".
items.needs: a file open in the editor and a reply with a code block
items.note: Only the "Apply" path was traced to the diff provider; other ways of proposing a change were not checked.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Account & Usage" > "Cloud usage: N% used" row; the sidebar usage bar is labelled "AGI Managed Cloud plan usage"
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Account & Usage".
Find the "Cloud quota" section and the row that starts "Cloud usage:" with the percent used and "Plan:" beside it.
Open the AGI Code sidebar and find the usage bar labelled "AGI Managed Cloud plan usage" (with "Usage" to show details if it is collapsed).
Check the percent, the reset text in the bar (or "No reset pending") and that the bar matches the palette row.
Optional: with VoiceOver on, focus the bar and check that it reads the percent.
items.needs: a paid AGI Cloud plan (Free accounts do not get this meter in the code path checked)
items.note: The position of the usage bar in the sidebar was not confirmed; the bar is only shown when the account has usage data.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Account & Usage" > "Add credits" (shown only when the account has a credit balance)
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Account & Usage".
Look for the row "Add credits" with the description "Buy credits in Settings > Billing on Web".
Check the sidebar usage list titled "Managed Cloud usage limits" for the credit row with its balance and an "Add credits" button.
Choose "Add credits" and check that the web billing page opens.
Compare the balance shown with Expected: the balance and the add-credits action sit together.
items.needs: a paid account that has a credit balance

labels.text: Buy credits in Settings > Billing on Web

items.note: The palette row does not show the balance itself; the balance is in the sidebar usage list, which needs the usage bar to be expanded.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Permissions"
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Permissions".
Read the list: "This session" shows the mode and tools; "Rules for every session" lists saved rules; "Trusted folders" lists trusted folders.
Compare the list with what the assistant may do: check the mode label and any "Turned off" tools.
Pick "Add a rule" and look at the choices offered (allow, ask first, block) without saving, then cancel.
items.needs: none
items.note: Trusted folders appear only when the CLI offers trust settings; "Turned off" tools appear only when some are off.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a task that needs an action approved > "Approval needed" card with Approve and Deny buttons
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and send a task that asks AGI to run a shell command.
When the "Approval needed" card appears, read the action named in the card.
Click one of the approve buttons (once or for the session) and check that the card shows an approved state and the run continues.
Send another such task, click "Deny" (or type guidance in the box and press Enter) and check that the run stops or changes course.
"Abort turn" stops the whole reply; check that it ends the run.
items.needs: a task that triggers an approval (a shell command)
items.note: The approve button text is built from "Approve" in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts, so the exact wording may be "Approve once" or "Approve for session".

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" > group "Working" > pick a running task
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks".
Under the "Working" group, pick a task that is running.
Read its state and description, and open its detail with the task's title.
Wait about 15 seconds and check that the state or progress has changed when it has changed in the cloud.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a running cloud task
items.note: The list refreshes every 15 seconds in the code; the steps-done text and latest action were not traced to a visible line in the detail view.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > click the "/" button (title "Commands") > type in the "Filter actions…" box > press Enter on a choice
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and click the "/" button beside the chat box.
Check that the list opens with a "Filter actions…" box focused.
Type part of a command name, for example "model", and check that the list narrows.
Press Enter on the highlighted item and check that it runs.
items.needs: none
items.note: No keyboard shortcut that opens this list was found in package.json. Typing / in the chat box opens a menu without the filter box. Cmd or Ctrl+Shift+P opens VS Code's own palette, not this one.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: New Project"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: New Project" and press Enter.
In the box titled "Code, New Project", type a name and confirm.
Watch for the progress notice "creating project…".
Check for the message that the project is on your account, on every client, and that the new project appears in the projects list.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: The name box is titled with "New Project" built from a constant, so its exact wording was not copied. The project list location was not checked.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Fork Conversation"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Fork Conversation".
Pick a session from the list, or run it on an open chat.
In the box "Name for the forked session", keep the suggested name or change it, then confirm.
Check that the new copy opens as its own session, and compare with the Expected line.
items.needs: an existing developer session to copy
items.note: The code has no word "Duplicate"; the action is called Fork. The copy is opened directly, and no message naming where the copy is was found.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Archive Conversation"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Archive Conversation".
Pick a developer session.
In the dialog that names the session, check it says Archive developer session with the session title, then click Archive or Cancel.
Run "Code: Archived Sessions" from the palette and check the session is listed there, with a Restore button.
items.needs: an existing developer session
items.note: The archive dialog does not itself say where archived sessions are; the Archived Sessions view does. No undo message was found, but the Restore button in that view is the way back.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Archive Conversation"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Archive Conversation".
Pick a developer session.
Check the dialog names the session in quotes before anything changes.
Click Cancel and check the session is still in the list.
items.needs: an existing developer session
items.note: No command titled plain "Delete" was found for sessions. Archiving is the confirmed removal from the list; the permanent delete is covered by S10.07.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Permanently Delete Conversation"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Permanently Delete Conversation".
Pick a developer session.
Read the dialog: it names the session, says the transcript and file changes are removed, and says this cannot be undone.
Check that nothing is removed until you click "Delete Permanently"; Cancel should leave it in place.
items.needs: an existing developer session you can afford to lose in a test
items.note: A second route exists in the archived sessions view under the button "Delete permanently" (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json). The dialog is a single modal confirm, not a typed second confirmation.

items.where: Chat: the + button in the message box > "Attach workspace files"
steps: Open the AGI chat in the sidebar and click the + button beside the message box.
Click "Attach workspace files" in the menu.
In the file chooser titled "Attach Workspace Files to Chat", pick one or more files and click Attach.
Check that the picked files appear as attachments on the message before you send.
items.needs: a file to upload and a trusted workspace (the picker does nothing in an untrusted one)
items.note: The chooser opens at the workspace folder but is a standard file dialog. The + button's visible label was not confirmed. The control menu has a separate "Attach file…" item that is not this path.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Select Model"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Select Model", then Enter.
In a chat that uses a model with tools or images, pick a model that cannot do those things.
Check the dialog "Switch to <model>?" with the detail "Unlike <model>, it cannot use tools..." appears before the switch.
Click Cancel and check the model is unchanged; or click "Switch anyway" and check the new model is used.
items.needs: a conversation that uses tools or images, and a model without those capabilities in the list

labels.text: cannot use tools, so it cannot read or edit files or run commands

items.note: Only the tools and vision losses were read in the code; the context-limit case was not confirmed. The sidebar model picker was not checked for the same warning.

items.where: Chat: the context counter ("x / y") near the message box; an inline notice appears above the message box at the warning level
steps: Open a long chat in the AGI sidebar, or send many long messages until the context counter nears the model's window.
Watch the context counter turn to the warning colour.
Read the notice above the message box: "This chat has used N% of the model's context... start a new chat to keep full context."
Compare with Expected: the notice names a new chat but does not mention trimming, and the summarize command is "Code: Summarize Session to Free Context" in the palette.
items.needs: a long conversation that reaches the warning threshold

labels.text: start a new chat to keep full context.
Code: Summarize Session to Free Context

items.note: The warning has no button; trimming or summarizing is only in the palette command. The exact on-screen position was not confirmed.

items.where: Chat: the usage banner or the error message in the chat when a usage limit is hit ("Managed Cloud quota exhausted" or "You have reached a usage limit on your account.")
steps: Use an account that has reached its usage limit (or wait until a limit is hit during a chat).
Send a message and read the error or the usage banner at the top of the chat.
Check that it names the limit, says when it resets ("It resets <time>" or "Check your usage"), and offers an action such as Upgrade.
Compare with Expected: the banner shows "· <reset>" when the reset time is known.
items.needs: an account that has hit a usage limit (hard to reach in a test; a Free or near-limit account)

labels.text: You have reached a usage limit on your account.

items.note: The reset wording depends on whether the server gives a reset time; the exact banner placement was not confirmed.

items.where: Sidebar AGI chat in an untrusted workspace > "Manage trust"
steps: Open a folder that VS Code has not trusted (untrusted workspace).
Open the AGI chat in the sidebar.
Read the line "Trust this workspace before AGI can use project files or tools." and the button "Manage trust".
Click "Manage trust" and check that VS Code asks you to trust the folder before the assistant can read or write it.
items.needs: an untrusted folder (a folder not yet trusted in VS Code)

labels.text: Trust this workspace before AGI can use project files or tools.

items.note: The code gates on VS Code workspace trust for the whole folder, not a separate per-read grant. No per-folder prompt was found; the closest is the trust approval kind 'directory trust' in approvalScope.ts.

items.where: Chat: send a request that makes the agent run a shell command or edit a file; an approval card appears in the chat
steps: In a trusted workspace, ask the chat to run a shell command or edit a file (for example, "create a file named test.txt").
Read the approval card that shows the action.
Click "Approve once" or "Deny" for that call only; compare with Expected.
Optionally click "Approve for session" on a second request and check that the next call of the same tool runs without asking.
items.needs: a trusted workspace and a model that can use tools
items.note: The card buttons are built from the label constants: "Approve once", "Approve for session", "Deny", "Abort turn". "Approve for session" remembers the tool, not one call, so it does not match 'that one call' in Expected.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Remote Control"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Remote Control", then Enter.
Read the panel titled "Remote Control" with its QR code and the words "Pair with Desktop".
On the phone, open the Mobile app, choose "Pair with Desktop", and scan the code.
Check that the phone appears as paired on this computer and that the code expires; "Cancel pairing" stops the pairing.
items.needs: a phone with the Mobile app signed in to the same account, and a signed-in desktop account
items.note: The code shows a confirmation with the pairing code before the phone can take control, but no explicit line that pairing is bound to the signed-in account was found.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Send Feedback"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Send Feedback", then Enter.
Pick "Report a Bug", "Feature Request" or "General Feedback".
Type a message in the box "Describe your feedback" (placeholder "Your feedback here…") and press Enter.
Check the confirmation that the feedback was sent.
items.needs: a signed-in account (feedback is refused when signed out)
items.note: Reachable from the VS Code command palette only; a product-wide dialog on other surfaces was not checked.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > "Code: Export Diagnostics"
steps: Sign in to the AGI account in VS Code.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Export Diagnostics", then Enter.
Watch for a save dialog; the file is written only after you choose a location.
Compare with Expected: no text before the send says what is included; the only other choice in Settings is the "Share usage events" toggle.
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: No consent dialog before the server export call was found. The code says diagnostics are redacted on the server. The 'Share usage events' toggle covers usage events, not diagnostics, and its Settings location was not confirmed.

items.where: AGI Code icon in the VS Code Activity Bar > sidebar header buttons 'Sessions', 'Settings', 'New chat', 'More actions'
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the Activity Bar to open the sidebar.
Turn on VoiceOver and move across the header buttons 'Sessions', 'Settings', 'New chat' and 'More actions'.
Check that each one is announced by its name and what it does, as in Expected.
items.needs: VoiceOver turned on
items.note: The code gives aria-labels on these buttons; the spoken result itself is not verified by reading code.

items.where: Settings (gear button) > page titled 'Settings' with section headings such as 'Model and reasoning'. The empty chat also has the heading 'Start a conversation'.
steps: Click the 'Settings' button in the AGI Code sidebar header.
Turn on VoiceOver and use its heading navigation to jump between headings.
Check the top heading is 'Settings' and sections such as 'Model and reasoning' are headings below it.
items.needs: VoiceOver turned on
items.note: Which Settings nav section holds 'Model and reasoning' was not confirmed.

items.where: 'More actions' button (the ellipsis icon) in the AGI Code sidebar > menu items 'Output style', 'Next message effort', 'Focus view'
steps: Press Tab until the 'More actions' button has focus, then press Enter.
Press the Down Arrow key to move between the menu items.
Press Escape to close the menu and check the menu closes with no mouse.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu keyboard handler (wireMenuKeyboard) handles Escape and Tab; the Arrow key branch was counted, not fully read.

items.where: Tab key on any control in the AGI Code sidebar; the focus outline is a style rule (button:focus-visible)
steps: Click in the 'Chat input' box, then press Tab repeatedly.
Look at each focused button for a visible outline ring.
Check the focused control is always clearly outlined, as in Expected.
items.needs: none

items.where: Command Palette > 'Code: Show Getting Started' opens the dialog 'Work with your code' (role dialog)
steps: Open the Command Palette and type 'Show Getting Started', then press Enter.
Press Tab repeatedly and check focus stays inside the dialog (Next and links).
Press Escape and check the dialog closes, as in Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Escape-to-close handling was not read; only the Tab trap code was read.

items.where: 'More actions' button > menu, then Escape in the AGI Code sidebar
steps: Press Tab until 'More actions' has focus, then press Enter to open the menu.
Press Escape to close the menu.
Check focus is back on the 'More actions' button, as in Expected.
items.needs: none

items.where: Inner behaviour: the sidebar's status regions (role 'status', aria-live 'polite') announce finished events while focus stays put
steps: Turn on VoiceOver, click 'Chat input', type a short message and send it with Enter.
Keep focus in the chat input while the reply runs.
Listen for a short announcement when the reply finishes, and check focus did not move, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can get a reply
items.note: The code line cited for this item (webviewContent.ts:3122) is the developer runtime status region, not a reply-finished announcement; the completion announcement itself was not located.

items.where: Inner behaviour: the transcript region (role 'log', aria-live 'polite', aria-relevant 'additions') announces a streaming reply
steps: Turn on VoiceOver and send a message that gets a long streamed reply.
Listen while the reply streams and count how often it is announced.
Check it is spoken calmly in chunks or once when done, not word by word, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a live provider reply (live-web)
items.note: Code status unverified: the cited line no longer holds the quoted code. The transcript log region is aria-live polite with additions, which may announce every streamed chunk; not verified.

items.where: Chat > send a request that needs approval (for example a file edit or shell command) > card titled 'Approval needed' with status and approve or deny buttons
steps: Make sure a workspace folder is open and send a request that asks AGI to change a file or run a command.
When the card 'Approval needed' appears, turn on VoiceOver and move through it.
Check the card announces its summary and state, and that the approve and deny buttons have names, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a workspace folder open
items.note: Which buttons show depends on the request type; the exact tool step states were read from tool-status.ts.

items.where: '+' button ('Attach or use tools') in the composer > 'Attach workspace files'
steps: Click the '+' button labelled 'Attach or use tools' next to the chat input.
Click 'Attach workspace files' and pick a text file, instead of dragging.
Check the file is attached without any drag, as in Expected.
items.needs: a workspace with a text file
items.note: Drop onto the composer is the drag path (webviewContent.ts around line 7720). No resize or reorder control was found in the code.

items.where: Inner behaviour: the sidebar's looping spinner icons (for example a pending reply or a running tool step) are turned off by the Mac's reduced-motion setting
steps: Turn on the Mac's Reduce motion setting.
Open AGI Code, send a message and watch the spinning icon while the reply is pending.
Check the spinner stops or is replaced, as in Expected.
items.needs: a Mac with Reduce motion on and a reply in progress
items.note: The rule is a CSS media query for prefers-reduced-motion in webviewContent.ts; the app has no own setting for it.

items.where: 'Chat input' box in the AGI Code composer
steps: Switch the Mac to a Japanese input method (or Chinese or Korean).
Click 'Chat input' and type a word so the text is still being composed.
Press Enter to confirm the conversion and check the message is NOT sent, the text stays in the box.
items.needs: a Japanese, Chinese or Korean input method on the Mac
items.note: The guard is in the keydown handler that returns early when isComposing is true.

items.where: Settings > 'Usage & billing' (plan usage line such as '% used · resets <date>')
steps: Change VS Code's display language to another language and restart VS Code.
Open Settings from the AGI Code sidebar and click 'Usage & billing'.
Compare the reset date and numbers with your system format, as in Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with a usage meter (Free shows no meters)
items.note: The label is written as 'Usage & billing' in the file. Dates use the browser locale. Token counts in webviewContent.ts (around line 5687) are hard-coded to en-US. Chat language follows vscode.env.language (l10n/index.ts).

items.where: A chat reply that runs several tool steps shows a count such as '3 actions' (the activity summary)
steps: Change VS Code's display language to Spanish or French and restart VS Code.
Send a request that makes AGI run several tool steps.
Read the count, and compare one step ('1 acción') with several ('3 acciones'), as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a prompt that runs tools
items.note: The exact visible spot of the activity count was not confirmed; plural forms come from Intl.PluralRules.

items.where: Chat > a failed reply shows the error text in the reply area, with a 'Retry' button
steps: Change VS Code's display language to Spanish or French and restart VS Code.
Cause a failed reply (for example a provider timeout or an invalid request).
Read the error text and check it is in that language, as in Expected.
items.needs: a way to make a reply fail
items.note: The error key chatError.generic is shown for unknown failures. Forcing a failure on demand was not confirmed.

items.where: Settings > 'Send key' (composer.enterBehavior), then the 'Send' button in the composer (tooltip 'Send (Enter)')
steps: Open Settings and set 'Send key' to the modifier option.
Go back to the chat and check the send hint or tooltip.
Compare the modifier text with Expected: it should show Cmd on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere.
items.needs: none
items.note: The code writes the word 'Cmd' (not the symbol ⌘) on Mac (webviewContent.ts line 4458). The visible spot of the hint text was not fully confirmed.

items.where: Inner layout rule: long labels in the AGI Code sidebar and Settings at a narrow width
steps: Change VS Code's display language to German and restart VS Code.
Narrow the AGI Code sidebar and open Settings > 'Usage & billing'.
Check long labels wrap or truncate without overlapping or clipping controls, as in Expected.
items.needs: a narrow sidebar and another display language
items.note: The plan gives no code location. CSS overflow and ellipsis rules exist in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts, but per-control behaviour was not verified.

items.where: Open the AGI sidebar view, then click the button titled "New chat" in the sidebar header. The empty screen shows "Start a conversation".
steps: Open the AGI sidebar view.
Click the "New chat" button (icon button at the top of the sidebar).
Look for an empty conversation area with no earlier messages and the composer ready at the bottom, with the headline "Start a conversation" and the line "Ask about your code or describe a change."
items.needs: a signed-in account
items.note: I did not check the name of the activity-bar icon that opens the AGI sidebar, so the first step names only the view.

items.needs: none
items.note: I searched webviewContent.ts for a greeting, a personal name and personalization and found none; the new-chat headline is fixed text ("Start a conversation"), so there is no personal greeting to compare with the Expected rule.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat > Projects group > a project name row (button "Use in this chat").
steps: Sign in and make sure you have at least one project.
Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Look for the "Projects" heading with up to three project rows, each with the detail "Use in this chat".
Click a project row and compare: the chat should open for that project, and the project should show in the "Active project" strip above the composer.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
items.note: The list is limited to three projects and is empty when signed out (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/startSuggestions.ts).

items.needs: none
items.note: I found no recently-used-files group in startSuggestions.ts or the new-chat markup. The only file attach options are in the "+" menu ("Attach workspace files", "Open editors"), which is not a recent-file suggestion.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat > Skills group > a skill name row.
steps: Make sure at least one skill is enabled and consented.
Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Look for the "Skills" heading with up to three skill rows, each showing the skill's description.
Click a skill row and compare: the composer should fill with "Use the <skill name> skill to " ready for your request.
items.needs: at least one enabled and consented Skill
items.note: The group is hidden when no Skill is enabled and consented (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/startSuggestions.ts).

items.where: Sidebar > New chat > Connected apps group > an app name row (detail "Ask with it").
steps: Connect at least one app or connector and sign in.
Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Look for the "Connected apps" heading with rows whose detail reads "Ask with it".
Click an app row and compare: the composer should fill with "Using <app name>, " ready for your request.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one connected app
items.note: The group is shown only when connectors are allowed for the account and the app reports as connected (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/startSuggestions.ts).

items.where: Sidebar > composer "+" button (title "Attach or use tools") > "Browse the web".
steps: Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Click the "+" button at the bottom left of the composer, then click "Browse the web".
Look for the chip "Browse the web for current sources" above the composer and the check state on "Browse the web".
Type a question that needs current information, send it, and compare: the web search should be used for that message only.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a search key for Local or BYOK (see "Set up web search" in the same menu)
items.note: The menu description says "Local privacy mode refuses network"; I did not verify the final send-time behaviour.

items.where: Sidebar > composer "Mode and reasoning effort" button > choose "Auto" (or "Plan" from the "+" menu as "Plan mode").
steps: Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Click the button titled "Mode and reasoning effort" in the composer bottom row.
Choose "Auto" (or "Plan", or "Plan mode" from the "+" menu) and close the menu.
Send a task that needs several steps, such as "find and fix a failing test", and compare: it should run tool steps rather than a single plain answer.
items.needs: none
items.note: There is no separate "agentic" button on the new-chat screen; the agentic choice is made through the mode picker.

items.needs: none
items.note: I found no labelled coding-session entry on the new-chat screen or in commandSetup.ts; the nearest text is "Choose a folder to establish the developer-session scope" (webviewContent.ts), which is not a coding-session start control.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat > composer bottom row > model pill (default text "Auto").
steps: Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Look at the composer bottom row for the pill with the text "Auto" (its title is "Model").
Click the pill and compare: the list should show the model the next message will use.
items.needs: none
items.note: The pill changes to the model name only after the CLI reports the session route (webviewContent.ts comment near line 3880), so a new chat may show "Auto" until then.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat > Projects group > "Use in this chat" on a project; the chosen project shows in the "Active project" strip.
steps: Sign in and open the AGI sidebar, then click "New chat".
Under "Projects", click the row for the project you want.
Look at the strip above the composer labelled "Active project" and confirm it shows that project's name.
Send a message and compare: the new chat should be created in that project.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project
items.note: I found no separate project dropdown before sending; the only pick is the Projects rows, and the ChatStateManager.ts line cited in the plan is a web-search check, not project selection.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat > "Mode and reasoning effort" button (mode list shows "Ask", "Auto", "Plan", "Bypass permissions"). Command palette: the "Modes" picker.
steps: Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Click the button titled "Mode and reasoning effort".
Read the description under each mode: "Ask", "Auto", "Plan", "Bypass permissions".
Open the mode picker from the Command Palette and compare: the "Ask" entry should show the example "Example: AGI can read parseDate while preparing a test, then asks before writing the file."
items.needs: none
items.note: The example text is in the Command Palette mode picker (commandSetup.ts); I did not confirm that the sidebar popover shows examples.

items.where: First open of the AGI sidebar on a fresh profile: onboarding steps "Work with your code", "Follow cloud tasks", "Review changes in your editor", "Choose how actions are approved" (button "Skip intro").
steps: Use a fresh VS Code profile, or clear the stored onboarding flag, so the intro has not been seen.
Open the AGI sidebar view.
Read the step titled "Work with your code" and move through the steps; the progress reads "Setup · 1 of 4".
Compare: the steps should introduce the key features, and "Skip intro" should close the intro.
items.needs: a fresh VS Code profile (first use)
items.note: The intro shows only while the onboarding-seen flag (ONBOARDING_SEEN_KEY in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/onboarding/onboardingState.ts) is unset; I did not check that the sidebar shows it before the first chat.

items.where: Sidebar > New chat > type text in the composer without sending, then reload the window or move away and back.
steps: Open the AGI sidebar and click "New chat".
Type a sentence in the composer but do not send it.
Run a reload (for example, "Developer: Reload Window") or switch to another view and come back to the AGI sidebar.
Look at the composer and compare: the typed sentence should still be there.
items.needs: none
items.note: The draft is saved in the webview state for the new-chat thread (saveComposerDraft and restoreComposerDraft in webviewContent.ts); I did not check the exact step for the window reload command name.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar (activity bar) > composer box with placeholder "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter) button
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar to open the sidebar.
Click in the box that says "Describe a task…".
Type a short plain sentence, for example: Explain this file in one line.
Click the send button at the bottom right of the composer (tooltip "Send (Enter)") or press Enter.
Look: the message appears in the chat as your message, the box clears, and a reply starts.
items.needs: none

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…"
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…".
Type a first line, press Shift+Enter, type a second line, press Shift+Enter, type a third line.
Look: the cursor moves to a new line each time and nothing is sent.
Press Enter to send, then look at the sent message in the chat and check the line breaks are still there.
items.needs: none
items.note: Line breaks are kept by the native text box; the code does not rewrite them on send, but I did not trace the send payload to confirm the kept breaks reach the reply.

items.where: Composer box "Describe a task…" grows as text is added
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…".
Type or paste many lines (press Shift+Enter between them) without sending.
Look: the box gets taller with each line until it reaches about 140 px, then stops growing and a scroll bar appears inside it.
items.needs: none
items.note: The growth is a layout rule in autoResize (height capped at 140px); the cap is in code, not a visible setting.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer > send button at the bottom right (tooltip "Send (Enter)")
steps: With the composer empty, look at the send button: it is greyed out and cannot be clicked.
Type a message in the box "Describe a task…".
Look: the send button becomes active.
Click the send button and look for the message in the chat.
items.needs: none
items.note: The button is disabled when the box is empty, when the runtime is blocked, or while a new thread is being set up; no visible reason text is shown next to it, only the tooltip changes, so the disabled reason may not be visible.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer, while a reply is generating > Stop response button
steps: Send a prompt that gives a long answer, for example: List 30 facts about the Moon.
While the reply is still streaming, look at the bottom of the composer for the stop button (tooltip "Stop response").
Click "Stop response".
Look: the reply stops, the text already written stays in the chat, and the send controls return.
items.needs: a reply that takes a few seconds to generate
items.note: Escape also stops a reply, but only when the setting Escape stops response is turned on (it is off by default).

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > Shift+Enter (default). Setting: Settings > Session behavior > Send key
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…" and type some text.
Press Shift+Enter.
Look: a new line is added and the message is not sent.
Optional: open Settings > Send key and check the option text matches the behaviour seen.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Send key setting can change which key sends; with it set to Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Enter behaves differently.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > Cmd+Z and Shift+Cmd+Z
steps: Click in the box that says "Describe a task…" and type a word.
Type a second word, then press Cmd+Z.
Look: the last typed text is taken back.
Press Shift+Cmd+Z and look: the text comes back.
items.needs: a Mac with the keyboard (device)
items.note: The composer is a plain text box and the code adds no undo handler of its own; undo comes from the browser text box. I did not find a line of code that blocks it.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > paste (Cmd+V)
steps: Copy a text snippet and an image or a file from Finder.
Click in the box "Describe a task…" and press Cmd+V with the text.
Look: the text appears in the box.
Press Cmd+V with the image or file, and look for a chip in the strip above the box (Pending attachments).
items.needs: a file or an image on the clipboard

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > paste (Cmd+V) formatted text
steps: Copy a formatted line from a web page (bold or coloured text, links).
Click in the box "Describe a task…" and press Cmd+V.
Look: only plain text appears, with no bold, colours or links.
items.needs: a web page or document with formatted text
items.note: The paste handler only takes over file pastes; formatted text relies on the native plain-text box, not on a code path that strips markup.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer bottom row, small counter beside the Auto model button, shown after a turn finishes
steps: Send a short message and wait for the reply to finish.
Look at the bottom row of the composer, next to the model button, for a small token count.
Hover over the count and read the tooltip.
items.needs: a finished reply
items.note: The counter is filled from a context message after a turn; I did not confirm when it first appears before any turn.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > empty chat (start screen) > Skills rows. Also VS Code Chat view > @agi answer > follow-up buttons
steps: Open a new chat so the start screen is showing.
Look for the group heading "Skills" under the start screen.
Click one skill row: the composer fills with a prompt for that skill.
Optional: in the VS Code Chat view, ask a question to the AGI Code participant and look for follow-up buttons under the answer.
items.needs: a skill available to the account for the sidebar rows; the VS Code Chat view for the follow-up buttons
items.note: The follow-up buttons exist only in VS Code's native Chat view, not in the AGI Code sidebar; the sidebar offers Skills, Projects and Connected apps rows instead of follow-up questions.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer > Commands button (/) > pick a prompt command
steps: Click the "Commands" button next to the + button in the composer.
Look for a command listed from your prompt commands and click it.
Look: the composer shows the command name with a space after it, ready for your own text.
Type your text after it and press Enter.
items.needs: a saved prompt command in your account or CLI (not confirmed which exist)
items.note: The code puts the command name in the composer for prompt-type commands (source prompt); whether the user's own saved templates appear depends on the runtime list, which I did not check.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > type /
steps: Click in the box "Describe a task…" and type a single slash /.
Look: a list of commands opens above the box.
Type a letter after the slash, for example /co, and look: the list narrows to matching commands.
Use the arrow keys and Enter, or click a row, to choose one.
items.needs: none
items.note: If no command matches, the list shows "No matching command"; the list loads once commands arrive.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > empty chat (start screen) > Skills > click a skill
steps: Open a new chat so the start screen shows.
Under the heading "Skills", click one skill row.
Look: the composer is filled with a sentence naming that skill, with the cursor at the end.
