Type what you want done and send it, then check the reply uses that skill.
items.needs: a skill listed under Skills on the start screen
items.note: The composer fills with a sentence asking to use the skill; no skill chip is shown in the composer, and a check that the next message runs with it depends on the reply.

items.where: VS Code Chat view (the native chat, not the AGI Code sidebar) > type @ > AGI Code
steps: Open the VS Code Chat view.
Type @ in its input box and look for the AGI Code entry.
Select AGI Code and send a question.
Look: the reply comes from AGI Code.
items.needs: a VS Code build with the Chat view
items.note: The sidebar composer has no agent picker; the mention exists only in VS Code's native Chat, and the code skips it if the Chat API is missing.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer box "Describe a task…" > type @ then part of a file name
steps: Click in the box "Describe a task…" and type @.
Type part of a file name, for example @app.
Look: a list titled Workspace files and symbols opens above the box.
Choose a file with the arrow keys and Enter, or click it, then look for the @ file token in the box and send.
items.needs: a workspace folder open in VS Code
items.note: The code inserts an @path token; I did not trace that the file contents are added to the message.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > + (Attach or use tools) > Add context > Selection, Open editors, Problems, Git changes, Terminal output or Web page
steps: Click the + button at the bottom left of the composer.
Under "Add context", click one item, for example Open editors.
Look: a chip appears in the strip above the box with a name and an × button.
Click the × on the chip and look: it disappears.
items.needs: an open editor or a selection in VS Code for some items
items.note: Project chips show a Stop using this project button; the skill chip named in Expected is not in the composer code.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > + (Attach or use tools) > Tools > Browse the web
steps: Click the + button, then click Browse the web under Tools.
Look: a chip reading "Browse the web for current sources" appears above the composer.
Click the × on that chip (Remove web browsing) and look: the chip goes away.
items.needs: a signed-in account; Browse the web is greyed out when web search is denied

labels.text: Browse the web for current sources

items.note: Connector resources and page sources as chips were not found in this strip; only the web browsing chip is in the composer markup.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > + (Attach or use tools) > Tools > Plan mode or Browse the web
steps: Click the + button and look at the Tools heading.
Click Plan mode.
Look at the mode button at the bottom of the composer (next to the model): it changes to the plan mode label.
Click Browse the web under Tools and look for its chip above the composer.
items.needs: none
items.note: Research, code and office-file tools named in Expected were not found in this menu; only Browse the web and Plan mode appear under Tools, and Plan mode shows as the mode button rather than a chip.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > + button (tooltip "Attach or use tools") at the bottom left of the composer
steps: Click the + button.
Look at the menu titled Add context: Attach workspace files, Selection, Open editors, Problems, Git changes, Terminal output, Web page.
Look under Tools: Browse the web, Set up web search, Plan mode.
Click Attach workspace files and check that a file picker opens.
items.needs: none
items.note: The menu lists text files under Attach workspace files; no media entry appears in the menu, and images come in by paste or drop.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > composer, while a reply is generating > type in the box > send button labelled Queue
steps: Send a prompt that gives a long reply.
While it is still streaming, type a second message in the box "Describe a task…".
Look: the send button's label reads Queue.
Click it and look: your message appears in the chat with a Queued tag and sends after the reply finishes.
items.needs: a reply that takes a few seconds to generate
items.note: The label reads Steer instead when the Active-turn send setting is set to Steer.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat > the queued message shows Edit and Cancel buttons under it
steps: Queue a message while a reply is streaming (see S13.38).
Look under the queued message for two small icon buttons, Edit and Cancel.
Click Cancel: the queued message is removed and not sent.
Queue another message, clear the box "Describe a task…", click Edit and look: the text goes back into the box.
items.needs: a reply that is still streaming
items.note: Edit is refused while the box has text; the message tells you to send or clear the box first.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > gear (Code: Open Settings) > Session behavior > Active-turn send > Steer current turn
steps: Open Settings from the gear icon in the AGI Code sidebar.
Find Session behavior and set Active-turn send to Steer current turn.
Start a long reply, then type guidance in the box "Describe a task…" and send it while it runs.
Look: the send button reads Steer, and the message shows a Steered tag while the reply keeps going.
items.needs: a reply that is still running
items.note: The package.json description says conflicts fall back to the next-turn queue; I did not verify that fallback.

items.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code, and trust the workspace.
Click the + button at the bottom of the message box.
Click Attach workspace files.
In the file dialog, select one text file and click Attach.
Look at the message box: the file name should appear as a chip, ready for the next message.
items.needs: a folder open in a trusted workspace, a text file in that folder
items.note: The chooser is VS Code's file dialog opened in the workspace folder, and it accepts text files only (see S14.24), not any device file.

items.where: Drag files from Finder or the VS Code Explorer onto the message box (no visible label)
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag one or more text files from Finder onto the message box.
Watch the message box border highlight while the files are over it, then release.
Look at the message box: each dropped file should appear as a chip before sending.
items.needs: a folder open in a trusted workspace, one or more files on the Mac
items.note: The drop target is the composer card (the message box) only, not the whole chat panel.

items.where: Click in the message box and press Cmd+V with an image on the clipboard (no visible label)
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Take a screenshot to the clipboard (Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4), or copy an image.
Click in the message box and press Cmd+V.
Look at the message box: an image chip should appear and the text should not contain the image data.
items.needs: an image on the clipboard
items.note: Pasted files of any type go through the same intake path; images are sent as image input by the host.

items.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Web page, then type the link in the box titled Attach a web page
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Click the + button at the bottom of the message box.
Click Web page.
In the input box, type a full https:// link to a public page and press Enter.
Look at the message box: a chip named after the site's host should appear, or an error that the page could not be read.
items.needs: a Free or paid account is not needed beyond sign-in; an internet connection and a public web page link
items.note: The page is fetched once when attached; the input box title is built as the product name followed by Attach a web page.

items.needs: a code repository
items.note: No repository attachment was found: the + menu (Attach workspace files, Selection, Open editors, Problems, Git changes, Terminal output, Web page, Browse the web) has no repository item, and the file picker is files-only. Searched apps/extension-vscode for repositor, repo and folder near attach.

items.needs: a folder with files
items.note: No folder attachment was found: the file picker sets canSelectFolders to false (ChatStateManager.ts), and the + menu has no folder item. Searched apps/extension-vscode for folder near attach.

items.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files, then select several files in the dialog and click Attach
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Click the + button, then click Attach workspace files.
In the file dialog, hold Cmd and click three or more text files, then click Attach.
Look at the message box: every selected file should appear as its own chip.
items.needs: a folder open in a trusted workspace, three or more text files in it
items.note: Picks are capped per batch; a larger selection shows the warning Choose up to N files at a time. The extra files are skipped.

items.where: Paste (Cmd+V) or drag an image (PNG or JPG) into the message box (no visible label)
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Copy an image or take a screenshot to the clipboard.
Click in the message box and press Cmd+V.
Look at the chip: it should show a small picture of the image instead of an icon.
items.needs: an image file or an image on the clipboard
items.note: The thumbnail appears only for images added by paste or drag; a picker-added image is refused as binary, so it gets no thumbnail.

items.where: Drag a non-image file onto the message box (no visible label)
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a file with a code extension (for example .ts) onto the message box, then drag a .csv and a .pdf in turn.
Look at each chip's icon: code files show a code icon, csv a table icon, and other types a generic file icon.
items.needs: a few sample files of different types
items.note: The icon mapping is in webviewContent.ts; PDF and spreadsheets such as .xlsx use the same chip but the host refuses binary types, so the chip shows a failed note (see S14.24).

items.where: Drag or paste a text file into the message box (no visible label)
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a text file of known size onto the message box.
Look at the chip: the file name and a size such as KB or B should show.
Hover over the chip: the tooltip should show the name and size.
items.needs: a text file of known size
items.note: Size appears only on chips added by drag or paste; chips added through Attach workspace files show the name without a size.

items.where: Attach any file, then look at the Send button
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code, with the message box empty.
Note that the Send button is disabled.
Drag one text file onto the message box.
Wait until the chip stops looking faded, then look at the Send button: it should be enabled.
items.needs: a text file
items.note: No explicit ready text exists in the code; readiness shows only as the chip losing its faded uploading style and Send becoming enabled.

items.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files, choose a text file longer than 40,000 characters
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code that has a text file longer than 40,000 characters.
Click the + button, then click Attach workspace files, choose that file and click Attach.
Look at the chip: a Truncated note should appear.
Hover over the chip: the tooltip should say only the first 40,000 characters are sent.
items.needs: a text file longer than 40,000 characters
items.note: Only the character cut-off is reported; a file that fails to decode shows the warning Some files could not be opened as text. rather than a partial-read notice.

items.where: Drag a binary file (for example a .zip) onto the message box
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a .zip file onto the message box.
Look at the chip: the file name should be followed by the reason in brackets.
items.needs: a binary file such as a .zip
items.note: Through Attach workspace files the refusal instead appears as a VS Code warning Choose text files for workspace context., not as a chip.

items.where: Attach a text file, then click the × on its chip
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a text file onto the message box, or use + > Attach workspace files.
Click the × on the chip; the chip should disappear and Send should disable if the box is empty.
Type a question that asks what the file contains and send it; the reply should not use the removed file's content.
items.needs: a text file
items.note: The × button's accessible name is Remove attachment followed by the file name.

items.where: Drag a file the chat refuses (for example a .zip) onto the message box
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a .zip file onto the message box.
Look at that file's chip: its name should be followed by the reason, not a generic message.
Drag a valid text file in the same drop and check that its chip shows no error.
items.needs: a binary file such as a .zip and a text file
items.note: Per-file errors show on drag or paste chips; the file picker instead joins its skip reasons into one VS Code warning.

items.where: Chat panel > bottom of the message box, the button that shows the model name (its tooltip is "Model"; it reads "Auto" by default)
steps: Sign in and open the chat panel.
Look at the button at the right of the composer bottom bar. It shows "Auto" by default.
Pick a specific model (see S15.10) and look at the button again.
Compare the name on the button with the model the next message will use, as Expected says.
items.needs: none
items.note: The bottom status bar item (tooltip "Code, click to change model", apps/extension-vscode/src/extension.ts) also shows the model name.

items.where: Chat panel > the model button at the bottom of the message box > group headings in the list (for example "Anthropic"); also Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the provider headings in the list
steps: Click the model button at the bottom of the chat.
Read the group headings. Provider headings show a provider name such as "Anthropic" or "OpenAI".
Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model" and compare the provider headings there.
Check each model row sits under the provider that makes it, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a provider key
items.note: Headings in the chat list are built as "Your providers · <provider>" or "Managed Cloud · <provider>" and only appear for groups that have models.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (the list opens with a text box; type to filter)
steps: Open Command Palette and type "Code: Select Model", then press Enter.
Type part of a model name into the box at the top of the list.
Look at the list: it should narrow to matching rows by name.
Clear the box and check the full list comes back.
items.needs: none
items.note: The model button popover in the chat has no search box. Only the Command Palette list filters by typing.

items.where: Chat panel > model button at the bottom of the message box > row "Auto" under Recommended; also Command Palette > Code: Select Model > row "Auto"
steps: Click the model button at the bottom of the chat.
Choose the row "Auto" in the Recommended group.
Send a short message and check the model button still reads "Auto".
Compare with Expected: the product picks a model per message.
items.needs: a signed-in account whose plan includes Auto

labels.text: Picks the model for each message from the task, your plan and cost.

items.note: The Auto list also has "Instant", "Best" and "Economy" variants shown as "Auto · <name>" rows.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model, with no chat conversation open (the picker then saves a default); the saved value is the setting Default LLM model
steps: Close any open chat conversation, or use a fresh panel with no conversation.
Open Command Palette, run "Code: Select Model" and pick a model.
Read the message: it should say new chats now use that model.
Open Settings, search for agiWorkforce.model, and check the value is the chosen model.
items.needs: none
items.note: The default is saved only when no conversation exists (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts selectModel). How a tester reaches the no-conversation state in the UI was not confirmed from code.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > pick a model row (not Auto); or the model button at the bottom of the chat
steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Pick a specific model row, for example one from a provider group.
Check the model button at the bottom of the chat now shows that model's name.
Send a message and check it runs on the chosen model, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a provider key with at least one reachable model
items.note: The Select Model list only offers models the plan can use; locked rows open an upgrade or key prompt instead.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the grey description text on each model row (the detail line shows the model id and limits)
steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Read the description on each model row: it shows a plan line, best-use phrases, "Thinking" for thinking models and a speed word.
Read the detail line under a row for the model id and context limits.
Compare with Expected: each model has a short note of what it is good for.
items.needs: none
items.note: The row text is built from catalog best-for phrases, so it is a short tag list, not a written description. The chat model button popover uses the same description text.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the speed word in the description of each model row
steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Read the speed word on several rows, for example "Fastest", "Fast", "Medium speed" or "Slower".
Compare the words between models.
Check the faster and slower models show different words, as Expected says.
items.needs: none
none
items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode for cost and usage text in the model list. The picker rows show plan, speed and capability only, not cost or usage. MODEL_COST_RATES in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts feeds only the token counter in apps/extension-vscode/src/data/tokenCounter.ts. Turn cost appears only as a status bar message after a turn (apps/extension-vscode/src/data/turnUsage.ts), and the Model Dashboard (Code: Model Dashboard) shows requests and latency, not cost.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > the group heading "Upgrade your AGI plan" (locked rows sit under it); in the chat model button popover, a group with the text "Your plan uses Auto; upgrade your AGI plan to choose these models"
steps: Sign in with an account whose plan does not include every model (for example a Free account).
Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Find the heading "Upgrade your AGI plan" and read the rows under it; each shows a lock icon and a line such as "<plan> plan and up".
Compare the plan named on each locked row with Expected: the plan that unlocks the model is shown.
items.needs: a Free account or any account whose plan lacks some models

labels.text: Your plan uses Auto; upgrade your AGI plan to choose these models

items.note: The plan names come from billing plan labels in code, so the exact words depend on the plan catalog.

items.where: Chat panel > the button with tooltip "Mode and reasoning effort" at the bottom of the message box > group "Reasoning effort"; also Command Palette > Code: Set Reasoning Effort, and the "..." More actions menu > "Next message effort"
steps: Choose a reasoning-capable model (see S15.10).
Click the button with tooltip "Mode and reasoning effort".
Read the group "Reasoning effort" and its options (None, Minimal, Low, Medium, High, xHigh, Max).
Pick one level, send a message and check the choice applied, as Expected says.
items.needs: a reasoning-capable model (for example a thinking model on the plan)
items.note: For a model without effort levels the group says "This model does not take a reasoning effort."

items.where: Chat panel > model button at the bottom of the message box > group "On this device"
steps: Start Ollama or LM Studio on this computer and load a model.
Click the model button at the bottom of the chat.
Look for the group "On this device" and the local model names in it.
Pick a local model, send a message and check the model button shows it, as Expected says.
items.needs: Ollama or LM Studio installed and running with a model loaded
items.note: The local group is built only in the chat model popover (openModelPopover in ChatStateManager.ts). The Command Palette list was not confirmed to show local models.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Provider API Keys > pick a provider > enter the key; then the model button at the bottom of the chat shows models under "Your providers"
steps: Open Command Palette and run "Code: Provider API Keys".
Pick a provider from the list and enter your own API key.
Read the confirmation: it says that provider's models are now under Your providers in the model picker.
Open the model button at the bottom of the chat and look for the "Your providers" group, as Expected says.
items.needs: your own provider API key (from that provider's console)
items.note: The key is saved through the AGI CLI, and the list and its title are in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (with no conversation open) > pick a model; then reload VS Code and open a new chat to see the model button
steps: Close any open conversation and run "Code: Select Model" from Command Palette.
Pick a model and confirm the message that new chats now use it.
Run Developer: Reload Window from Command Palette, or quit and reopen VS Code.
Open a new chat and check the model button shows the same model, as Expected says.
items.needs: none
items.note: The value is saved to the global setting agiWorkforce.model. The package.json description mentions a shortcut cmd+shift+m, but no keybinding for agi-workforce.selectModel exists in package.json.

items.where: Open a chat that already has messages (Sessions button in the chat header) > model button or Command Palette > Code: Select Model > pick a different model
steps: Open an existing chat that has at least one message (Sessions in the chat header opens the list).
Pick a different model from the model button or from Code: Select Model.
Read the message: it says this chat now uses that model and new chats still start with the default.
Click New chat and check the model button still shows the default, as Expected says.
items.needs: an existing chat with messages
items.note: The conversation scope is chosen when a conversation exists (ChatStateManager.ts selectModel). Confirm the exact way a conversation gets created before a tester starts.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model > pick a model that cannot use tools, cannot read images, or has a smaller context than the current model; a modal dialog appears with the button "Switch anyway"
steps: Use a chat on a model that can use tools or read images.
Open Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model".
Pick a model that lacks tools or image input, or has a smaller context window.

Read the modal dialog: it says Switch to <model>? and explains what is lost (for example it cannot read or edit files or run commands). Choose Switch anyway to confirm or cancel to stop, as Expected says.
items.needs: a chat on a model that can use tools or images, and a target model that cannot
items.note: The check runs only from the Command Palette path (commandSetup.ts). Choosing a model from the chat model button does not show this dialog. The check also needs catalog metadata for both models.

items.where: Chat panel > send any message > look at the right-aligned bubble. There is no visible name or avatar; the author label "You said:" is screen-reader text only (webviewContent.ts 5771).
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in the VS Code sidebar.
Type "Hello" in the message box and press Enter.
Look at your message: it is a bubble on the right, with a dashed border while it is sending.
Compare with Expected: the author is shown by alignment and bubble style, but no visible name or avatar appears; the name is only announced to screen readers.
items.needs: none
items.note: Expected asks for a visible avatar or name; the code shows the author only by bubble alignment and style, with the name visually hidden.

items.where: Chat panel > type a message and press Enter > the bubble shows your text.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Type "Hello, list the files here" in the message box.
Press Enter.
Look at the right-aligned bubble: the same text should appear exactly as typed.
items.needs: none

items.where: Chat panel > + (Attach or use tools) > attach a file, then send > chips appear under your bubble.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Click the + button ("Attach or use tools") above the message box and attach a file or image.
Check that the file chip shows in the strip above the message box.
Type a message and press Enter.
Look under your bubble: the file is listed as a chip named after the file (with an icon). Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a file to upload
items.note: The exact menu item for picking a file was not confirmed from the + menu; the code has "Attach workspace files" and "Attach file…" text in different places.

items.where: Chat panel > + (Attach or use tools) > turn on Browse the web > send > the sent message shows a Context chip list.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Click the + button ("Attach or use tools") and turn on "Browse the web".
Type a message and press Enter.
Look under your bubble: a "Browse the web" chip appears, and a Context (count) toggle lists the non-file context when it was sent.
items.needs: none
items.note: Quoted text, page and @mention chips were not traced to a control in this pass; only the Browse the web chip and editor context strip were confirmed.

items.where: Chat panel > hover over your sent message > click the Resend icon (redo arrow) on the message.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel and send a message, then wait for the reply.
Move the pointer over your message bubble so the action icons appear under it.
Hover the redo-arrow icon to see the tooltip "Resend", then click it.
Look at the transcript: a new reply comes back for the same unchanged text, with a new message entry.
items.needs: none
items.note: The button is icon-only; its word "Resend" is the tooltip and accessible name.

items.where: Chat panel > hover over your sent message > click the Branch icon (fork icon) on the message.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel and send two or more messages with replies.
Move the pointer over an earlier message bubble and hover the fork icon to see the tooltip "Branch".
Click it.
Look at the result: a new session opens with the message ready to edit in the message box; the first message starts a fresh conversation.
items.needs: a conversation with at least two turns
items.note: Code shows a new session with the message placed in the composer for editing, not a sent copy of the thread; the exact thread contents were not confirmed.

items.where: Chat panel > send a message > look under your bubble for "Sending" until the service accepts it.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Type a message and press Enter.
Look immediately under your bubble for the caption "Sending".
Compare with Expected: the caption should change once the service accepts the message.
items.needs: none
items.note: The state may last under a second on a fast connection, so the tester may need a slow network or a long wait to see it.

items.where: Chat panel > send a message that fails > look under your bubble for "Not sent" and the red error block.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Cause a failed send, such as losing the network or signing out, then type a message and press Enter.
Look under the bubble for "Not sent" in the error colour.
Look below the transcript for the error block with a "Retry" button.
items.needs: a way to make a send fail
items.note: The code does not say which action causes the failure; the tester needs a method for it.

items.where: Chat panel > after a failed send, click "Retry" in the error block.
steps: Make a send fail as in S16.15.
Click the "Retry" button in the error block under the transcript.
Look: the error block disappears and the same text is sent again with a new reply.
Compare with Expected: the failure should be replaced by the new outcome; check the attachments are still listed on the message.
items.needs: a way to make a send fail, and an attachment for the attachment check
items.note: The Retry button appears only when the error is marked retryable; attachment re-sending was not confirmed from the code.

items.where: Chat panel > send a message while a reply is still running > look under the new bubble for "Queued".
steps: Open the AGI chat panel and send a long request so a reply starts streaming.
While the reply is still running, type a second message and press Enter (the button beside Stop reads "Queue" or "Steer").
Look under the new bubble for "Queued" with Edit and Cancel icons.
Wait for the first reply to finish: the "Queued" caption should clear and the message should go out.
items.needs: none
items.note: The follow-up behaviour (Queue or Steer) is a setting; the Steer path shows "Steered" instead of waiting.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar (activity bar icon "AGI Code") > type a question and press Send > look at the answer
steps: Open the AGI Code view from the activity bar and type a short question in the composer.
Press Send and wait for the answer to finish.
Look for the model name shown with the answer (hover the answer's small meta line for the token detail).
Turn on VoiceOver and move to the answer: it should announce the answer as from AGI with the model name, not as your message.
Compare with Expected: the answer must look and sound different from your own message, and name the model.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The author label is a visually hidden line that prefixes the answer as 'AGI (<model>) replied:' in the code; the visible difference is by layout and the model name shown in the meta line.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > type a question and press Send > watch the answer area while it is still arriving
steps: Ask for a longer answer that uses a list, bold text and a code block, for example 'Explain a sorting algorithm with a code example'.
Watch the answer while it arrives, without clicking anything.
Check that text appears a little at a time, not all at once at the end.
Check that the list, bold words and code block are formatted as they arrive.
Compare with Expected: the answer must fill in gradually with formatting shown on the way.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The 'Stop response' control is icon-only with a tooltip, so it is a useful marker to find while the answer streams.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > type a question and press Send > watch the space under your message before the text arrives
steps: Send a question that takes a few seconds to answer.
Look straight after you press Send, before any text appears, for the small AGI mark that appears as the answer's placeholder.
Turn on VoiceOver and move to that mark: it should be announced as 'AGI is responding'.
Look for the 'Activity' row with 'Starting…' if the answer uses tools.
Compare with Expected: a working indicator must show before and during the answer, and be announced.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The indicator is an image mark with an aria-label, and the 'Starting…' text only appears with the Activity row.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that makes AGI use a tool (for example 'Read the README in this workspace') > click the 'Activity' row above the answer
steps: Ask a question that needs AGI to read a file or run a tool.
When the answer shows an 'Activity' row above it, click that row.
Check that the row opens and closes, showing its steps and a chevron.
Press Tab to the row and press Return or Space to open and close it with the keyboard.
Compare with Expected: the summary of work must collapse and expand on demand. The model's reasoning text itself was not found in this screen.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer, and a workspace folder
items.note: Only a collapsible Activity (tool steps) summary was found; no separate reasoning-summary disclosure was found in the webview code.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that makes AGI use a tool > click the 'Activity' row > expand one tool step
steps: Ask for something that uses a tool, such as 'List the files in this folder'.
Wait for the 'Activity' row to appear above the answer and click it open.
Click one of the tool steps to expand it.
Check that each step shows the tool's name, a status (running, done or error) and its result.
Compare with Expected: each tool call must show its name, status and result.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer, and a workspace folder

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover the answer > click the copy icon (tooltip 'Copy')
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Move the pointer over the answer to show its action icons.
Click the copy icon, the first one, whose tooltip is 'Copy'.
Paste into a text editor (Cmd+V) to see the copied text.
Compare with Expected: the whole answer's text must be on the clipboard, and the icon should briefly show 'Copied'.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The copy takes the answer's stored source text (the text the code keeps for the answer), not a separately rendered plain-text version; the tester should judge the pasted result against Expected.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > wait for the answer to finish > hover the latest answer > click the refresh icon (tooltip 'Regenerate')
steps: Send a question and wait until the answer is complete.
Hover over the latest answer and find the refresh icon, tooltip 'Regenerate'.
Click it.
Check that a new answer replaces the previous attempt for the same question in the same place.
Compare with Expected: a new attempt for the same prompt must appear, not a copy of the old one.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The button is shown only on the latest answer (CSS class message--latest).

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > cause a failed answer (for example, turn off the internet and press Send) > click 'Retry' in the error block
steps: Turn off the internet connection, or otherwise make the next answer fail.
Send a question and wait for the error block to appear.
Read the error block and find the 'Retry' button.
Turn the internet back on, then click 'Retry'.
Compare with Expected: the failure must be replaced by the new outcome; the error block should disappear and the new answer should appear.
items.needs: a way to make the next answer fail (for example, turn off the internet)
items.note: The Retry button appears only when the failure is marked retryable; the code shows it as a button in the error block.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover an answer > click the fork icon 'Branch from here'
steps: Send two or more messages so there is an earlier answer.
Hover an earlier answer and click the fork icon, tooltip 'Branch from here'.
Check that a new session opens with the conversation up to that answer.
Go back to the original session and check it still has all its messages.
Compare with Expected: the new session keeps history up to that answer and the original is unchanged.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The new session's history and the unchanged original were not checked against code beyond the branch handler.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover the answer > click the thumbs-up icon 'Good response'
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the answer and click the thumbs-up icon, tooltip 'Good response'.
Check that the icon fills in and reads as pressed.
Click it again and check the tooltip changes to 'Remove rating' and the icon clears.
Compare with Expected: a thumbs-up must record positive feedback for that answer; the UI shows only the pressed state, so the record itself cannot be seen here.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The recorded feedback is sent to the server; the UI only shows the pressed state.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > hover the answer > click the thumbs-down icon 'Bad response'
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Hover the answer and click the thumbs-down icon, tooltip 'Bad response'.
Check that the icon fills in and reads as pressed.
Click it again and check the tooltip changes to 'Remove rating' and the icon clears.
Compare with Expected: a thumbs-down must record negative feedback for that answer; the UI shows only the pressed state, so the record itself cannot be seen here.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The recorded feedback is sent to the server; the UI only shows the pressed state.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > look at the small line under the answer (the model name), then hover it
steps: Send a question and wait for the answer to finish.
Look at the small text line under the answer; it shows the model that answered.
Hover that line to see the token details (input and output tokens).
If the answer used prompt caching, look for the 'Prompt cache' line below it.
Compare with Expected: the model that actually answered and its token usage must be visible. No cost figure was found in this area.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: No cost figure was found in the answer details; time is shown only per tool step in the Activity row.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > the answer stops partway (for example, the connection drops while it streams) > read the error block below the partial answer
steps: Send a long question that streams for a while.
Turn off the internet while the answer is still arriving.
Look at the partial text that already arrived; it should stay on screen.
Read the error block below it for the words about the stop and its reason.
Compare with Expected: the partial answer must stay and be marked incomplete, with the reason shown in the error block.
items.needs: a way to cut the connection while an answer streams (for example, turn off the internet)
items.note: The label is the English template with a {provider} placeholder that the app fills in; the code keeps partial text and marks it retryable, but no separate 'incomplete' wording was found.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that the safety system refuses > read the error block
steps: Send a request that the safety system is likely to refuse.
Wait for the error block to appear under the turn.
Read the words in the error block.
Compare with Expected: it must say a safety refusal with a next step ('Rephrase the request, or try a different model.'), not a generic error.
items.needs: a request the safety system refuses

labels.text: The safety system stopped this response. Rephrase the request, or try a different model.

items.note: The refusal has its own sentence, but it uses the same error block as other failures; no separate visual refusal state was found.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message > click the 'Stop response' button while the answer streams > read the note on the answer
steps: Send a long question.
While the answer is still arriving, click the 'Stop response' button.
Check that the answer stops and keeps the text that already arrived.
Look for the 'Stopped' marker or the note about the stopped turn, and whether a Retry option is offered.
Compare with Expected: the answer must be marked stopped, keep what arrived, and offer to try again. The exact words shown after a user stop were not confirmed in the code.
items.needs: an account or local runtime that can answer
items.note: The stop path posts a done message with stopped set, but the webview's handling of that flag did not show which words appear; 'The turn was stopped.' is the words for an interrupted failure.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a message that gets no reply from the model > read the error block
steps: Send a message that the model answers with nothing (this depends on the provider; it may be hard to trigger).
Wait for the error block under the turn.
Read the words: they should say the provider could not answer.
Check whether a 'Retry' button is offered.
Compare with Expected: an explicit error with retry must appear, not an empty bubble.
items.needs: a turn that returns no output (hard to trigger on demand)
items.note: The CLI maps an empty response to a provider-unavailable failure, and the extension shows the words '{provider} could not answer.'; no separate 'no response' wording was found in the English strings, and whether Retry is offered depends on the protocol's retryable flag, which was not checked.

items.where: No control of its own. Seen in the Sessions list: the Sessions button in the AGI Code panel header (title "Sessions")
steps: Sign in, open the AGI Code panel and send a first message in a new chat.
Click the Sessions button (title "Sessions") in the panel header.
Compare: the new session's row shows the start of your first message (cut at 80 characters), not a blank row. An empty first message gets the fallback title "Developer session".
items.needs: none
items.note: The evidence line apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1243 no longer holds the feature. The title is set in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts (title: text.trim().slice(0, 80) || 'Developer session'). Not a title generated by a model, and I did not confirm the row text in the Sessions sheet.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Archive Conversation (archive). Restore: Sessions button > Archived sessions, or Command Palette > Code: Show Sessions History > Archived sessions
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Archive Conversation".
Pick the session to archive, then click "Archive" in the modal warning.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Archived Sessions" (or click the Archived sessions button in the Sessions sheet).
Select the archived session and click the Restore button (tooltip "Restore"), then compare: the session is back in the normal Sessions list and was not lost.
items.needs: a session to archive
items.note: Archive has no button in the panel; it is only in the Command Palette. Restore is a button in the archived list.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Permanently Delete Conversation. Or Sessions button > Archived sessions > trash button (tooltip "Delete permanently")
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Permanently Delete Conversation".
Pick the session to delete.
Read the modal warning and click "Delete Permanently".
Compare: the session is gone from the Sessions list and from the Archived sessions list.
items.needs: a session to delete (archive it first to test the archived route)
items.note: Both routes ask for confirmation. Whether it disappears from every AGI surface is not checked in the code I read.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Fork Conversation (the app says Fork, not Duplicate)
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Fork Conversation".
Pick the session to copy.
Keep the suggested name "<session title> (fork)" or type a new one, then press Enter.
Compare: a new session opens with the copied history, and the original session is unchanged.
items.needs: a session with some messages
items.note: The visible word is Fork, not Duplicate. Whether the copy is fully independent was not checked in this code.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Set Agent Mode, then pick Ask, Auto, Plan or Bypass permissions
steps: Open a session and send one message in the current mode.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Set Agent Mode".
Pick a different mode, for example "Plan".
Send another message and compare: the reply follows the new mode (for example, plans first instead of editing).
items.needs: a session that can send messages
items.note: The modes are Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass permissions, not chat/agent/work/plan. The command reads and writes the Config.agentMode setting, so I could not confirm that it is scoped to one conversation.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Session Activity (quick pick titled "Code, Session: <title>"). Also Command Palette > Code: Session Status for model, mode and context
steps: Open a session that has messages.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Session Activity".
Read the list under "Details": Model, Folder, Branch, Trust mode, and "Started from ... last active ...".
Compare with Expected: the created and updated times, model, project and a link ("Copy a link to this session") are there. Message count is not shown.
items.needs: a session that has messages, opened in the panel

labels.text: Copy a link to this session

items.note: Expected lists message count and id. The receipt shows no message count, and the id appears only inside the copied link. Session Status shows the ID with a copy row.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Context Files (quick pick titled "Code, Context"). Also Command Palette > Code: Session Status > Context row (token count)
steps: Open a session and attach or use a file in it.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Context Files".
Read the list placeholder "Files in this conversation’s context…" and the files listed.

Run "Code: Session Status" and read the "Context" row: "X of Y tokens (Z%)" or "Not measured yet in this window". Compare with Expected: files and token use are shown. Instructions and memory are not confirmed.
items.needs: a session with at least one file in context
items.note: The context quick pick is built from the context panel provider. I did not confirm that it lists instructions or memory, which Expected mentions.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Token Breakdown (also opened from the token count in the status bar)
steps: Send a few messages in one or more sessions.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Token Breakdown".
Read the quick pick titled "Code -- Token Usage Breakdown": Input Tokens, Output Tokens, Estimated Credits, Billed Credits, Turns.
Compare: the counts rise with use. A message appears if nothing is measured yet.
items.needs: a signed-in account to see billed credits
items.note: The breakdown is for this editor session across all models, not for one conversation, so Expected (per conversation) is not what the code shows. Plan usage is in Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Remote Control (pairs a phone; the phone then follows this window's sessions). Also Command Palette > Code: Continue in the Cloud, and the Sessions sheet button "Continue in the cloud"
steps: Open this folder in VS Code, trust it, and sign in.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Remote Control". Read the pairing QR code and pairing code.
On the phone, open the AGI Mobile app and choose "Pair with Desktop" (wording from the app's text, not verified on the phone).
Start a session in VS Code, then check that the same session shows on the phone and can be continued there. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a phone with the AGI Mobile app signed into the same account; a trusted folder open in VS Code
items.note: Remote Control pairs a phone; the cloud route is a separate continue action. The owner's notes say Remote Control is hidden in v1 for mobile, which I did not check in this code.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar icon) > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter)
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar, or run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette.
Click the box "Describe a task…", type a short question, and press Enter or click "Send (Enter)".
Look at your message: it should show "Sending", then "Running", and the AGI typing mark (aria label "AGI is responding") should appear before any answer text.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: "Running" is CSS text on the user message, set when the turn starts; no separate accepted message was found.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter) while a reply is still running
steps: Send a question that takes a while to answer.
While the reply is still streaming, type a second message and press Enter or click "Send (Enter)".
Look at the second message: it should show "Queued".
When the first reply finishes, look for "Starting queued follow-up" above the box, with a count of waiting messages if others are queued.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: Queued messages also show "Edit this queued message" and "Cancel this queued message" controls (aria labels only).

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > "+" button ("Attach or use tools") to add a file or context > Send (Enter)
steps: Click the "+" button (title "Attach or use tools") and add a file or the editor context.
Type a question and press Enter or click "Send (Enter)".
Look between sending and the first answer: the AGI typing mark (aria label "AGI is responding") shows, and "Context (N)" appears under your message.
items.needs: a file to attach (optional)
items.note: No preparing-context wording was found; only the generic typing mark and the attached-context label are shown, so the Expected text naming context or memory reading is not visible.

items.where: AGI Code > "+" button ("Attach or use tools") > Browse the web > chat box "Describe a task…"
steps: Click the "+" button and choose "Browse the web"; the chip "Browse the web for current sources" appears.
Ask a question that needs current facts, for example a news question, and press Enter.
Look for a tool row with a search icon while the search runs, and the search summary text the runtime sends in that row.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model; the model must choose to search
items.note: The search query text is not written by the webview; it appears only if the runtime puts it in the row summary.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > ask for a command to run, such as "run the tests"
steps: Set the mode with the control labelled "Mode and reasoning effort" to "Auto" or "Ask".
Type "run the tests in this project" and press Enter.
Look for a tool row with a terminal icon. It shows as pending until it ends, then changes to done or error.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model; a project folder open in VS Code
items.note: The running-code wording comes from the runtime summary; the webview shows a terminal icon and a pending row.

items.where: AGI Code > start screen "Connected apps" > "Ask with it"
steps: Connect an app or MCP server (Settings via "Code: Open Settings" or "Code: Open Agent Configuration").
Open the chat, click "Ask with it" under "Connected apps", type a request, and press Enter.
Look for a tool row with a plug icon that names the connected service and shows as pending until it ends.
items.needs: a connected app or MCP server
items.note: The plug icon is set for category mcp or connector; the service name must come from the tool row label, which was not traced.

items.where: AGI Code > controls "Mode and reasoning effort" > Ask > chat box "Describe a task…"
steps: Open the mode control (aria label "Mode and reasoning effort") and choose "Ask".
Type a request that edits a file or runs a command, such as "add a comment to README", and press Enter.
Look for an approval card in the chat with buttons "Approve once", "Approve … for session", "Deny" and "Abort turn" (and "Review change" when offered). The reply should pause there.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model; a project folder open in VS Code
items.note: Button text is built from the approve verb plus "once" or "for session", so the full words are not literal in one file.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter)
steps: Send any question and press Enter.
Watch the AGI typing mark (aria label "AGI is responding") after sending.
Look for the first answer text to appear in the reply bubble.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: The token handler re-shows the typing mark after each text update, so the mark stays under the streaming text rather than giving way to it; compare this with Expected.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter)
steps: Send a question that gets a long answer, for example "explain how a hash map works", and press Enter.
Watch the reply bubble while it is still streaming.
Look for the text to grow piece by piece, with the "Stop response" button available in the box.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: The token handler appends and re-renders the text on each token.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter)
steps: Send "give me a list, a table and a short code example of a for loop" and press Enter.
Watch the reply while it streams.
Look for the list, table and code block to show as formatted parts (not raw markdown symbols) while the reply is still streaming, and the code block to get its copy actions.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: Rendering is incremental through renderAssistantInto; the exact markdown behaviour mid-stream was not traced further.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter), then wait for the reply to end
steps: Send a question and press Enter.
Wait until the reply stops growing and the typing mark is gone.
For a reply that used tools, open the activity group above the reply and look for "Completed" in its summary line.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: A plain text reply with no tool calls shows no completed label; only the typing mark stops and the stop button is replaced.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > a request where one tool step fails (for example a command that exits with an error)
steps: Send a request that runs a command likely to fail, such as "run a command that does not exist", and press Enter.
Wait for the reply to end.
Look at the activity group summary above the reply: it should read "Completed with errors" when a tool step failed and the rest finished.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model; a project folder open in VS Code
items.note: No separate "Partially completed" wording exists in the code; "Completed with errors" is the only partial-style label, so it is not distinct from a failed run that shows "error" status.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box while a reply runs > "Stop response" button
steps: Send a long question and wait until the reply is streaming.
Click the "Stop response" button in the box (title "Stop response").
Look just above the box: the status line should read "Stopping…" and the button should be busy until the stop takes effect.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model

items.where: AGI Code > chat box while a reply runs > "Stop response" button
steps: Send a long question, wait for some text to appear, then click "Stop response".
Wait for the stop to take effect.
Look at the reply: the text that already arrived should stay, and the turn should end with the stop copy or the status clearing.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: "The turn was stopped." is the interrupted failure headline in errorPresentation.ts; a separate cancelled state appears only on queued messages ("Cancelled"). Whether an error card appears on a user stop was not confirmed.

items.where: AGI Code > Search sessions (sessions list) > open the session that was running
steps: Start a long reply in a chat, then close the AGI Code view or editor chat tab while it runs.
Reopen AGI Code, find the session in the list (placeholder "Search sessions"), and open it.
Look for the running reply to continue with its activity rows still updating, rather than starting over.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model
items.note: The code reattaches a running turn on resume (ChatStateManager.ts), but closing the view calls cancelInFlight (sidebarProvider.ts) which interrupts the active turn, so a conflict is likely; no "Resuming" wording exists.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter) on a model whose provider is rate-limiting this account
steps: Send a request on a model whose provider is rate-limiting this account (a tester cannot force this on demand).
Look for the error card with the rate-limit text and the buttons "Retry" and "Switch model".
Check that a wait time appears when the provider gave one.
items.needs: a provider that is rate-limiting this account; not forced by the tester

labels.text: {provider} is taking too many requests right now. Try again in a moment, or switch model.

items.note: Only reachable when the provider rate-limits; the copy and buttons are in code (errorPresentation.ts, provider_rate_limited).

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter) on an account that has used its usage limit
steps: Send a request from an account that has reached its usage limit.
Look for the error card with "You have reached a usage limit on your account…".
Check that the card offers "Upgrade your plan" or "See your usage".
items.needs: an account that has reached its usage limit
items.note: The headline changes to a reset time or wait when the server supplies one.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Sign Out of AGI Cloud" > AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter)
steps: Run "Code: Sign Out of AGI Cloud" from the Command Palette.
Open AGI Code and send a message.
Look for the error card "Sign in to AGI to run this model on your plan." with the button "Sign in to AGI".
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account to sign out of

labels.text: Code: Sign Out of AGI Cloud

items.note: Expired sign-in is not forced on demand; signing out is the nearest reproducible path, and an invalid provider key shows "{provider}'s key was rejected" with "Sign in to {provider}" instead.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Restart Local Runtime" (or stop the local runtime) > AGI Code > runtime status panel
steps: Stop the local runtime, or make it unavailable on this computer.
Open AGI Code and try to send a message.
Look for the runtime status panel titled "Developer runtime needs setup" with the message "AGI's local runtime isn't running." and the "Try again" button.
items.needs: a computer where the local runtime can be stopped
items.note: The message is set in errorPresentation.ts when the runtime is not running; the exact panel placement was not traced.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter) on a model whose provider is down
steps: Send a request on a model whose provider is unavailable (a tester cannot force this on demand).
Look for the error card "… could not answer." with "Retry" and "Switch model" buttons.
Click "Switch model" and check that the request can continue on another model.
items.needs: a provider that is down; not forced by the tester
items.note: The card and its buttons are in code (provider_unavailable in errorPresentation.ts); the outage itself cannot be produced on demand.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter) with a very long message or conversation
steps: Paste a very long text (or keep one chat going until it is very long) and press Enter.
Look for the error card "This conversation is longer than the model can read at once."
Check that the card tells you what to change before resending.
items.needs: a very long text to paste

labels.text: This conversation is longer than the model can read at once.

items.note: The card has no explicit fix suggestion or action for this code; a retry button appears only if the failure is marked retryable.

items.where: AGI Code > chat box "Describe a task…" > Send (Enter); the provider stream breaks part way through
steps: Send a long question and wait for some answer text to appear (a provider fault is needed to break it).
Look for the error card "… stopped replying part way through." with the text received so far still above it.
Check that the card offers "Switch model".
items.needs: a provider stream that breaks mid-answer; not forced by the tester
items.note: The mid-stream failure cannot be forced; the stream_interrupted mapping is in errorPresentation.ts.

items.where: Quit and reopen VS Code > AGI Code (activity bar) > Search sessions > open the chat
steps: Have one finished chat and one chat where you pressed "Stop response" midway.
Quit VS Code completely and open it again.
Open AGI Code, find the chat in the list (placeholder "Search sessions"), and open it.
Look for the messages and the notice "The previous turn stopped early. You can continue here." on the stopped chat.
items.needs: a signed-in account that can run a model; one stopped chat

labels.text: The previous turn stopped early. You can continue here.

items.note: Only the stopped-turn notice was found for restored final state; failed-turn restore was not traced.

items.where: Close the AGI Code view or editor chat tab while a reply runs, then reopen the chat from the sessions list
steps: Start a long reply and close the AGI Code view or the editor chat tab while it is still streaming.
Wait a minute, then reopen AGI Code and open the same session from "Search sessions".
Look at whether the reply finished and is there, or is still running, or shows "The turn was stopped.".
items.needs: a device that stays on while you wait
items.note: Code audit suggests the opposite of Expected: closing the view calls cancelInFlight (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/sidebarProvider.ts, view dispose) and the editor panel does the same (apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/chatEditorPanel.ts), which interrupts the active turn. Not verified by running.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar and sign in if asked.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Write two short paragraphs about rain, separated by a blank line", press Enter.
Wait for the reply to finish and look at the reply: the two paragraphs should be separate, with space between them.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Rendering is done by the reply; the model's wording decides the exact text.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Answer with a # title, a ## section and a ### subsection", press Enter.
Wait for the reply to finish and look: the title and sections should show as larger headings, with no # symbols visible.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Write one sentence with **bold**, *italic* and ~~strikethrough~~ words", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: bold, italic and struck-through words should show their styles, with no asterisks or tildes.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: The styles come from markdown-it in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts; the model may not echo the markup exactly.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Give a numbered list of 3 steps, starting at number 3", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the list should show numbers starting at 3 with indented items.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: The list indent style is in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts; the start value depends on the model writing it.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "List three fruits as a bulleted list", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the items should show bullet markers and indent.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Give a bulleted list of two fruits, each with two indented sub-items", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the sub-items should sit under their parent with a deeper indent.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Make a checklist: one unchecked item, one checked item, written as - [ ] and - [x]", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the items should show checkboxes, one ticked and one empty.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Task-list support is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/markdownItTaskLists.ts, used by apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Quote a short line from a famous book, starting with >", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the quote should show as an indented block set apart from the text.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Write a paragraph, then a line with three dashes (---), then another paragraph", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: a thin divider line should appear between the paragraphs, and no dashes should show as text.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Name the function `print` in one sentence", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the word in backticks should show in a monospace font different from the text around it.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Show a short Python function in a code block with indentation", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the code should sit in a monospace block with its spaces and indentation kept, and a Copy button should show at the top of the block.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Give one link to the Markdown guide written as [Guide](https://example.com)", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the text Guide should show as a link you can see and click.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Links get target _blank and rel noopener noreferrer in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts; the code does not show where a click ends up (outside VS Code or not), so that part is unverified.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Give the address of the Python website as a bare URL, no brackets", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the bare web address should show as a clickable link.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Autolinking is on (linkify) in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Make a table with columns Name, Price and Stock, and 3 rows", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the table should show a bold header row and aligned cells in a grid.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Make a table with six columns and 3 rows", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then scroll sideways over the table with a trackpad or Shift plus the mouse wheel.
Look: the wide table should scroll sideways inside the answer, with every column still readable.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: The scroll wrapper is in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Write a sentence that includes the inline formula $x^2 + 1$", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the formula should show as typeset math inside the sentence, not as raw $ signs.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Math is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/markdownItMath.ts and apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts; the \( \) delimiter was not checked in the code.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Show the integral of x squared as a display formula on its own line, using $$ delimiters", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the formula should show centred on its own line as typeset math.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Display math is in packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/markdownItMath.ts.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Write the text 2 \* 3 and the price \$5 and the name my\_file", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the *, $ and _ should appear as plain characters, with no backslash in front of them.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Escapes are handled by markdown-it in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts; the model may not write the escapes as typed.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Write a long answer with headings, a list and a code block", press Enter.
Watch while the reply is still arriving: headings and lists should already be formatted, not show # or - symbols as raw text.
Look again after the reply finishes: the final text should look the same, with no change in formatting.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Incremental rendering is in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts (renderAssistantInto).

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Show a Python code block", press Enter.
While the reply is still streaming and the code block is not finished, look: the code should already show in a code block, not as normal text.
Wait for the reply to finish and look: the block should stay a code block.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Hard to time: it depends on catching the reply mid-stream. Code fence rendering is in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Reply with this exact text: bold and ", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the tags should show as plain text, the word bold should not be bold, and no alert box should appear.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Raw HTML is switched off (html: false) and DOMPurify runs in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts. The model may not repeat the text exactly.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Give two links: [Safe](https://example.com) and [Bad](javascript:alert(1))", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the Safe link should be clickable and the Bad link should not be a working link.
Click the Safe link and see where it opens: it should open outside the app, not run anything inside it.
