items.note: Only http and mailto links pass the sanitizer (apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts). Where the click opens is decided by VS Code, not shown in this code, so that part is unverified.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > an answer with paragraphs, a list and a code block
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar and get a reply with a paragraph, a list and a code block.
Press the mouse at the start of the first paragraph and drag down past the list and into the code block.
Press Cmd+C, then paste into a text editor.
Look: the pasted text should include all the selected parts, in order, with no gaps.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: Selection is only turned off for the tool-call bar (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts), not for answer text. The render.ts reference cited in the plan no longer contains the quoted code.

items.where: AGI Code (activity bar) > "Describe a task…" box
steps: Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar.
Click the "Describe a task…" box, type "Show a code block with the language name xyzlang containing the text hello", press Enter.
Wait for the reply, then look: the block should show its text readably, even though the language is not known.
items.needs: a signed-in account or a key set with Code: Set API Key
items.note: A failed diagram could not be found in the code; the unknown-language fallback is in apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts and packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/ (assistant-fence). The ID's failed-diagram case is unverified.

items.where: Chat > a reply that contains a code block > hover the code block > Copy
steps: Open AGI Chat from the activity bar and ask a question that gets a reply with code, such as "write a Python function that adds two numbers".
Move the mouse over the code block until the buttons Copy, Explain and Apply appear at its top right.
Click Copy.
Paste into a text editor or the composer and compare with the code block: the paste should match the code exactly, with no line numbers or button text.
items.needs: a reply that contains a code block
items.note: The Copy button shows Copied! for a moment after a successful copy.

items.where: Chat > a reply with a code block > Apply > Accept in the editor
steps: Open a file in the editor and click at the place where the change goes.
In AGI Chat, hover a code block in a reply that suggests a change and click Apply.
In the editor, look at the highlighted changed lines of the file.
Compare with Expected: added and removed lines should be visibly marked. Click Accept above the change to keep it.
items.needs: a file open in the editor, and a reply with a suggested code change
items.note: The colour of the changed lines is set in the editor decoration code, which I did not read in full.

items.where: Chat > a reply with a code block marked diff or patch
steps: Ask in AGI Chat for a change to a file and ask for the answer as a diff, for example "show the change as a diff".
Look at the code block the reply shows.
Compare with Expected: lines starting with + should be coloured as added, lines starting with - as removed, and @@ hunk lines and --- +++ file lines set apart.
items.needs: a reply that returns a diff or patch code block
items.note: Diff colouring applies only to code blocks whose language is diff or patch; the diff colour styles are in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts.

items.needs: none
items.note: I found no Run control on code blocks. Code blocks offer only Copy, Explain and Apply. Commands run only when the agent calls a shell tool, shown as activity rows (see S21.15). I searched for run-btn, Run, runCode, executeCode and sandbox in apps/extension-vscode/src.

items.where: Chat > activity row for a command the agent ran > click the row
steps: In AGI Chat, ask the agent to run a simple shell command, for example "run the command ls in this folder".
When the activity row for the command appears, wait until it finishes.
Click the row's bar to open it.
Look at the Command section (the command with a $ in front) and the Output section below it: the printed text should match what the command printed.
items.needs: a workspace the agent can run commands in, and approval to run the command
items.note: The output panel is an expandable section in the activity row, not a separate panel. Only agent-run commands show it.

items.where: Chat > activity row for a command the agent ran > after it finishes, the time shows on the row's summary line
steps: Ask the agent to run a command that takes a few seconds, such as "wait 3 seconds then print done".
Watch the activity row until it finishes.
Look at the end of the row's summary line: it should add a time such as "· 3.0 s" or "· 120 ms".
items.needs: a workspace the agent can run commands in, and approval to run the command
items.note: The time is added to the summary text when the row ends.

items.where: Chat > activity row for a command the agent ran > click the row > Exit status line
steps: Ask the agent to run a command that fails, such as "run the command exit 3".
When the row finishes, click the row's bar to open it.
Look at the line under the Output section.
Compare with Expected: it should read "Exit status 3" in the error colour. A successful command shows "Exit status 0".
items.needs: a workspace the agent can run commands in, and approval to run the command
items.note: If the output has no exit code, the line reads Command finished or Command failed instead.

items.needs: none
items.note: I found no list of files produced by a command run. Write tool rows only show an Open diff button for the file they changed, and apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/turnChanges.ts handles changed files for a turn, but I did not find a chat control that lists them as generated output. I searched for Generated, downloads and new files in the webview and sidebar folders.

items.needs: none
items.note: The only Retry is on an error block for a failed reply. It re-sends the last message and is not attached to a single command row, so no in-place re-run of one execution was found.

items.where: Composer > Stop response (the square button beside Send while a reply is running)
steps: Ask the agent to run a long command, such as "run sleep 60", and approve it if asked.
While the activity row shows the command running, click the Stop response button beside the Send button in the composer.
Look at the row: it should stop running and the reply should end.

For a command run in the background, click More (the ... button at the top right of the chat), choose Background commands, pick the command, then choose Stop command and confirm. Compare with Expected: the command is no longer running.
items.needs: a workspace the agent can run commands in, and approval to run the command
items.note: The Stop response button has no visible text; its tooltip and label are Stop response.

items.where: Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > Code: Restart Local Runtime
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P in VS Code and type Restart Local Runtime.
Choose Code: Restart Local Runtime.
If a dialog asks to restart, choose Restart Local Runtime.
Look at AGI Chat: the runtime should restart and new turns should start on a clean runtime. Running local turns are stopped by the restart.
items.needs: none
items.note: This restarts the local runtime; it does not clear the chat. The restart also stops running local turns and applies the current permission choices, which may be more than the Expected wording asks for.

items.where: Chat > a reply with a code block > hover the code block > Explain
steps: In AGI Chat, get a reply that contains a code block.
Move the mouse over the code block and click Explain.
Look at the chat: a new message starting "Explain this code:" should be sent, with the code block inside it.
Compare with Expected: the agent's reply should explain that code.
items.needs: a reply that contains a code block, and a signed-in account that can send chat messages
items.note: The message is sent as a normal chat turn, so it follows the usual model and plan limits.

items.needs: none
items.note: I found no Open in coding workspace control on code blocks. The code blocks offer only Copy, Explain and Apply, and Apply opens a diff in the editor. I searched for coding workspace and Open in in the webview and chat folders.

items.where: Chat > a reply with a code block > Apply > Accept in the editor
steps: Open the file to change in the editor. Select the code to replace, or leave the cursor at the place to insert.
In AGI Chat, hover the code block in the reply and click Apply.
In the editor, review the proposed change shown with the file.
Click Accept above the change to apply it to the file, or Reject to dismiss it. Compare with Expected: the file changes only after Accept.
items.needs: a file open in the editor, and a reply with a suggested code change
items.note: If no file is open, the chat shows a warning instead and nothing is proposed.

items.where: Chat > approval card shown when the agent wants to run a command
steps: Ask the agent to run a shell command, such as "run the command ls", in a chat where approval is needed.
When the approval card appears in the chat, read its title, its summary and its details.
Look for the risk word (Low risk, Medium risk or High risk) and for Can be undone or Cannot be undone.
Compare with Expected: the card should say what the command is and what it can touch, before it runs. Choose Approve or Abort turn.
items.needs: a workspace where approval is asked for, and a prompt that makes the agent run a command
items.note: The card only appears when the permission is not already allowed; the risk rating comes from the host. Whether the card shows what the command touches depends on the host sending a summary and detail.

items.where: Chat > session line (shows the label Runtime unavailable) when the AGI CLI is not connected to the workspace
steps: Open AGI Chat in a workspace where the AGI CLI is not connected, such as a new folder without the CLI set up.
Look at the session line near the composer for the label Runtime unavailable.
Try to send a message and read any error text in the chat.
Compare with Expected: the screen should say the runtime is unavailable, not stay silent. The title tooltip says to connect the AGI CLI to the workspace.
items.needs: a workspace where the AGI CLI is not connected
items.note: I did not confirm the exact screen position of the session line, only its element id sessionIdentity. The untrusted-workspace case shows different text.

items.where: AGI chat panel > "Describe a task…" box: pick "Ask" in the mode menu, then send a task that changes a file. When the agent asks, an approval card appears in the chat with "Approve once", "Approve for session", "Deny" and "Abort turn" buttons.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code and open the mode menu.
Choose "Ask" (the mode that asks before acting).
In the "Describe a task…" box, type a request such as: create a file named notes.txt with one line of text, then press send.
When the approval card appears, read the summary and detail text of what will happen, then compare with Expected: an approve/deny form is shown.
Optionally click "Deny" or "Abort turn" to check the card closes with its outcome message.
items.needs: A workspace folder open in VS Code, and a signed-in account that can run the agent.
items.note: The approve buttons are built from the word "Approve" plus "once" or "for session" in webviewContent.ts (around line 7034), so the full text "Approve once" is not a literal in any file. The exact trigger for the card depends on the agent's mode and the tool asked for; the mode-menu entry point was found only in the QuickPick code (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts), not as a confirmed sidebar control.

items.where: AGI chat panel > "Describe a task…" box: ask for a comparison, for example "compare two options as a table". A Markdown table in the answer renders as a scrollable table with a region label "Table".
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in VS Code.
In the "Describe a task…" box, type: compare three database options in a table with columns for cost, speed and setup, then press send.
When the answer arrives, look for a grid with a header row and aligned cells.
Make the table wider than the panel if you can, and check that it scrolls sideways inside its own box rather than moving the whole panel.
Compare with Expected: the comparison appears as a readable table, not as raw pipe characters.
items.needs: A signed-in account that can get an answer from the agent.
items.note: The table renderer is apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts (lines 72-74, aria-label "Table" is not visible text). I did not confirm that the sidebar answer view uses this renderer, since webviewContent.ts does not import it, so the table's visible appearance is unverified. The model decides whether it writes a table, so the tester must ask for one.

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > New project (or Command Palette > Code: New Project)
steps: Sign in to AGI Code from the sidebar if asked.
Click the More button (…) in the AGI Code sidebar header and click Projects.
Click the New project icon in the Projects title bar, or run Code: New Project from the Command Palette.
Type a project name and press Enter. Leave the instructions box empty or type some, then press Enter.
Look for the message saying the project is on your account, on every client, and for the new project in the Projects list.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Creation asks only for a name and instructions; a description cannot be set at creation, only later (see S23.02).

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > pick a project > Edit > Rename or Description
steps: Open Projects from the More menu in the AGI Code sidebar header and pick a project.
Under Edit, pick Rename, type a new name, and press Enter.
Back in the project list, pick Description, type a short description, and press Enter.
Look for the saved-to-your-account message, then check that the new name and description show in the project's title and row.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a project you can edit
items.note: The description is not asked for at creation (projectActions.ts createProjectInteractively asks only name and instructions), so it is set only through Edit after creation.

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > pick a project
steps: Open Projects from the More menu in the AGI Code sidebar header.
Pick a project from the list.
Look at the top of the quick pick: the project name is the title and the description line is shown as the placeholder.
Scroll through the sections About, Knowledge files, Recent conversations, Actions and Edit, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a project with a description, instructions, files and conversations
items.note: Counts are not section headers; they appear in each project's row description in the Projects list (files and chats counts from projectPresentation.ts), and the overview shows the name and description only as the title and placeholder.

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > pick a project > Recent conversations > pick a conversation
steps: Open Projects from the More menu and pick a project that has chats.
Look under the Recent conversations section and compare the listed chats with Expected.
Pick one conversation; it opens in the web browser on the chat page.
Look at the browser tab to see that the chat opens.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a project that already has chats
items.note: The list and opening are in the extension; no control to start a new chat filed under a project was found in the extension, and the only other project action is Use in this chat.

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > pick a project > Edit > Instructions
steps: Open Projects from the More menu and pick a project.
Under Edit, pick Instructions, type an instruction such as a style rule, and press Enter.
Pick the project again and choose Use in this chat.
Open the chat in the AGI Code sidebar and look for the Active project chip, then send a message and compare the reply with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a project you can edit
items.note: The code applies instructions to VS Code turns in the current workspace only after Use in this chat, not to every chat in the project; the input box text says every chat on every client.

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > pick a project > Edit > Default model
steps: Open Projects from the More menu and pick a project.
Under Edit, pick Default model.
Choose the option offered (Use your model, or No default model) and confirm.
Back in the project list, check the Default model description; then pick Use in this chat and check whether a Choose the model prompt appears.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The quick pick offers only your current configured model or No default model, and applying a project with a different default model only shows a prompt; it does not switch the model by itself.

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > pick a project > Use in this chat
steps: Open the folder you want to work in with File > Open Folder in VS Code.
Open Projects from the More menu, pick a project, and choose Use in this chat.
Look for the Active project chip above the chat composer in the AGI Code sidebar.
Open a different folder and check whether the Active project chip is gone, then compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a local folder open in VS Code
items.note: No folder picker or folder-to-project link was found; the association is stored per open VS Code workspace (activeProject.ts uses workspaceState), so it applies to the folder that is open.

items.where: Sidebar > More > Projects > pick a project > Delete project
steps: Open Projects from the More menu, pick a project you own, then pick Delete project under Actions.
In the modal, read the warning text for the knowledge files and conversations, then click Delete project.
Look for the message saying the project was deleted from your account.
Reopen Projects and check the project is gone; then open a chat that was in it on the web and check it still exists.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account, a project you own, and a chat that was in it
items.note: The extension does not check ownership itself; the owner check, if any, is server-side and was not verified here. The trash icon on a row (Delete this project) is a second route.

items.where: Chat panel > More actions ("More" button) > Artifacts; or Command Palette > "Code: Show Artifacts"
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud (the Artifacts view needs an AGI Cloud account).
Open the AGI Workforce chat panel in the editor sidebar and click the "More" button (aria-label "More actions").
Click "Artifacts" in the menu. A quick pick titled "Code, Artifacts" opens, with the placeholder "Open an artifact…".
Look for the artifacts list. Each row is an artifact title; with a signed-out account you see "Sign in to see your artifacts" instead, and with none you see "No artifacts yet".
Click (or press Enter on) an artifact row. It opens read-only in an editor tab, which compares with Expected: the artifact opens.
items.needs: a Free or paid AGI Cloud account; at least one artifact made by a chat (for the open step)
items.note: The quick pick is the list view; the sidebar tree view for artifacts is not registered in package.json, so there is no separate Explorer panel. Code path for listing and opening: artifactsTree.ts getChildren and the agi-workforce.openArtifact command (commandSetup.ts). "Code: Show Artifacts" is the palette entry; "Code: Open Artifact" is hidden from the palette (when: false). Note: the Artifacts menu item label comes from surfaceMenu.ts, not a translation file, and the empty/sign-in texts are in artifactsTree.ts. Plan's "Where to find it" was blank, so this path is derived from code only.

items.where: Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > Code: Show Artifacts > pick a code artifact
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud if asked. Artifacts belong to that account.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Show Artifacts" and press Enter.
Pick an artifact that holds source code (its row shows a code type) and press Enter.
Look at the opened tab: it should show as a read-only text tab with syntax colouring for the code language, the same as Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one code artifact
items.note: The code only covers AI-produced artifacts, not workspace source files; the tab language comes from the artifact's language or type, not from the file on disk.

items.where: Open a file > select some text > right-click the selection > Code: Send Selection to a New Chat
steps: Open any source file in the editor.
Select a few lines of text with the mouse.
Right-click the selection and choose "Code: Send Selection to a New Chat" (or press Cmd+Shift+Alt+E for "Code: Explain Selection").
Look at the chat composer: it should show a reference to the file and the selected range, with an empty place to type your question. Type a question and send it to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a file open in the editor; a signed-in account to send the chat (not confirmed in the code)

labels.text: Code: Send Selection to a New Chat

items.note: "Code: Send Selection to a New Chat" starts a new chat and resets the current conversation; if a reply is still being written it asks first.

items.where: Open a file > select a range of lines > right-click the selection > Code: Send Selection to a New Chat
steps: Open a long file in the editor.
Select a range of lines, for example from line 10 to line 20.
Right-click the selection and choose "Code: Send Selection to a New Chat".
Look at the chat composer: the file reference should carry the selected start and end lines. Type a question about that range and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a file open in the editor with several lines; a signed-in account to send the chat (not confirmed in the code)

labels.text: Code: Send Selection to a New Chat

items.note: The code has no page selection; it only handles text ranges in a text editor, so a page of a PDF or a page break is not covered.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Show Artifacts > click the copy icon on an artifact row (tooltip Copy the content)
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud if asked.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Show Artifacts" and press Enter.
Click the copy icon on an artifact row. Its tooltip reads "Copy the content".
Paste somewhere (Cmd+V). The whole artifact text should appear, and a notice should say it was copied; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one artifact
items.note: The copy command copies the whole artifact, not a selected part; no code path copies a selection from a preview tab, so Expected (selected content) is not matched by the code.

items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one artifact
items.note: No command opens an artifact or file in its native application. I searched apps/extension-vscode/src for revealFileInOS, openPath, openWith, "Open With", "Reveal in", "native app" and "Open in". The nearest match is "Code: Open Published Artifact" (openPublishedArtifact), which opens the share web page in the browser, not a native app.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then read the row title
steps: Sign in and make sure the account has at least one artifact.
Click More in the chat panel.
Click Artifacts. The list opens under the title Code, Artifacts.
Read the title on each row. Rows with no title should show Untitled followed by the type.
Open a row and compare the file name shown on the viewer tab with the title. The tab shows the title turned into a file name with an extension, not the title text itself.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact, and one artifact with no title for the fallback check
items.note: The fallback is Untitled plus the type (artifactPresentation.ts:79), not a fixed word; the viewer tab name is a slug of the title plus an extension, so it does not show the title verbatim.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then read the row description
steps: Sign in and make sure the account has artifacts of more than one type.
Click More in the chat panel, then click Artifacts.
Read the text after the icon on each row. The first word is the artifact type.
Open a row and look at the language shown in the status bar of the viewer.
Compare the type word and icon with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with artifacts of different types
items.note: The code only gives special icons to html, react, svg, mermaid and code; other types such as diagram, document or spreadsheet are shown as the raw type word from the server, with the generic file-code icon, and the code does not confirm those kinds exist.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then click a row. The palette command is Code: Open Artifact
steps: Sign in and make sure the account has an artifact.
Click More in the chat panel, then click Artifacts.
Click an artifact row.
Look for a read-only text tab that shows the artifact content.
items.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact
items.note: No control to open an artifact was found in the chat webview, so the list is the only path from the UI; the palette command Code: Open Artifact takes an artifact id and no picker was found for it.

items.where: Artifacts > click a row > close the viewer tab with its close button or Cmd+W
steps: Open an artifact from More > Artifacts.
Close its editor tab with the tab close button or Cmd+W.
Click More, then Artifacts again.
Look for the same row still in the list.
Click the row and check that the content opens again.
items.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact
items.note: The extension has no close command; closing is VS Code's own tab close. The row actions are copy, save into the workspace and open on web, and none deletes an artifact.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then click the same row again
steps: Open an artifact, then close its tab.
Click More, then Artifacts, and click the same row.
Run Developer: Reload Window from the Command Palette, then repeat the Artifacts step.
Compare the reopened content with the first view.
items.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact; the reload step needs VS Code's Developer: Reload Window command
items.note: No toggle was found; the list is loaded from the server index, so reopening after a reload works only while signed in.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then click a different row
steps: Use a conversation with at least two artifacts.
Click More, then Artifacts, and click the first artifact.
Click More, then Artifacts again, and click the second artifact.
Compare the second content with the first and check that both can be opened.
items.needs: a signed-in account with a conversation that has several artifacts
items.note: Switching goes through the list picker, which closes after each pick; the viewer itself has no switch control, so the expectation of switching without leaving the viewer is not met by the code.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then hover a row
steps: Sign in and open More, then Artifacts.
Hover a row and read its tooltip.
Click the row to open the artifact.
Try to type into the viewer tab.
Compare the tooltip and the viewer with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact

labels.text: Opens read-only, re-derived from the message that produced it

items.note: The read-only state comes from the document being served by a content provider; the code sets no explicit read-only flag, and no older-version or shared-copy read-only state was found.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then hover a row and click the Copy the content icon
steps: Open More, then Artifacts.
Hover the row of an artifact and click its copy icon, tooltip Copy the content.
Paste into any editor.
Compare the pasted text with the artifact content, and check for a confirmation message that says copied with the title.
items.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact
items.note: The confirmation text is the product name, then copied and the title in quotes; the product name comes from a constant, so it is not a literal in the file.

items.where: Chat panel > More > Artifacts, then read the row description
steps: Sign in with an account that has a published artifact and one that is not published.
Click More, then Artifacts.
Read the end of each row description for the visibility words.
Hover a published row and read the tooltip explanation.
Compare the labels with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one published artifact and one unpublished artifact
items.note: Only published artifacts get a label; an unpublished artifact shows no label, and the word private does not appear anywhere in the code. No publish control was found in VS Code.

items.needs: a reply that is still producing an artifact
items.note: The viewer loads the content once when opened and does not change as a reply streams; the list refreshes every 60 seconds while the picker is open (ARTIFACTS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/artifacts/artifactsTree.ts), and treeQuickPick.ts:178 only turns that timer on. Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for artifact in the chat webview and chatSetup.ts: no live content path found.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Artifacts > pick a row in the "Code, Artifacts" list (placeholder "Open an artifact…")
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud with an account that has artifacts.
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Artifacts".
Look at each row: the row name should be the artifact's title.
Find an artifact with no title and check the row shows "Untitled" followed by its type.
Click a row to open it and check the editor tab name matches the title.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with artifacts, including one with no title
items.note: The Artifacts tree class exists but no tree view is registered, so the list the person sees is the quick pick; there is no separate card or viewer title beyond the row name and tab name.

items.where: Select some text in an editor > right-click > Code: Explain Selection or Code: Refactor Code; or click the lightbulb (or press Cmd+.) and look for Refactor with Code
steps: Open any code file and select several lines.
Right-click inside the selection.
Look for "Code: Explain Selection" and "Code: Refactor Code" in the menu.
Press Cmd+. (or click the lightbulb) with the selection still active.
Look for "Refactor with" followed by the product name "Code" and "Explain with" in the list.
items.needs: none
items.note: There is no floating toolbar in the code; the selection actions are the editor right-click menu and the code-action (lightbulb) menu, which only appear when text is selected.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Artifacts > hover a row > click the save icon "Save into the workspace" (command "Code: Save Artifact into Workspace")
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud with an account that has a Markdown artifact.
Run "Code: Show Artifacts" from the Command Palette.
Hover the Markdown artifact row and click the save icon labelled "Save into the workspace".
In the save dialog, choose a folder and keep the suggested name.
Check the saved file name ends in .md and that its content matches the artifact.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a Markdown artifact
items.note: No command is named or labelled as Markdown export. The closest path is saving an artifact into the workspace; the file gets a .md extension only when the artifact's language is markdown (artifactPresentation.ts maps markdown to md).

items.needs: a connected email account
items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for send-email, sendEmail, recipient, draft-email and email-confirm patterns and packages/ui for the same words; found no review-before-send step, only a resend confirmation in ChatStateManager.ts. The ledger gives no code location.

items.where: More actions (…) > Artifacts > Open an artifact… > pick an artifact with code
steps: In the AGI Code sidebar, click the button labelled More actions (the … icon in the header).
Click Artifacts, then pick an artifact in the list (the placeholder text reads Open an artifact…).
Click inside the code and type a line; check that the text changes and can be edited.
Hover the row's save icon labelled Save into the workspace and click it to keep the result; check that a saved file opens in the editor, as in Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact that contains code, and a folder open in VS Code to keep the result
items.note: The artifact opens through a content provider (agi-artifact scheme) and the code sets no read-only flag, but the app has no code path that saves that document back to its source; the keep step is Save into the workspace. Whether typed edits persist was not verified.

items.needs: none
items.note: Not found. Artifacts list as a flat list (artifactsTree.ts sets TreeItemCollapsibleState.None), and the cited lines in package.json and extension.ts are now unrelated commands. Searched the app folder for file tree, fileTree, multi-file and TreeItemCollapsibleState.Collapsed. Only VS Code's own Explorer applies once a folder is open.

items.needs: none

steps: In the AGI Code sidebar, click the button labelled More actions (the … icon in the header).
Click Artifacts, then pick an artifact that contains code (the placeholder text reads Open an artifact…).
Look at the opened editor tab: the code should show colours for keywords and strings, as in Expected.
Click at the end of a line that opens a bracket and press Return; check that indentation and matching brackets follow the language.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact that contains code
items.note: The app sets the editor language from the artifact (artifactEditorLanguage in artifactPresentation.ts); highlighting and indentation come from VS Code, not from app code.

items.where: More actions (…) > Artifacts > Open an artifact… > hover the row's save icon and click Save into the workspace
steps: In the AGI Code sidebar, click the button labelled More actions (the … icon in the header).
Click Artifacts, then pick an artifact that contains code (the placeholder text reads Open an artifact…).
Hover the row's save icon, whose tooltip reads Save into the workspace, and click it.
In the save dialog, keep the suggested file name and click Save; check that the file opens in a normal editor tab in the open folder, ready to keep developing.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact that contains code, and a folder open in VS Code (without one the app shows: open a folder first)
items.note: Open Published Artifact opens a web share link in the browser and is not a coding workspace; the coding path is Save into the workspace.
