Nearest candidate is the artifact command 'Code: Save Artifact into Workspace' (package.json:714, handler saveArtifactToWorkspace in src/features/artifacts/artifactActions.ts:163, file extension from artifactFileExtension in artifactPresentation.ts:94), which writes the artifact text to a workspace file via a save dialog; it is not confirmed to produce a standalone HTML file, and the menu placement for it was not confirmed. The Code line's package.json:593 reference no longer matches a file entry.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Artifacts > pick an artifact row > hover it and click the save icon (tooltip: Save into the workspace)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Show Artifacts" and press Return.
If the list says the artifacts belong to your AGI Cloud account, select that item and sign in first.
Make sure a folder is open in VS Code, because the save needs a workspace folder (File > Open Folder).
Select an artifact row, hover it, and click the save icon with the tooltip "Save into the workspace".
In the save dialog, pick a place inside the open folder and click Save, then check the file appears in the Explorer with the artifact's content and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one artifact, and a folder open in VS Code
items.note: No whole-app source download exists in the code (searched 'download source', 'downloadSource', 'source archive', 'zip' in apps/extension-vscode/src and package.json); plan's package.json:593 no longer holds it. The closest feature saves one artifact file into the workspace (registered at apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2650), not the app's full source, and the command itself is hidden from the palette.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Sessions History", then type in the box titled "Sessions history"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Show Sessions History". Press Enter.
In the box that opens, read the placeholder "Search sessions by title or message text".
Type a word from the title or from a message of a past chat that you know exists.
Wait a moment for the list to update, then check that the matching chat is listed and that unrelated chats are not.
Click or press Enter on the matching row to open it, and check that the chat opens.
items.needs: a past conversation with a known word in its title or messages

labels.text: Search sessions by title or message text

items.note: The sidebar also has a "Search sessions" box that appears above the session list, but the code shows it only when the session list has rows.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Projects", then type in the box that says "Open a project…"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Show Projects". Press Enter.
Read the placeholder "Open a project…" in the box that opens.
Type a project name you created on the web.
Check that the matching project is listed.
Press Enter on the match and check that the project opens.
items.needs: an account with at least one project
items.note: The code uses the generic quick pick, which matches typed text against the name, description and detail. The code does not show that a project's description is put in those fields, so a match by description is unverified.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Artifacts", then type in the box that says "Open an artifact…"
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and type "Code: Show Artifacts". Press Enter.
Read the placeholder "Open an artifact…" in the box that opens.
Type a word from an artifact's title.
Check that the matching artifact is listed and unrelated ones are not.
Press Enter on the match and check that the artifact opens.
items.needs: an account with at least one artifact
items.note: The code uses the generic quick pick, which matches typed text against the name, description and detail. The code does not show that artifact content (not just the title) is searched, so a match on content is unverified.

items.needs: a work source connected to the account, such as Drive, Slack or Notion
items.note: The search happens on the server when a chat request is made (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts). The extension has a start-screen group named "Connected apps" with an "Ask with it" action (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts), but I found no control in the extension to connect Drive, Slack or Notion. I searched for "connector", "knowledge" and "collection" in apps/extension-vscode/src.

items.where: Sidebar chat > "+" button (title "Attach or use tools") > "Browse the web"
steps: Open the chat sidebar and click the "+" button under "Attach or use tools".
Click "Browse the web" so it is checked.
Check that the strip "Browse the web for current sources" appears above the input.
Type a question that needs current information, such as today's news on a topic, and send it.
Check that the answer uses web results and that sources are listed under the answer.
items.needs: a search key if the account is in Local or BYOK mode ("Set up web search" in the same menu)
items.note: The menu text says "Local privacy mode refuses network", so web search is refused in that mode. I did not check the server rules for when a search key is needed.

items.needs: a project with knowledge files, if testing project knowledge
items.note: I found no control in apps/extension-vscode to put chosen sources into a named collection or to limit a chat's search to one. The only related screen is the read-only "Knowledge files" list in a project (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/projects/projectActions.ts), whose description reads "Knowledge files are added and removed there", meaning on the web. I searched for "collection", "knowledge" and "source" in apps/extension-vscode/src.

items.where: Sidebar chat > an answer's "{count} sources" disclosure > click a source link
steps: Ask a question that gets a web-sourced answer, using "Browse the web" if needed.
Under the answer, find the disclosure labelled "{count} sources" and click it to open the list.
Hover a source link to check its full address.
Click the source link and check that the original page opens in the browser.
items.needs: a web-sourced answer with at least one source ("Browse the web" turned on)
items.note: The code accepts only http and https addresses for these links, and I did not find the code that opens the link itself.

items.where: Code: Show Cloud Tasks > select the research task in the Cloud tasks list > Actions > $(stop-circle) Stop this task > Stop this task (modal confirmation)
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud if asked, then run the command Code: Show Cloud Tasks from the Command Palette.
Select the research task row in the Cloud tasks list while it is still running (not finished, failed or stopped).
In the task detail list, scroll to the Actions section and select Stop this task.
In the modal dialog that asks Stop "<task title>"?, click Stop this task.
Look for the notice This task was asked to stop. Then refresh the list and check the task shows as stopped (state label stopped), with the work done so far kept in the conversation.
items.needs: A signed-in AGI Cloud account and a research run that has not yet finished.

labels.text: This task was asked to stop.

items.note: The extension stop control is generic to any cloud task; no research-specific control was found in the extension. The 'recorded as cancelled' part is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/research-loop.ts (persists 'interrupted' and emits state 'cancelled' with summary 'Research was cancelled.'), which the tester cannot see directly. The Stop action is hidden once the run is settled, and I did not confirm that a research run appears in the Cloud tasks list.

items.where: Chat panel > turn on Browse the web for current sources > send a question that needs current facts > under the answer, click the "{count} sources" line to expand it (shows as "1 source" or "2 sources")
steps: Sign in and open the AGI chat panel in the editor sidebar.
Turn on the attachment option "Browse the web for current sources" in the composer.
Type a question that needs current facts, for example a recent news question, and send it.
When the answer finishes, click the "{count} sources" line under the answer to expand the list.
Hover over each source link to see its full URL in the tooltip, then check that each source shows a title, a hostname and an opening link.
Compare with Expected: each source shows its URL or resource identifier and can be opened.
items.needs: a signed-in account with web search available on the current route

labels.text: Browse the web for current sources

items.note: The URL is shown as the link tooltip (title attribute) and the link label falls back to the raw URL when no title is sent. Only http and https links are rendered as links; other URLs appear as plain text. I did not confirm that a click opens the link in the browser, since the click handler was not traced, and the code for the source list is only in the webview script. The exact wording of the expanded list needs a live check.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects (or Command Palette > Code: Show Projects)
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and click the More button (tooltip More).
Click Projects in the menu.
Look for a list of your projects with the placeholder Open a project. If you are signed out, the list shows Sign in to see your projects instead.
Click one project in the list and check that its detail menu opens with the project name as its title.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
items.note: The code calls these projects, not notebooks; the Expected item's notebook is the same object as a project.

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects > New project (or Command Palette > Code: New Project)
steps: Click More in the AGI Code sidebar, then click Projects.
Click the New project icon at the top of the list (tooltip New project).
Type a name such as QA test notebook and press Enter. An empty name is refused with the message A project needs a name.
Leave Instructions empty and press Enter, or type some and press Enter.
Look for the message saying the project is on your account, on every client, and check that the project now appears in the list.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects > [project name] > Rename or Description
steps: Open Projects from the More menu and click a project.
Click Rename, type a new name, and press Enter.
Open the same project again, click Description, type a description, and press Enter.
Look for the message saying the project was saved to your account, and check that the new name is the menu title and the description shows under it.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project

items.where: AGI Code sidebar > More > Projects > [project name] > Instructions
steps: Open Projects from the More menu and click a project.
Click Instructions under the Edit heading, type text such as Always answer in bullet points, and press Enter.
Open the project again and check that Instructions now shows Set.
Click Use in this chat on the project, then send a message in this workspace's chat and compare the reply with the instructions.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
items.note: In the code, the instructions only reach chat turns in a workspace where the project is used in this chat; the prompt text says every chat in the project, on every client, which is set on the server.

items.where: AGI Code chat start screen > Projects group > Use in this chat (then Use in this chat in the project menu)
steps: Open a new chat in the AGI Code sidebar.
In the Projects group of the start suggestions, click the Use in this chat button on a project row. The project menu opens.
Click Use in this chat in that menu.
Look at the chip above the message box with a folder icon and the project name (labelled Active project), then send a message in the chat.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
items.note: The Projects group appears only when the start screen has project suggestions; I did not confirm when it shows. The same Use in this chat item is also in the project menu from More > Projects.

items.where: Code: Open Settings > Instructions & editor > Memory > Use saved memory facts (switch)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Open Settings", press Enter.
Click "Instructions & editor" in the left list (it shows as Instructions & editor).
In the Memory card, switch "Use saved memory facts" off.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, run "Code: Add Memory Fact", type a fact, press Enter.
Compare: a dialog says "Memory is off, so saved facts are not sent with any turn." and no fact is saved, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: If the workspace sets agiWorkforce.optOut.memory, the switch cannot turn memory on there (message "Memory stays off here"). The code for a chat turn that skips memory was not run.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory", press Enter.
Click "List & remove facts".
Compare: every saved fact appears in the list, under its topic heading.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with saved facts
items.note: When signed out, the list shows "Sign in to see your memory" instead of facts.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the search box at the top of the list
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Type a word that appears in one saved fact.
Compare: only matching facts stay in the list. Delete the text to see all facts again.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least two saved facts

labels.text: Your account memory, shared with every AGI client…

items.note: The search also matches the source and date line under each fact.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts (topic headings in the list)
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Look for topic headings with a count, such as "Preferences", "Decisions", "Facts", "Context", "Summaries" or "Skills".
Compare: each fact sits under the topic it was saved with. Topics with no facts do not appear.
items.needs: a signed-in account with facts in at least two topics
items.note: A fact with no topic is listed under "Facts".

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Add Memory Fact (also Code: Memory > Add a memory fact)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Add Memory Fact", press Enter.
Type "I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work." and press Enter.
Read the message "Saved to your account, on every client."
Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts" and find the new fact.
Compare with Expected: ask a chat question that the fact would answer.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account

labels.text: Saved to your account, on every client.

items.note: The fact is sent with chat turns only while Memory is on.

items.where: Editor: select text, right-click it, choose "Code: Remember This"
steps: Open any file and select a sentence.
Right-click the selection and click "Code: Remember This".
Compare: the "Add Memory Fact" box opens with the selected text filled in. Press Enter.
Read the message "Saved to your account, on every client."
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a file open in the editor

labels.text: Saved to your account, on every client.

items.note: No "remember" action inside the chat itself was found; the chat /memory command only opens the Memory list.

items.where: Effect seen in "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts" after ordinary AGI Code chats
steps: Have a normal chat that states a lasting preference, such as "I usually write tests in pytest."
Wait for the reply to finish.
Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Compare: a new fact from that chat is listed, as Expected says.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Memory on
items.note: The save is done by the server and the AGI CLI after a turn. The VS Code code has no control for it, and which turns qualify, and whether CLI on-device memory reaches this list, were not confirmed.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the edit button on a fact row
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact and click the pencil button "Edit this fact".
Change the text and press Enter.
Read the message "Updated in your account, on every client."
Compare: reopen the list and check the new text is shown; then ask a chat question the fact should change.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one saved fact

labels.text: Updated in your account, on every client.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the trash button on a fact row
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact and click the trash button "Delete this fact".
Read the dialog and click "Delete".
Read the message "Deleted from your account, on every client."
Compare: the fact is gone from the list.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one saved fact

labels.text: Deleted from your account, on every client.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > Clear account memory
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory", press Enter.
Click "Clear account memory".
Read the dialog ("Delete all N memory facts from your Cloud account?") and click "Forget everything".
Read the message "All memory facts deleted from your account."
Compare: open "List & remove facts" and check no facts remain.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved facts

labels.text: All memory facts deleted from your account.

items.note: The Memory list itself has no separate delete-all button; this is the one-action path found.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the detail line under a fact
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact (or read its detail line) to see where it came from.
Compare: facts typed in VS Code show "Saved from VS Code"; facts from a chat show "Saved from the conversation" with its title; facts with no recorded source show "Source not recorded".
items.needs: a signed-in account with facts from more than one source (a typed fact and a chat-saved fact)
items.note: The code says "Saved from an import" for imports and has no "typed by you" wording.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then hover a fact
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact and read the "Created:" line.
Edit that fact with the pencil button "Edit this fact" and save.
Reopen the list and hover the same fact.
Compare: an "Updated:" line now appears under "Created:".
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one saved fact
items.note: The "Updated:" line appears only when the update time differs from the creation time.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, first row
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Read the first row: "Personal memory" with "Read in your personal chats on every device", or "<workspace name> memory" with "Workspace memory, kept apart from your personal memory".
Hover that row to read the separation text.
Compare: workspace facts appear only in workspace chats, and personal facts only in personal chats.
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account that belongs to a workspace, with a personal account memory and a workspace memory to compare

labels.text: Workspace memory, kept apart from your personal memory
Read in your personal chats on every device

items.note: The workspace row appears only when the account is in a workspace; clicking it opens Team settings on the web.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > Never remember…, then Add a term
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory", press Enter.
Click "Never remember…".
Click "Add a term", type a client or project name, press Enter.
Compare: the term appears under "Never remembered".
Run "Code: Add Memory Fact" with a sentence containing that term and compare: it should be refused.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a test term
items.note: No credential or password check was found in the extension files read, so automatic refusal of credentials is unverified.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > Clear account memory (memory reset only)
steps: Note the chats you have in the sidebar.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, run "Code: Memory", click "Clear account memory", then "Forget everything".
Compare: the chats are still listed, and "List & remove facts" shows no facts.
items.needs: a signed-in account with saved facts and at least one chat
items.note: No link from deleting a chat to the memory store was found in the chat state code, so the chat-deletion half could not be located; sign-out also clears the local memory cache.

items.where: Effect seen in the "AGI Code" chat, with any model picked
steps: With Memory on and a fact saved (for example "I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work"), open the "AGI Code" chat and pick a model.
Ask a question the fact answers, such as "What language should you use for my data scripts?"
Switch to a different model in the chat and ask the same question again.
Compare: both replies use the saved fact.
items.needs: a signed-in account with Memory on and a saved fact
items.note: Memory is added to every turn by the same code path; the model is not checked in it.

items.where: Effect seen in the AGI Cloud web app, the AGI CLI or mobile, signed in to the same account
steps: In VS Code, run "Code: Add Memory Fact" and save a fact such as "I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work."
Open the web app, the CLI or mobile on the same account and look for that fact.
Compare: the fact appears there and is used in their chats, as Expected says.
Edit or delete the fact in VS Code and check the other client again.
items.needs: a second client (web app, CLI or mobile) signed in to the same account

labels.text: Saved to your account, on every client.

items.note: The other clients' memory screens were not read, so where to look in them is unverified.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > What should AGI call you?
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click What should AGI call you? and type a name, then press Enter.
Check the row now shows that name instead of Not set.
Send a new chat message and check the reply uses that name.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Personalization is stored for AGI Cloud answers only, per its picker placeholder; the reply check is server-side.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > What do you do?
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click What do you do? and type a short background, up to 120 characters, then press Enter.
Check the row shows that text instead of Not set.
Send a chat message that depends on that background and check the reply keeps it in mind.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: No separate free-text background field exists; the closest is this 120-character field, so it covers Expected only partly. Custom instructions in Settings is a further free-text option.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > What do you do?
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click What do you do? and type a role, such as a job title, then press Enter.
Check the row shows the role.
Send a question in that field of work and check the reply fits that role.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Tailoring of replies happens on the server; the code only stores the text.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Style
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style, then pick Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal or Default.
Check the Style row shows the chosen name.
Send a question and compare the reply with the style chosen.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Only one style can be chosen at a time, as Expected says.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Style > Formal
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and pick Formal.
Check the Style row shows Formal.
Send a question and check the reply uses a formal register.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: There is no separate more or less formal control; only the Formal style option exists, so the check is partial.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Style
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and look at the named choices: Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal.
Pick one preset, then check the Style row shows it.
Send a question and check the reply follows that one preset.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The named presets are the Style choices; the Tone section holds separate on or off traits, not presets.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Tone > Warmth
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Under the Tone heading, click Warmth.
Pick Warm and personable, or Neutral and businesslike, or Default.
Check the Warmth row shows the choice, then send a question and compare the tone of the reply.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Only three settings exist (Default and the two ends), not a graded scale.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Tone > Enthusiasm
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Under the Tone heading, click Enthusiasm.
Pick Energetic and encouraging, or Measured, or Default.
Check the Enthusiasm row shows the choice, then send a question and compare the reply.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Only three settings exist (Default and the two ends), not a graded scale.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Formatting
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Formatting and pick Prose, or Headings and bullet lists, or another option.
Check the Formatting row shows the choice.
Send a question and compare whether the reply uses headings and lists or flowing prose.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: A second setting, Tone > Headers and lists, also covers this; Formatting holds the fuller choice list.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Tone > Emoji
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Under the Tone heading, click Emoji.
Pick No emoji or Emoji welcome.
Check the Emoji row shows the choice, then send a question and check whether the reply uses emoji.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Only the two ends and Default exist, not a graded scale.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Technical level
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Technical level and pick Beginner, Intermediate or Expert.
Check the Technical level row shows the choice.
Send the same technical question and compare the depth of the reply.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: none

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Language
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Language, type a tag such as de, then press Enter.
Check the Language row shows de.
Send a question in English and check the reply is written in German.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The language prompt is a free tag; leaving it empty returns to answering in the language the user writes in.

items.where: Settings > Instructions & editor > Custom instructions > Host default
steps: Click the Code: Open Settings command (or Sidebar > Settings).
Click Instructions & editor in the left list.
Under Custom instructions, type a standing instruction in Host default, then click Save host instructions.
Open a new chat and check the reply follows it; the Effective turn prelude box should show the text.
items.needs: none
items.note: No on or off switch exists in the code: the only way to stop them is to clear the text and save, which deletes it, so Expected's switch-off without deleting is not met. The text is stored locally, not per account.

items.where: Sidebar > Projects > (select a project) > Edit > Instructions
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Projects, then select a project.
In the project list under Edit, click Instructions.
Type project instructions in Project instructions and press Enter.
Open a new chat in that project and check the reply follows the instructions; the Instructions row should now show Set.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one project
items.note: Project instructions are cloud data set on a project; the Instructions & editor section shows only local repository files, which are a separate source.

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Style > Explanatory
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and pick Explanatory.
Check the Style row shows Explanatory.
Ask a how-to question and check the reply explains the reasoning and context.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: none

items.where: Sidebar > Personalization > Style > Concise
steps: Open the sidebar menu and click Personalization.
Click Style and pick Concise.
Check the Style row shows Concise.
Ask a question and check the reply is short and direct.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: Length > Shorter is a related but separate setting in the same menu.

items.where: Settings > Instructions & editor > Effective turn prelude
steps: Click the Code: Open Settings command (or Sidebar > Settings).
Click Instructions & editor in the left list.
Read the Effective turn prelude box; it shows the exact instruction block added to new turns, with its scope in the header.
Read the Runtime-discovered project sources list and compare the named sources with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The header line naming the scope (this VS Code host or this VS Code workspace) comes from apps/extension-vscode/src/features/instructions/customInstructions.ts; the Context panel's Custom instructions row also shows the scope.

items.where: Code: Open Settings > Runtime > Where your data goes > Session history
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Open Settings".
Click "Runtime" in the Settings navigation on the left.
Scroll to the card "Where your data goes".
Read the "Session history" row and compare it with Expected: it should say developer sessions are saved on this computer and are not uploaded to the account.
items.needs: none
items.note: The text is the only evidence in the code: the old quoted code in conversationTreeProvider.ts is gone, and there is no device-only toggle in the settings panel, so the tester can only confirm the statement, not a setting.

items.where: Code: Open Settings > Runtime > Where your data goes (Session history, Memory, AGI Cloud rows; buttons Privacy settings and Memory)
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Open Settings".
Click "Runtime" in the Settings navigation, then scroll to "Where your data goes".
Look at the separate rows: "Session history" and "Memory" each have their own row, and the "AGI Cloud" row states the model-training position.
Click the "Privacy settings" button and the "Memory" button in that card; compare with Expected: history, training and retention each need a clear control or statement.
items.needs: none to read the panel; a web browser for the "Privacy settings" button, which opens a Web page
items.note: Model training is a sentence inside the AGI Cloud row, not its own control; data retention has no wording in this panel and is only reached through the Privacy settings button, which opens the Web page.

items.where: Code: Open Settings > Runtime > Where your data goes
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Open Settings".
Click "Runtime" in the Settings navigation, then scroll to "Where your data goes".
Read the intro line and each row: "Local models", "Your own provider key", "AGI Cloud", "Session history", "Memory".
Compare with Expected: each row should say, in place, what that setting or path does to the data.
items.needs: none
items.note: The explanations sit beside the data paths rather than beside individual toggles, and the Memory row explains the Memory setting only as a statement.

items.where: Code: Open Settings > Runtime > Where your data goes
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Open Settings".
Click "Runtime" in the Settings navigation, then scroll to "Where your data goes".
Read each row for where it is processed: "Local models" (this computer), "Your own provider key" (that provider), "AGI Cloud" (AGI servers, then the provider serving the chosen model).
Compare with Expected: each feature should say on device, AGI cloud or a named provider; the AGI Cloud row names no provider, only "the provider that serves the model you picked".
items.needs: none
items.note: The card covers five data paths, not a per-feature list, and the AGI Cloud row does not name the provider; a "Who processes AGI Cloud requests" button in the same card opens the sub-processor list.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Schedules (or type /schedule in the chat input) > Schedules list > on an active schedule row, click the pause button (tooltip: Pause this schedule). On a paused row the button is Resume this schedule.
steps: Sign in and open the Command Palette, or type /schedule in the chat input.
Run Code: Show Schedules. A quick pick titled Code, Schedules opens.
Find a schedule row that is active and hover it. Click the button whose tooltip is Pause this schedule.
Look at the row: it should now show Paused, as the Expected line says it can be paused.
On the same row, click the button whose tooltip is Resume this schedule, then check the row shows active again.
items.needs: A schedule already created on the account (none is created by the app itself). Sign-in is needed first. Account tier unknown.
items.note: The item is titled Pause briefings, but the code only pauses and resumes schedules (routines). I searched apps/extension-vscode (src and package.json) for briefing and found no match. The pause and resume controls are icon buttons with tooltips only, not visible text. Pause and resume are refused with the message 'this schedule cannot be paused or resumed in its current state' when the schedule is not in a state that allows toggling. The Command Palette entries Code: Pause Schedule and Code: Resume Schedule are hidden (when: false) and reachable only from the row buttons.

items.where: Code: Open Chat > click "Describe a task…" and paste (Cmd+V) an image, or drag an image file onto the composer
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P) to open the chat panel.
Copy a PNG or JPG image, or drag an image file from Finder onto the composer at the bottom.
Look for an attachment chip that shows the file name and a thumbnail.
Type "What is in this image?" in "Describe a task…" and send.
Compare: the reply should describe the image you attached.
items.needs: an image file; a signed-in account
items.note: The "+" menu item "Attach workspace files" and the "/" menu item "Attach file…" both use a text-only picker that rejects images, so only paste and drag work for images.

items.where: Code: Open Chat > drag several image files onto the composer, or paste several images into "Describe a task…"
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Select 2 or 3 image files in Finder and drag them together onto the composer, or copy several images and press Cmd+V in "Describe a task…".
Check that one chip appears for each image.
Type "Compare these images and list the differences" and send.
Compare: the reply should refer to every attached image, not just one.
items.needs: two or more image files; a signed-in account
items.note: A single drop or paste takes at most 8 files and silently ignores the rest (slice in webviewContent.ts).

items.where: Code: Open Chat > click "Describe a task…" and paste (Cmd+V) a screenshot
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Take a screenshot with the macOS screenshot tool so it is copied to the clipboard.
Click in "Describe a task…" and press Cmd+V.
Check that an attachment chip with a thumbnail appears.
Type "Explain what this screenshot shows" and send; compare the reply with what is on the screenshot.
items.needs: a screenshot on the clipboard; a signed-in account
items.note: The extension has no capture button of its own; the code comment on the paste handler names grim and the Snipping Tool as sources, and the macOS capture step comes from the OS, not this code.

items.where: Code: Open Chat > click "Describe a task…" and paste (Cmd+V) a photo, or drag a photo file onto the composer
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Drag a photo of a printed page (JPG or PNG) onto the composer, or copy it and press Cmd+V in "Describe a task…".
Check that the attachment chip appears.
Type "Read this document and summarize it" and send.
Compare: the reply should read the text on the page and summarize it.
items.needs: a photo or scan saved as JPG or PNG; a signed-in account
items.note: A scanned PDF cannot be attached: non-image binary files are skipped with reason 'unsupported binary attachment' (ChatStateManager.ts), so only image files work; a PDF is not tested here.

items.where: Code: Open Chat > drag a chart image onto the composer, or paste it into "Describe a task…"
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Save a chart as a PNG and drag it onto the composer, or copy it and press Cmd+V in "Describe a task…".
Check that the attachment chip appears.
Type "What trends does this chart show? Give the main values" and send.
Compare: the reply should describe the trend and values shown in the chart.
items.needs: a chart image file; a signed-in account

items.where: Code: Open Chat > drag a diagram image onto the composer, or paste it into "Describe a task…"
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Save a diagram as a PNG and drag it onto the composer, or copy it and press Cmd+V in "Describe a task…".
Check that the attachment chip appears.
Type "Explain the structure of this diagram" and send.
Compare: the reply should name the parts of the diagram and how they connect.
items.needs: a diagram image file; a signed-in account

items.where: Code: Open Chat > drag a photo of handwritten notes onto the composer, or paste it into "Describe a task…"
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Take a photo of the handwritten notes, save it as JPG or PNG, and drag it onto the composer.
Check that the attachment chip appears.
Type "Transcribe these handwritten notes" and send.
Compare: the reply should give the written text of the notes.
items.needs: a photo of handwriting saved as JPG or PNG; a signed-in account
items.note: Handwriting is not a separate control; it uses the same image attachment path as the other image items.

items.where: Code: Open Chat > attach an image, ask for its text, then copy the text from the reply
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Drag an image containing text onto the composer, or paste it into "Describe a task…".
Type "Transcribe all the text in this image exactly" and send.
When the reply arrives, select the text and press Cmd+C, or use the "Copy" button on a code block in the reply.
Compare: the copied text should match the text in the image and can be pasted elsewhere.
items.needs: an image with readable text; a signed-in account
items.note: No separate OCR control exists in the code; text extraction is a chat request, and the "Copy" button in the code only appears on code blocks, so plain reply text is copied by selection.

items.where: Code: Open Chat > attach an image, then ask how many items appear in it
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Drag a photo with several countable objects onto the composer, or paste it into "Describe a task…".
Type "How many apples are in this image? Count each one" (use your own object) and send.
Compare: the reply should give a count and the count should match the objects you can see.
items.needs: a photo with countable objects; a signed-in account

items.where: Code: Open Chat > drag two scene images onto the composer, or paste them into "Describe a task…"
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Select two photos of different scenes in Finder and drag both onto the composer, or copy each and paste into "Describe a task…".
Check that two attachment chips appear.
Type "Describe the differences between these two scenes" and send.
Compare: the reply should describe differences from both photos.
items.needs: two scene photos as image files; a signed-in account

items.where: Code: Open Chat > drag a screenshot or photo of the problem onto the composer, or paste it into "Describe a task…"
steps: Run "Code: Open Chat" from the Command Palette to open the chat panel.
Take a screenshot of the error or a photo of the device, save it as PNG or JPG, and drag it onto the composer.
Check that the attachment chip appears.
Type "What is wrong here and what steps should I try?" and send.
Compare: the reply should name the problem shown and give troubleshooting steps.
items.needs: a screenshot or photo of a problem as an image file; a signed-in account

items.where: Settings > Skills > Loaded skills (full list: Settings > Skills > Manage skills, or Command Palette > Code: Show Skills)
steps: Click Settings in the app, then click Skills in the left list.
Read the Loaded skills list: each row shows a skill name and its description.
Or open the Command Palette and type Code: Show Skills to open the full list.
Compare with Expected: the skills installed or made for you should appear in the list.
items.needs: at least one installed or created skill
items.note: The cited commandSetup.ts:2309 and surfaces/index.ts:382 quotes are gone; the list is built in capabilityManagement.ts (manageSkills) and settingsWebviewContent.ts.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Manage skills > Create a skill > Personal
steps: Click Settings, then Skills, then click Manage skills.
Click Create a skill and choose Personal.
Type a lowercase name with hyphens, such as release-notes, and a description, following the prompts.
The new skill file opens for editing. Check it saved under ~/.agiworkforce/skills (or AGIWORKFORCE_HOME if set), and that the list shows its scope as user.
Compare with Expected: the skill is yours and is not tied to one folder.
items.needs: none
items.note: The list shows the raw scope word user, not Personal; the personal folder path comes from code, not a run.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Manage skills > Create a skill > This project
steps: Open a project folder in VS Code.
Click Settings, then Skills, then Manage skills.
Click Create a skill, choose This project, and name the skill.
Check the list: the new skill shows scope project and not allowed yet until you allow it.
Click Allow this folder’s project skills, then open another folder and check the skill does not appear there.
Compare with Expected: the skill loads only in the project it was made for.
items.needs: a project folder open in VS Code
items.note: The project folder is <workspace>/.agiworkforce/skills per skillAuthoring.ts; the check in the other folder is inferred from that path, not run. The quoted capabilityManagement.ts:101 line is gone.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Loaded skills (also Command Palette > Code: Show Skills)
steps: Click Settings, then Skills.
Look at each row in Loaded skills: the skill name is the title and its description is shown under it.
Open Command Palette, type Code: Show Skills, and check each entry shows the name, description and scope.
Compare with Expected: each skill shows its name and what it does.
items.needs: at least one installed or created skill
items.note: A skill not yet allowed in this folder shows Not allowed in this folder yet in place of its description (capabilityManagement.ts).

items.where: Inside a skill run, seen in the chat answer
steps: Create a skill (Settings > Skills > Manage skills > Create a skill > Personal).
In its folder, next to SKILL.md, add a references folder with a text file that holds a made-up fact.
Make sure the skill is on, then in the chat ask a question that needs that fact and asks for the skill to be used.
Compare with Expected: the answer uses the fact from the reference file.
items.needs: none
items.note: Code shows the skill's bundled files are listed under its folder for the model (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:1218); that the model reads them was not confirmed by reading code.

items.where: Inside a skill run, seen in the chat answer or a command the chat runs
steps: Create a skill and add a scripts folder with a small script that writes a marker file.
In SKILL.md, tell the model to run that script.
Make sure the skill is on, then in the chat ask for the task the skill covers.
Compare with Expected: the script runs and the marker file appears.
items.needs: none
items.note: apps/cli/src/skills.rs hashes the scripts folder and lists it for the model (line 1218), but no code found that runs scripts automatically; that whether they run is unknown.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Manage skills (read the detail line of a skill row)
steps: Click Settings, then Skills, then Manage skills.
Find a skill whose SKILL.md lists a tool it needs, or create one that names a tool.
Read the detail after its description: it shows Needs followed by the tool names.
Compare with Expected: a skill whose tool is missing shows Missing ... so it will not load, and does not load.
items.needs: a skill that lists required tools, such as one you write
items.note: The Loaded skills rows show only the description; the requirement line appears only in the Manage skills list.

items.where: Chat start screen > Skills (group) > click the skill name
steps: Open the chat and start a new chat so the start screen shows.
Under the Skills heading, click a skill name; the message box fills with Use the <name> skill to.
Type the task after it and send.
Compare with Expected: the reply follows that skill.
items.needs: a skill that is on and allowed in this folder
items.note: The start-screen group lists only skills that are on and allowed (startSuggestions.ts); the conditions for showing the start screen were not checked, and the /skills slash entry opens the manager, not a picker for a message.

items.where: Inside a chat request; seen in the chat answer
steps: Create a skill with a clear description, such as one about writing release notes.
Make sure it is on and allowed (Settings > Skills > Loaded skills).
In the chat, ask for a task that matches the description without naming the skill.
Compare with Expected: the reply follows the skill's steps.
items.needs: a skill that is on and allowed
items.note: The skill catalog is placed in the model prompt (apps/cli/src/agent/prompt.rs and apps/cli/src/skills.rs format_skill_catalog_for_prompt); the choice is made by the model, so the cited quote is gone and it is not a code rule. The description-matching itself was not run.

items.where: Settings > Skills > Loaded skills (switch on each row), or Settings > Skills > Manage skills > the skill row's Turn off / Turn on button
steps: Click Settings, then Skills.
In Loaded skills, flip the switch of a skill to off; the status line shows Turning <name> off.
Click Manage skills and check the row now shows the off icon.
Flip it back on, and check the skill is still listed (it was not deleted).
items.needs: a skill that is allowed in this folder (the switch is disabled otherwise)
items.note: Removing a personal skill is a different action and deletes its folder; it is not part of this check.

steps: Click the button titled More in the sidebar header (the ... button).
Look through the menu for one Customize entry that holds Skills, Connectors and Plugins together.
Compare with Expected: the menu lists Connectors, Skills, Plugins and MCP servers as separate rows, and no Customize entry exists.
items.needs: the AGI CLI connected to this window
items.note: No 'Customize' wording exists anywhere in apps/extension-vscode (searched case-insensitively). Skills, Connectors and Plugins are separate rows in the sidebar More menu (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/surfaceMenu.ts), and Connectors is not in the Settings nav. The closest single place is Settings > Integrations, which holds Plugins and Skills but not Connectors.

items.where: More > Plugins
steps: Click the button titled More in the sidebar header.
Click Plugins in the menu.
Look at the list: the Browse AGI Cloud Marketplace row comes first, then the installed plugins below it (and an Install a plugin row if installing is offered).
Compare with Expected: the list shows installed plugins, and marketplace plugins are reached through the Browse AGI Cloud Marketplace row, not listed directly.
items.needs: the AGI CLI connected to this window; an installed plugin to see rows (otherwise it reads 'No plugins are installed yet')
items.note: The plugin list itself shows installed plugins only; the available-plugin list is reached through the marketplace browser, so Expected's 'available' is only partly visible in this list. Also reachable at Settings > Integrations > Plugins, which has a Manage plugins button.

items.where: More > Skills (the Skills row sits directly above Plugins)
steps: Click the button titled More in the sidebar header.
Look at the menu: the Skills row sits directly above the Plugins row.
Click Skills and look at the list of loaded skills, with Create a skill and Install a skill rows at the top.
Compare with Expected: Skills sits beside Plugins in the same menu and opens its own list.
items.needs: the AGI CLI connected to this window
items.note: Settings > Integrations also lists Plugins and Skills as separate nav buttons, which is a second route to the same pair.

items.where: More > Plugins, then read the Skills: line under an installed plugin; then More > Skills
steps: Click the button titled More in the sidebar header, then click Plugins.
Look at an installed plugin row: if the plugin includes skills, its second line reads 'Skills:' followed by the skill names; a plugin without skills shows its folder path instead.
Click More > Skills and look for those skill names with the scope word plugin in the row description.
Compare with Expected: the plugin shows its included skills, and those skills appear in the Skills list.
items.needs: an installed plugin that includes skills; the AGI CLI connected to this window
items.note: Usable depends on the skill: a plugin skill shows ', not allowed yet' until it is consented, and the Turn on or Turn off button only appears for consented skills, so usability is not shown on the plugin row itself.

items.where: More > Plugins > click the installed plugin row > Turn off (or Turn on)
steps: Click the button titled More in the sidebar header, then click Plugins.
Click an installed plugin row; a small menu titled with the plugin name opens with a Turn off or Turn on entry.
Click Turn off. The Plugins list reopens; the plugin row icon changes from a filled circle to an empty circle and the plugin is still listed.
Click the same plugin again and choose Turn on. Compare with Expected: the plugin is switched off and on again without being removed from the list.
items.needs: an installed plugin; the AGI CLI connected to this window
items.note: The same toggle also appears as an icon button on the plugin row, with tooltips Turn off and Turn on. Do not use the Remove entry, which uninstalls the plugin.

items.where: Sidebar "More" button (icon only, tooltip "More") > Connectors, then select a connector row. Or Command Palette > Code: Show Connectors.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud in the AGI sidebar. Connectors need a signed-in account.
Click the "More" icon at the top of the AGI sidebar.
Click "Connectors" in the menu. A list opens titled "Code, Connectors".

Hover over a connector row, or select it, and read the detail text. Look for the lines "Can make changes: ..." and "Can read only: ...", plus the line "Connecting and disconnecting happen in the browser, not in VS Code."
Compare with Expected: before connecting, the read and change lines should say in plain words what the connector can read and change.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account; a connector that is listed but not connected yet (its scopes must come from the server)

labels.text: Connecting and disconnecting happen in the browser, not in VS Code.

items.note: The read and change lines come from a name-based guess at each scope (write words like send, edit, delete make "Can make changes"; read, list, view make "Can read only"), and they appear only if the server sends scopes for an unconnected connector. The explanation before connecting is not a separate screen in VS Code; the connect step itself happens on the web app. Not verified in the running app.

items.where: Sidebar "More" button (icon only, tooltip "More") > Connectors, then select a connected connector row. Or Command Palette > Code: Show Connectors.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and connect a connector on the web app first (Connectors are set up on the web, not in VS Code).
Click the "More" icon at the top of the AGI sidebar, then click "Connectors".
Hover over or select the connector row. Read the detail text after the connector name.
Look for "Can make changes: ...", "Can read only: ..." and "Other access: ...", which list the scope names the server returned.
Compare with Expected: the scopes shown should be the ones granted on the account, and they should match what the web app shows.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one connector connected on the web app; a connector that has scopes
items.note: The lines are sorted by name pattern, not shown as a raw list; scope names that match neither pattern appear under "Other access". Whether the list is the granted set depends on the server response, which the code does not check. Not verified in the running app.

items.where: Sidebar "More" button (icon only, tooltip "More") > Connectors. Each connector row shows its health in the row description, after the connector name.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud with at least one connector connected on the web app.
Click the "More" icon at the top of the AGI sidebar, then click "Connectors".

Read the description on each connector row. The first words are the health state, such as "Connected", "Needs reauthorization", "Not responding", "Not connected", "Not configured here" or "Not available on the web app".
To refresh, click the refresh control in the list title (tooltip "Refresh connectors") and read the rows again.
Compare with Expected: each connector should show whether it is healthy, needs reauthorization or is not responding.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account; a connector in a "needs reauthorization" or "not responding" state to see those states (they come from the server and are hard to make on demand)
items.note: The health label comes from the server's health field. If the server sends no health field, the app shows only "Connected" or "Needs reauthorization". The list refreshes itself every 2 minutes. Not verified in the running app.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > Gmail > Ask with it, then type a search request
steps: Sign in to the extension and open the AGI sidebar chat.
In the Connected apps group, click the Ask with it row for Gmail (it is listed only when Gmail is connected on the web).
Type: find emails from a sender you know, and send.
Compare the reply with Expected: matching messages from that sender are listed.
items.needs: an outside account (Google) with Gmail connected on the web
items.note: The search runs on the server through the Gmail connector; the extension only shows the chat, and the tool result was not run.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > Gmail > Ask with it, then type a read request
steps: Open the AGI sidebar chat.
Click Ask with it on the Gmail row under Connected apps.
Type: open the latest email from a named sender and show the full text.
Compare the reply with Expected: the full body of that email is shown, not only a summary line.
items.needs: an outside account (Google) with Gmail connected on the web
items.note: Whether the full body is returned depends on the server tool, which was not run.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > Gmail > Ask with it, then type a draft request
steps: Open the AGI sidebar chat.
Click Ask with it on the Gmail row under Connected apps.
Type: draft a reply to the latest email from a named sender, and do not send it.
Open Gmail in a browser and check the Drafts folder for the new draft, comparing with Expected.
items.needs: an outside account (Google) with Gmail connected on the web
items.note: The Gmail scopes include gmail.compose for drafts, per packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/connector-scopes.ts; the draft itself was not checked.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > Google Calendar > Ask with it, then type a calendar request
steps: Open the AGI sidebar chat.
Click Ask with it on the Google Calendar row under Connected apps.
Type: what events do I have next Tuesday, or search for the word standup.
Compare the reply with the calendar in Google Calendar, using Expected as the test.
items.needs: an outside account (Google) with Google Calendar connected on the web
items.note: The calendar connector id is google-calendar in apps/web/features/connectors/data/connectors.ts; no visible display name for it was found there.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > OneDrive or Google Drive > Ask with it, then type a file search request
steps: Open the AGI sidebar chat.
Click Ask with it on a cloud drive row under Connected apps (OneDrive or Google Drive).
Type: find files named with a word you know in that drive.
Compare the reply with Expected: matching files from the drive are listed.
items.needs: an outside account (Google or Microsoft) with a cloud drive connected on the web
items.note: Google Drive has connector id google-drive in apps/web/features/connectors/data/connectors.ts with no display name found; the search was not run.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > OneDrive or Google Drive > Ask with it, then type a read request
steps: Open the AGI sidebar chat.
Click Ask with it on a cloud drive row under Connected apps.
Type: open the file named with a word you know and show its text.
Compare the reply with Expected: the text of that file is shown.
items.needs: an outside account (Google or Microsoft) with a cloud drive connected on the web
items.note: The download behaviour is a server tool and was not run.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > OneDrive or Google Drive > Ask with it, then type a create request
steps: Open the AGI sidebar chat.
Click Ask with it on a cloud drive row under Connected apps.
Type: create a new text file named with a test word in that drive.
When the approval prompt appears in the chat, read it and choose approve or deny; then check the drive for the new file against Expected.
items.needs: an outside account (Google or Microsoft) with a cloud drive connected on the web
items.note: Google Drive creation is limited to the drive.file scope and OneDrive to its app folder, per packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/connector-scopes.ts.

items.where: Sidebar chat start screen > Connected apps > OneDrive or Google Drive > Ask with it, then type an edit request
steps: Open the AGI sidebar chat.
Click Ask with it on a cloud drive row under Connected apps.
Type: add one line that says a test word to a file you created in that drive.
When the approval prompt appears, read it and choose approve or deny.
Open the file in the drive and check the new line against Expected.
items.needs: an outside account (Google or Microsoft) with a cloud drive connected on the web, and a file you can safely change

items.where: Chat panel > More (the "..." button in the panel header) > MCP servers. Or Command Palette > Code: Show MCP Servers
steps: Sign in, then open the AGI chat panel in the editor.
Click the "..." button in the panel header (tooltip "More").
Click "MCP servers" in the menu.

Look at the list titled "Code, MCP servers". Each configured server is a row with its name, status, transport and scope. With none configured it shows "No MCP servers are configured yet" and "Add an MCP server". Compare with Expected.
items.needs: Signed in, with the AGI CLI available. At least one MCP server configured helps; none shows the empty message.
items.note: The header button has tooltip "More" in the code, so the tester sees that word, not "More actions". The list also appears in Settings under "MCP servers".

items.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Test connection
steps: Open the chat panel and click the "..." button in its header.
Click "MCP servers", then click a server row (not a Remove action).
In the "Choose an action" list, click "Test connection".
Watch for a notification such as "connected in N ms and offers N tools" (success), or a failure message saying the server "did not connect" with a reason. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A configured MCP server. A user-added server is needed for the row to offer actions when its status is not blocked or off.
items.note: The "Test connection" action appears only when the server is not blocked or off. Success text comes from the "mcp.connected" message in apps/extension-vscode/packages/ui path (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json) and reads "Code: {name} connected in {ms} ms and offers {count} tools.".

items.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Show tools
steps: Open the chat panel, click the "..." button in its header, then click "MCP servers".
Click a server row. In the "Choose an action" list, click "Show tools".
Look at the list titled with the server name. Under the "Tools" heading, each tool is shown with its name and description.
If the server has no tools, the list says "This server offers no tools". Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A configured MCP server that connects, so its tools can be listed.
items.note: The code lists tools only when the person chooses "Show tools"; adding a server does not show its tools automatically, which differs from the wording of Expected.

items.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Server details
steps: Open the chat panel, click the "..." button in its header, then click "MCP servers".
Click a server row, then click "Server details" (or use the info button on the row).
A text document named "<server name> MCP server" opens. Read its "Protocol", "Server" and "Capabilities" lines.
Compare the fields shown with Expected (protocol, tools, resources, prompts, extensions).
items.needs: A configured MCP server that is not blocked or off, so the details action appears.
items.note: The details show the server's advertised capabilities as a list, not a fixed list of tools, resources, prompts and extensions. Whether those names appear depends on what the server reports.

items.where: Chat panel > More > MCP servers > click a server row > Server details
steps: Open the chat panel, click the "..." button in its header, then click "MCP servers".
Click a server row, then click "Server details".
Read the "Health" line in the document: "Responding", "Connected, but it did not answer a ping" or "Did not connect".
Scroll to the "Recent output" section. It shows server logs, or "No output from this server yet." Compare with Expected.
items.needs: A configured MCP server that is not blocked or off.
items.note: The code shows recent server output only. It has no call history, so the "call history" part of Expected is not in the code.

items.where: Code: Show MCP Servers (Chat panel > More > MCP servers), then read the row description ending in "project"; Settings > MCP servers shows "From this workspace"
steps: Open the MCP servers list from the chat panel's "..." menu, or run Code: Show MCP Servers.
Look for a server whose row description ends with "project" or whose Settings row says "From this workspace".
Compare with Expected: that server should load only in this project.
items.needs: A workspace with a project-scoped MCP server already configured outside the extension, since the extension cannot create one.
items.note: The extension's "Add an MCP server" flow saves only user-scoped servers, with no project choice, so per-project configuration is not set from the UI; project servers are only shown as "From this workspace". Searched apps/extension-vscode for a project-scope setting or add option and found none.

items.where: AGI Code panel (activity bar) > chat > "Approval needed" card > "Approve" once or "Deny"
steps: Open the AGI Code panel from the activity bar.
Click the "Mode and reasoning effort" button and pick Mode > Ask.
Send a request that edits a file, for example "add a comment to README".
On the "Approval needed" card, click the "Approve once" button, or "Deny" to refuse.
Look at the card: it shows the decision and the run continues or stops, as Expected says.
items.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval (Ask mode).
items.note: The button reads "Approve once", built from the word "Approve"; Expected says "approve or deny" for one call.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" > click a task row with the check icon (tooltip "Approve this run")
steps: Sign in with "Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud".
Start a cloud task that is waiting for approval with several tool calls.
Run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" from the Command Palette and pick the waiting task.
Hover the row action with the check icon, tooltip "Approve this run", and click it.
In the dialog read "Let this task run" with all tool names, then click "Approve and continue". Look for the info message that says the task continues.
items.needs: Signed in to AGI Cloud, and a cloud task waiting on several pending tool calls.
items.note: Batch approval exists only for cloud tasks. The local approval card decides one call at a time.

items.where: AGI Code panel > "Approval needed" card > "Approve <tool name> for session" button
steps: Open AGI Code and set Mode to Ask ("Mode and reasoning effort" > Mode > Ask).
Send a request that makes the same tool ask for approval.
On the card, click the "Approve ... for session" button (it names the tool).
Send a second request that uses the same tool.
Look: no new "Approval needed" card should appear for that tool until the session ends.
items.needs: An AGI account signed in, and a request that triggers a tool approval.
items.note: The session button only appears when the host offers session scope (sessionScopeOffered).

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Permissions" > "Add a rule" > "MCP server or tool"
steps: Run "Code: Permissions" from the Command Palette.
Click "Add a rule".
Pick "MCP server or tool" and type the server name, or server/tool, for example github or github/create_issue.
Pick "Always allowed", "Asks first" or "Blocked".
Look: the rule appears under "Rules for every session" with its decision. Then ask the agent to use that app and check it follows the rule.

items.note: No list of connected apps is shown. The tester types the name. Enforcement at runtime was not checked.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Permissions" > "Trusted folders" section
steps: Run "Code: Permissions" from the Command Palette.
Look under "Trusted folders" for folder rows with the text "The agent may read, edit and run commands here".
Hover a folder row and click the trash icon, tooltip "Stop trusting".
In the modal dialog, click "Stop Trusting".
Look: the folder disappears from the list, and the next action in that folder asks again.
items.needs: At least one trusted folder already granted.
items.note: Revoking is shown. No control to grant a new folder from this list was found, so the granting step is unverified.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Permissions" > "Add a rule" > "Website"
steps: Run "Code: Permissions" from the Command Palette.
Click "Add a rule" and pick "Website".
Type a host, for example example.com or *.example.com.
Pick "Always allowed", "Asks first" or "Blocked".
Look: the rule appears in the list. Then ask the agent to fetch that site and check it follows the rule.
items.needs: A request that makes the agent reach a website.
items.note: Enforcement at runtime was not checked.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Permissions" (rules list)
steps: Add a rule with "Code: Permissions" > "Add a rule" (see S59.06).
Close the list and run "Code: Permissions" again.
Look: the rule is still listed with its decision.
Start a new chat or session and check the rule still shows.
Check whether it also shows on another signed-in device, as Expected says.
items.needs: Nothing beyond an AGI account; a second device to check the cross-device part.
items.note: Storage is kept by the CLI. Cross-device sync of these rules was not verified in this code.

items.where: AGI Code panel > "Mode and reasoning effort" button > Mode group, or Command Palette > "Code: Choose Agent Mode"
steps: Open AGI Code and click the "Mode and reasoning effort" button.
In the Mode group, pick Plan, Ask, Auto or Bypass permissions.
Or run "Code: Choose Agent Mode" from the Command Palette and pick a mode.
Look: the button label changes to the chosen mode, and the next tool action follows that mode.
items.needs: An AGI account signed in.
items.note: The VS Code modes are Plan, Ask, Auto and Bypass permissions, not the three Expected names. Bypass is the nearest to skip approvals.

items.needs: none
items.note: No read-only mode that refuses write, send and execute tools was found. The closest is Plan, described as "Generate a plan; no edits until approved" (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts), which does not say sends or commands are refused.

items.where: AGI Code panel > "Mode and reasoning effort" button > Mode > Ask
steps: Open AGI Code and click the "Mode and reasoning effort" button.
Pick Mode > Ask.
Send a request that reads a file and then edits it.
Look: the read runs without a card, and the edit stops at an "Approval needed" card.
