items.note: No screen names multi-round tool use; the registry value is not shown to a person.

items.where: Chat composer > Mode and reasoning effort button > Reasoning effort group
steps: In the chat composer, click the button labelled Mode and reasoning effort.
Read the Reasoning effort group in the popover.
Click the model pill (Auto) and choose a model; reopen Mode and reasoning effort.
Compare: the group lists only the levels that model takes, or shows This model does not take a reasoning effort. when it takes none.
items.needs: none

labels.text: This model does not take a reasoning effort.

items.note: The effort button is hidden while a reply streams; the picker does not say which models take effort.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (the N context figure), and the context figure in the chat composer after a reply
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Read the grey detail line under a model: its id, then N context and N output.
Close the picker, send a message in chat, then hover over the context figure in the composer.
Compare the tooltip text Context after the last turn with Expected and with the context figure from the picker.
items.needs: none
items.note: Trimming or refusal of over-long requests is not visible in the app; the context figure appears only after a reply.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (the N output figure on each model's detail line)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Read the detail line under a model: its id, N context, then N output.
Compare the N output figure with Expected.
items.needs: none
items.note: The output cap applied to a request is not shown; only the limit figure in the picker is visible.

items.where: No control of its own; the request path picks the transport
items.needs: none
items.note: Searched the extension for a streaming setting; none is shown to a person.

items.where: Chat reply > Prompt cache line under the reply (after a second message in the same chat)
steps: Sign in, open a chat and send a message; wait for the reply.
Send a second message in the same chat and wait for the reply.
Look under the second reply for a line starting Prompt cache with reused or written token counts.
Compare with Expected; the line appears only when the reply reports cache tokens.
items.needs: a chat whose route reports prompt-cache tokens (the app does not say which routes do)
items.note: Whether routing chooses a model or route for its cache class is not visible in the app.

items.where: No control of its own; routing refuses routes outside a region
items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for region and residency; no region setting or region text was found.

items.where: No control of its own; routing honours retention rules
items.needs: none
items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for retention; none found. Local privacy mode concerns network access, not retention.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Scroll through every provider group in the list.
Compare the models listed with Expected: models whose availability is not live are left out of the list.
items.needs: none
items.note: The picker shows no deprecated or retired label; a tester cannot see which models were removed without the registry.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Select Model (locked group headings at the bottom of the list)
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Select Model, press Enter.
Scroll to the bottom and read the locked group headings.
Click a locked model and read the message that explains it cannot run on this session's route.
Compare the headings and message with Expected.
items.needs: a session whose route locks some models (for example a signed-out or Free session)
items.note: Per-route price, retention and cache class are not shown in the picker; route ranking is not visible.

items.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) shows the combined result of plan, model and route; locked rows show a lock icon
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud in the VS Code extension
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model" from the Command Palette
Look at which rows are usable and which show a lock icon, then compare with the plan on the account
Expected: the list matches the plan and route the session resolved
items.needs: a Free account and a paid account, to compare
items.note: The resolver itself has no screen. Its effect is seen only in the picker rows. Server-side checks are not visible in the UI.

items.where: The composer button titled "Mode and reasoning effort" (its summary shows the mode and effort), then pick a model in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)
steps: Open the chat composer
Note the "Mode and reasoning effort" button and its label
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model", and choose a different model
Look at the model pill and the "Mode and reasoning effort" button: effort should appear, change or show "effort unavailable for this model" to match Expected
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least two models that differ in effort support
items.note: Attachment options per model were not located as a separate control. The only model-based attachment wording found is "cannot read images you attach" in modelConstants.ts. The sidebar view name was not verified.

items.where: The "Mode and reasoning effort" composer button, then the effort list after choosing a model
steps: Pick a model that supports effort in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)
Open the "Mode and reasoning effort" button and note the levels offered
Pick a model that does not take effort
Open the same button: it should read "This model does not take a reasoning effort." and no unsupported level should be sent, as Expected says
items.needs: a signed-in account with one model that takes effort and one that does not

labels.text: This model does not take a reasoning effort.

items.note: Whether unsupported levels are dropped from the request was only checked in the code, through supportedEffort in modelConstants.ts. The tester can see only what the menu offers.

items.where: Locked rows in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M). The entitlement check runs in the app for each model and on the server for each route
steps: Sign in with a Free account
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model"
Choose a row with a lock icon
Expected: the message "is not in the plan this session resolved. Upgrade your AGI plan to use it." appears and no turn starts
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The server-side check is not visible to a tester. Only the UI gate can be seen.

items.where: The "Usage" pill in the chat panel (expand it to see "Per-limit usage breakdown")
steps: Sign in to an AGI Cloud account
Find the "Usage" pill in the chat panel
Click it to show usage details
Compare the remaining allowance and per-limit list with the server's numbers on the account's usage page
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The rules that decide when the meter is shown were not traced. The pill and the list are the visible part.

items.needs: a workspace administrator policy and a member account
items.note: Found only "A workspace administrator can turn it off for every member." at apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/settingsWebviewContent.ts (line 1979). The setting it belongs to was not traced. Searched the extension's features, integrations and core folders for policy or admin wording.

items.needs: an account and a sign-in
items.note: The code lines named in the plan are gone or changed: deviceAuth.ts has no age or eligibility check, and AuthSwitchLine.tsx no longer exists. Searched deviceAuth.ts and webviewContent.ts for age and eligibility wording with no match. The web app device page was not searched.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Check the CLI in This Environment" (or "Code: Install AGI CLI")
steps: Open the Command Palette
Run "Code: Check the CLI in This Environment"
Read the result message
Optional: set the agiWorkforce.cliPath setting to a path that does not exist, run the check again, and read the message "The AGI CLI could not be started." to compare with Expected
items.needs: none

labels.text: Code: Check the CLI in This Environment

items.note: Whether the check command shows the localRuntimeClient message in the UI was not traced.

items.where: The model pill tooltip on the composer, which reads "effort unavailable for this model" when the model has no effort control
steps: Choose a model without reasoning effort in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)
Hover the model pill
Expected: the effort part of the pill and its tooltip are absent or say "effort unavailable" instead of a broken control
items.needs: a signed-in account with a model that takes no effort
items.note: The hidden-control rule is inside the webview. The visible part is the wording on the pill.

items.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) > a locked row, shown with a lock icon and disabled
steps: Sign in with a Free account
Press Cmd+Shift+M, or run "Code: Select Model"
Look for rows with a lock icon: they stay in the list but are disabled
Choose a locked row and read the reason that appears, as Expected says
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The sentence shown on choosing a locked row was read in code, not seen in the UI.

items.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) > a locked row, or the "Upgrade" button in the chat panel, or Command Palette > "Code: Upgrade Your Plan"
steps: Sign in with a Free account
Press Cmd+Shift+M, choose a locked row, and read which plan it names (for example "Max plan")
Close the picker and click the "Upgrade" button in the chat panel, or run "Code: Upgrade Your Plan"
Expected: the plan that unlocks the feature and the way to upgrade are shown
items.needs: a Free account
items.note: The plan name in a locked row comes from the picker capability label. The paywall actions in cloudUtilityErrorActions.ts were not triggered.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Set Agent Mode", then choose Bypass
steps: Open a folder in VS Code
Run "Code: Set Agent Mode" from the Command Palette
Choose the Bypass option
Read the warning "Turn on Bypass Permissions?" and its detail text, then press Cancel to compare with Expected
items.needs: a folder open in VS Code
items.note: The visible label for the Bypass option was not found as plain text outside the tests. It likely comes from a mode label constant that was not traced.

items.where: A chat turn that fails with provider unavailable, rate limit, spent free allowance, stream interrupted or safety refusal shows a "Switch model" action
steps: Choose a model and send a message that fails (for example, a model at its rate limit)
Read the failure message in the chat
Click the "Switch model" action
Expected: the model picker opens so another model can be chosen
items.needs: a condition that makes a turn fail, such as a Free account whose allowance is spent
items.note: The failure button text "Switch model" was found in tests and in errorPresentation.ts logic, not verbatim in the source. The listed label is the picker entry.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Continue in the Cloud"
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud and have a cloud task on a repository
Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Continue in the Cloud"
Read the result: the branch should be handed to a cloud session
Expected: the work continues in the other app or device
items.needs: an AGI Cloud account and a cloud task
items.note: The when-clause that decides when the command appears was not checked. Pulling a cloud result back is a separate command, Code: Pull Cloud Task Into Workspace.

items.needs: a signed-in account and a provider key
items.note: No explicit chooser for local model, own key or managed cloud was found. The picker shows the route through the "Sign in to AGI Cloud" and "Add another provider key" lock wording in modelConstants.ts, and a command agi-workforce.manageProviderKeys exists in package.json, but its title was not confirmed. Reachability.ts was only partly read.

items.where: The "Mode and reasoning effort" composer button, after changing model
steps: Choose a model with fewer effort levels in Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M)
Set the effort to the highest level in the "Mode and reasoning effort" button
Send a short message
Expected: the effort sent is moved to the nearest level the model accepts, and the button shows that level
items.needs: a signed-in account with two models that have different effort ladders
items.note: The correction happens in supportedEffort in modelConstants.ts. The request itself is not visible in the UI, so only the button label can be compared.

items.where: Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) rows change after a plan change, without restarting VS Code
steps: Open Code: Select Model (Cmd+Shift+M) and note the lock icons
Change the plan on the account (outside VS Code)
Return to VS Code and open Code: Select Model again without restarting
Expected: the locked rows update to match the new plan
items.needs: a second account or plan change to test with
items.note: The revalidation listener is in tierRevalidation.ts. What triggers the revalidation was not traced.

items.where: Model pill (the word Auto under the chat box) > Recommended > Auto
steps: Open a new chat in the AGI VS Code panel and read the model pill.
Confirm the pill says Auto and that Auto is the first row under Recommended when you click it.
Type a short question and send it.
Check that the answer arrives and the pill still says Auto, with no model picked by you. Compare with Expected: Auto picks a model for each request.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account (Auto is greyed out when signed out)
items.note: The app does not show which model answered a request on these screens, so the tester can only check that Auto is selected and the answer arrives.

items.where: Model pill > click a named model (not Auto); or Command Palette > Code: Select Model
steps: Click the model pill above the chat box.
Choose a named model from the list (for example one under On this device if a local model is running, or another listed model).
Send a short message.
Check that the pill now shows the model you chose, and that the answer comes back. Compare with Expected: the request runs on the model you picked.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account; a local model in Ollama or LM Studio for the On this device group (optional)
items.note: I confirmed the pill and the Code: Select Model command; I did not confirm the label of each cloud provider group.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Projects > open a project > Default model
steps: Run Code: Show Projects from the Command Palette.
Open a project with Code: Open Project.
Click Default model in the project list and pick a model (or No default model to clear it).
Run Code: Use Project in This Chat and start a new chat; compare the model pill with Expected. If the pill differs, a message offers Choose the model.
items.needs: a signed-in account with at least one project

labels.text: Code: Use Project in This Chat

items.note: The code offers the default model as a choice when the project is used; I did not confirm that every new chat in the project starts on it without that step.

items.where: Model pill > Recommended > Auto · Best
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Best.
Send a coding or reasoning question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Best and the answer arrives. Compare with Expected: a task-specific profile is applied.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account on a plan that includes the Best profile
items.note: Expected says premium for coding and reasoning, but the row is called Best and its description reads The most capable model your plan includes, for harder work. The task-type choice is inner and not shown.

items.where: Model pill > Recommended > Auto · Instant
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Instant.
Send a short question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Instant and the answer comes back quickly. Compare with Expected: the fastest eligible route is used.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account
items.note: The row is called Instant, and its description reads Answers fastest, on the quickest models your plan includes.

items.where: Model pill > Recommended > Auto · Best
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Best.
Send a harder question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Best and the answer arrives. Compare with Expected: the most capable eligible route is used.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account on a plan that includes the Best profile
items.note: The Best row is the same row as S79.04; the code has one quality profile for both.

items.where: Model pill > Recommended > Auto · Economy
steps: Click the model pill.
Under Recommended, choose Auto · Economy.
Send a simple question.
Check that the pill keeps Auto · Economy and the answer arrives. Compare with Expected: the cheapest eligible route is used.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account
items.note: The row is called Economy, and its description reads The lowest-cost model that can handle the task.

items.needs: a local model running in Ollama or LM Studio (for the nearest control)
items.note: No privacy-first profile is in the Auto rows (only Auto, Instant, Best, Economy). The nearest visible controls are the On this device group in the model pill and the trust-boundary warning in Code: Select Model. Searched the model-picker folder and the routing profile list for privacy.

items.where: Inner routing step; its effect is only seen through which model Auto uses
items.needs: none
items.note: Intent classification runs in the chat state code for each message when Auto is selected, with no control or label of its own.

items.where: Inner routing step; its effect is only seen through the answer
items.needs: none
items.note: Tool needs are classified per request with no control of their own; the Browse the web toggle is a separate manual control.

items.where: Seen when an image is attached in the chat box: the answer should describe the image
steps: Click the plus control in the chat box and choose an image under Add context.
Send a question about the image.
Check that the answer describes the image instead of saying it cannot see one. Compare with Expected: the request is sent to a model that accepts images.
items.needs: an image file and a signed-in AGI account
items.note: The exact label of the plus control was not confirmed; the menu is labelled Add context.

items.where: Inner classification; no screen shows the complexity level
items.needs: none
items.note: Complexity is classified per request with no visible label; the effort setting is a separate control.

items.where: Inner detection; the manual control is Browse the web in the plus menu
items.needs: none
items.note: The code detects fresh-information requests without a control. The Browse the web toggle is manual and is not the automatic detection Expected describes.

items.where: Model pill list: greyed rows and the Needs setup on this machine section
steps: Sign out, or use an account with no plan, then open the model pill.
Look for greyed Auto rows and any Needs setup on this machine section.
Open Command Palette > Code: Select Model and check that unavailable rows show a lock.
Compare with Expected: unavailable models are not offered as choices that fail.
items.needs: a signed-out or no-plan account
items.note: The pill list greys rows; the lock icon appears in the Code: Select Model list.

items.where: Inner provider-route choice; no screen shows the chosen route
items.needs: none
items.note: Route ranking by health, cost and cache is server and runtime logic with no visible control.

items.where: Model pill > click a named model (not Auto), then send a message that fails
steps: Pick a named model in the model pill.
Send a message.
If the turn fails, read the failure card; it offers Switch model, and the chat does not switch by itself.
If you pick a model that would lose something, read the Switch to <model>? prompt and its Switch anyway button. Compare with Expected: the chosen model is not replaced silently.
items.needs: a signed-in account; a route that fails (for example a spent free allowance) to see the card
items.note: The code keeps the chosen model; I did not confirm an end-to-end failure that keeps the same model.

items.where: Seen only when the free allowance or plan limit is spent: the failure card offers Switch model
steps: Use up the free allowance on a Free account, or hit a plan limit.
Send a message.
Read the failure card and check that it offers Switch model or names a reset time. Compare with Expected: routing accounts for the remaining budget.
items.needs: a Free account with a spent allowance
items.note: Budget-aware choice of route is inner logic; only the resulting failure card is visible.

items.where: Seen on a failed turn: the failure card offers Continue with <model> and Switch model
steps: Cause a route failure, for example a provider with no credit.
Read the failure card.
Click Continue with <model> if it is shown, and check the turn is sent again on another model. Compare with Expected: failed calls fall back to a healthy alternative.
items.needs: a route that fails (for example a provider with no credit)
items.note: Health-based demotion is inner; the visible part is the card and its offer.

items.where: Chat failure card > Switch model (opens the model list)
steps: Cause a route failure, for example a spent free allowance.
Read the red failure card.

Click Switch model and check that the model list opens. If the card instead shows Continue with <model>, click it and check the turn is resent on that model. Compare with Expected: a one-click switch is offered.
items.needs: a route failure, for example a spent free allowance
items.note: Switch model opens the model list rather than switching in one click; the one-click path is Continue with <model>, shown only when the failure names an alternative.

items.where: Model pill shows Auto as the default
steps: Open a new chat and do not change the model pill.
Check the pill reads Auto.
Send a plain message and check an answer arrives. Compare with Expected: an unclear request falls back to a safe default.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI account
items.note: The fallback itself is inner logic in the routing code; the visible part is that the default is Auto.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Compare Plans
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the list. Each row shows the plan name, a usage line, and an Includes or Adds over line.
Find the usage line on the paid plans. Look for "Same usage as <plan>" or "<n>x more usage than <plan>" and check that the baseline plan is named.
Compare with Expected: a plan that is the baseline for 5x/15x should be named with its concrete allowance. The Free row says "A usage allowance, free models only".
items.needs: a signed-in account (the list also opens signed out)

labels.text: Compare prices and upgrade on Web

items.note: No "1x" wording and no concrete allowance number was found in the plan copy; the baseline appears only by name in "Same usage as <plan>" (managed-usage-limits.ts:236) and in the multiplier lines.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Compare Plans
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the usage line of a paid plan, for example "<n>x more usage per session and <m>x more weekly usage than <plan>".
Open Code: Account & Usage (Cmd+Shift+P) and read the usage rows "Current session" and "This week" for the windows.
Compare with Expected: the copy should name which allowance is multiplied, the current session window and the weekly window. No monthly window was found in the code.
items.needs: a signed-in paid account is best to see the usage rows
items.note: The code names only the 5-hour session window and the weekly window; the Expected monthly window is not in the code.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Compare Plans
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the detail line under each plan: "Includes: ...", "Adds over <plan>: ..." or "No features beyond <plan>".
Compare the feature lists between two plans and check that they differ in features as well as usage.
Compare with Expected: each difference should be listed. The server-side enforcement of each gate is not visible from the extension and needs the web app or a live test.
items.needs: a signed-in account, ideally on a plan other than the top one, so that the "Adds over" line appears

labels.text: Compare prices and upgrade on Web

items.note: The feature list is built from billing-catalog.ts; the enforcement of each gate is inner behaviour and is not confirmed from the extension UI.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Open Actions > Model > Effort: <level>
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Open Actions" and choose "Code: Open Actions".
Under the "Model" separator, read the "Effort: <level>" row. Its description reads "Set reasoning effort (low / medium / high / max)".
Choose "Switch model…" and see which models are listed.

Compare with Expected: the Effort and model choice should be shown as gated options for some plans. The code does not show a plan gate on these rows, and the server-side clamp of each request is not visible from the UI.
items.needs: a Free account and a paid account, to compare which options are gated
items.note: The Effort row and Switch model row were found in the action sheet; no plan gate on them was found in the code, and the server clamp is inner behaviour.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage > "Most capable models" row
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Account & Usage" and choose "Code: Account & Usage".
Find the row labelled "Most capable models" with its usage and reset time.
Compare its description and limit with the weekly row "This week".

Compare with Expected: the flagship weekly cap should be shown separately and, when used up, the blocked-request message should appear. The row is shown only when the account has a flagship allowance.
items.needs: a paid account with a flagship weekly allowance; the cap-used message needs the allowance used up
items.note: The admission block message is in billing-catalog.ts (flagship_weekly_limit_reached); the cap-used state is hard to reach from the UI and is not confirmed here.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage > "<plan> subscription: <status>" warning row
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Account & Usage" and choose "Code: Account & Usage".
Look for a warning row "<plan> subscription: <status>" with the description "Paid Cloud capabilities are paused until billing is resolved".
Read the "Manage billing & subscription" row and its description.

Compare with Expected: a failed renewal should show what access remains and how to fix it. The extension shows only that paid capabilities are paused; no grace-period rule or grace length was found for paid plans.
items.needs: a paid account with a subscription that needs attention (for example a failed renewal), which the tester may not be able to create

labels.text: Paid Cloud capabilities are paused until billing is resolved

items.note: No grace-period rule for paid plans was found in the extension. Grace language exists only for enterprise contracts (packages/contracts/types/src/enterprise/contract-lifecycle.ts).

items.where: Code: Account & Usage shows the plan name, same as the web app for the same account
steps: Sign in to the VS Code extension with an account that has a paid plan.
Open Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage and note the "Plan: <name>" description on the "Cloud usage" or "Cloud quota" row.
Sign in to the same account on the web, and open its usage page.
Compare with Expected: both surfaces should show the same plan and usage. The per-surface server enforcement is not visible from the UI.
items.needs: the same account signed in on two surfaces (VS Code and the web)
items.note: The extension reads the server plan through /api/usage (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts); the sharing itself is inner behaviour seen only as matching values.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Compare Plans, then the "Adds over" detail of each plan
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Compare Plans" and choose "Code: Compare Plans".
Read the detail line of each plan. Plans above your plan show "Adds over <your plan>: <features>", and your plan shows its own features.
Open Code: Open Actions and find "Upgrade for higher capacity" (or run Code: Upgrade Your Plan) to see the upgrade prompt.
Compare with Expected: each plan should explain what it adds, and a blocked feature should say which plan it needs. The blocked-feature wording is in the server copy, not the extension.
items.needs: a signed-in account on a plan below the top plan

labels.text: Compare prices and upgrade on Web

items.note: The "why a blocked feature needs a plan" text is in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts and was not confirmed as shown in VS Code.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Open Settings" > "Usage & billing" (left list); the plan name is in the top card
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Open Settings".
Click "Usage & billing" in the left list.
Read the plan name in the top card and compare it with the plan on the AGI Cloud account page in the browser.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The plan name is filled from the server; the page shows "Unknown" until the account loads. Code could not confirm the wording of the plan name itself.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Open Settings" > "Usage & billing" > "Plan usage" row (reset date)
steps: Run "Code: Open Settings" from the Command Palette.
Click "Usage & billing".
Look at the "Plan usage" row for the "resets" date.
If the subscription is set to cancel, look for the cancellation date under the plan card.
items.needs: a paid account (the Plan usage row is hidden on the Free plan)
items.note: The code shows a reset date and, only when cancelling, the period-end date. No separate "renews on" line was found, so the renewal date may not appear as Expected says.

items.where: Sidebar chat > usage meter bar at the top of the panel (cloud icon, bar, "Usage: " text); the same meter is in Settings > "Usage & billing" > "Plan usage"
steps: Open the AGI sidebar in the Activity Bar and sign in to a Managed Cloud account.
Look for the thin usage bar with the cloud icon and the "Usage: " text.
Click the "×" button to collapse it, then the small pill labelled "Usage" to show it again.
Compare the bar fill with the percentage text in the Plan usage row in Settings.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account (the bar is hidden for BYOK and unbounded routes)
items.note: The bar is only shown for the Managed Cloud route, and its location in the panel is taken from the markup order, not from a screenshot.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Open Settings" > "Usage & billing" > "Usage history" > "By model" list
steps: Run "Code: Open Settings" from the Command Palette.
Click "Usage & billing".
Scroll to the "Usage history" heading and read the "By model" list.
Compare the per-model rows with the flagship weekly window in the plan usage rows.
items.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
items.note: The flagship cap comes from the server window list; the exact visible label for it was not confirmed in the code I read.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Open Settings" > "Usage & billing" > "Usage history" > "By product area" list
steps: Run "Code: Open Settings" from the Command Palette.
Click "Usage & billing".
Scroll to "Usage history" and read the "By product area" list.
Look for a coding or agent work row and compare it with Expected.
items.needs: a paid account with some settled usage
items.note: The list is by product area and the row names come from a shared function (usageWorkloadLabel) that I did not locate, so the exact coding label is unknown.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Account & Usage" > quick pick row "Credits: ..."; the same row is in Settings > "Usage & billing" > "Credits"
steps: Run "Code: Account & Usage" from the Command Palette.
Read the "$(credit-card) Credits: ..." row and the "plan usage" rows above it.
Click "Usage & billing" in Settings (Code: Open Settings) and read the "Credits" row.
Compare the balance with the plan windows listed.
items.needs: a paid account with a credit balance

items.where: Settings > "Usage & billing" > "Credits" row (spendability line); the plan windows are shown in the separate "Plan usage" rows
steps: Run "Code: Open Settings" from the Command Palette and click "Usage & billing".
Read the "Plan usage" rows (included allowance) and the "Credits" row (balance).
Read the spendability line under Credits: "Buy credits to work past a limit", "Spent when a limit stops you" or "Off - enable in billing to spend".
Compare what is listed as included with what is listed as credits.
items.needs: a paid account

labels.text: Buy credits to work past a limit

items.note: The code separates included plan windows from the credit balance, but no visible word "purchased" was found in the labels I read.

items.where: Command Palette > "Code: Account & Usage" > plan usage row (description shows the reset); sidebar usage meter shows the reset after the usage text
steps: Run "Code: Account & Usage" from the Command Palette.
Read the description on each "plan usage" row.
Open the sidebar and read the reset text after the "Usage: " bar.
Compare the time left with Expected. A row with no reset shows "No reset pending".
items.needs: a paid account with a usage window that resets
items.note: The countdown wording is made by a shared formatter (formatUsageResetIn) that I did not read, so the exact text is unknown.

items.needs: a paid account with an agent run
items.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for per-task, by-task, per-task usage and task cost; no per-task usage view was found. The only per-session figures are "Billed this session" and the usage history, which group by product area, model and period.

items.where: Status bar (bottom of the window) after a chat turn ends: a message appears for about 10 seconds; or Command Palette > "Code: Show Token Breakdown" > "Billed this session" row
steps: Send one chat message with a Managed Cloud account and wait for the reply to finish.
Watch the bottom status bar for the message "Code: this turn was billed ..." (it stays about 10 seconds).
If it says "so far" with a count of unsettled requests, wait a few seconds and check again.
Run "Code: Show Token Breakdown" and read the "Billed this session" row.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account and a finished chat turn
items.note: The turn message is a status bar message, not a popup, so the tester must look straight after the reply ends.

items.where: Sidebar chat > usage meter bar; the bar changes colour as the remaining share drops, and an "Upgrade" button appears when the server asks for it
steps: Use a Managed Cloud account close to its limit (or ask a tester who has one).
Open the sidebar and look at the usage bar's colour and fill.
Look for the "Upgrade" button on the bar.
Compare with Expected: the user should be warned before the limit is reached.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account close to a limit
items.note: The warning is a colour change and the Upgrade button; no text such as "running low" was found in the code I read. Thresholds come from the server.

items.where: Sidebar chat > send a message when the Managed Cloud quota is used up > warning popup at the bottom of VS Code with "Add credits", "Upgrade" or "View usage"; the bar shows "Managed Cloud quota exhausted"
steps: Use a Managed Cloud account whose quota is used up.
Send a chat message.
Read the warning popup: its title, the limit message and the reset time.
Read the buttons "Add credits", "Upgrade" and "View usage", and the sidebar bar text "Managed Cloud quota exhausted".
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account at its limit
items.note: The limit message text comes from the server, so the exact words of the reason are not in the code.

items.where: Same warning popup as S82.25 > button "Use ${modelDisplayLabel(alternative)}" (shows the model name), offered only when the server suggests a standard model and one is eligible
steps: Use a Managed Cloud account blocked on the chosen model, where a cheaper eligible model exists.
Send a chat message so the warning popup appears.
Look for the button that starts with "Use " followed by a model name.
Click it and check that the chat retries with that model.
items.needs: an account blocked on its model with an eligible alternative
items.note: The button is only shown when the server sets suggestStandardModel and an alternative is eligible; it is not always shown.

items.where: Same warning popup as S82.25 > reset time at the end of the message; no wait button exists
steps: Reach a limit as in S82.25.
Read the popup message: the reset time is added after the limit text.
Look at the buttons: "Add credits", "Upgrade", "View usage" (and "Use ..." if offered).
Compare with Expected: the code offers no button to wait until reset.
items.needs: a Managed Cloud account at its limit
items.note: The reset time is shown in the message, but no option to wait instead of paying exists in the code (the buttons are Add credits, Upgrade, View usage and the model switch). Expected is not met by the code.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage, then the row "subscription:" with a warning icon (under the plan name)
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the Command Palette with Code: Sign In to AGI Cloud, using an account whose paid subscription is not active.
Open the Command Palette and run Code: Account & Usage.
Look for a row that starts with the plan name and "subscription:" and a warning icon, with the description "Paid Cloud capabilities are paused until billing is resolved".
Look for the row "Manage billing & subscription"; when the subscription needs attention its description reads "Restore paid Cloud access on Web", which is the fix path.
Compare with Expected: the failure is shown clearly and the way to fix it is shown.
items.needs: a paid AGI Cloud account whose subscription is not active (a failed payment cannot be produced on demand from the tester's side)

labels.text: Paid Cloud capabilities are paused until billing is resolved
Restore paid Cloud access on Web

items.note: The app has no checkout or payment screen of its own; the failure is shown only as a status row in Account & Usage, and the fix is on the Web (the row text says so). The row text is built from the subscription status with underscores replaced by spaces.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage, then the "AGI Cloud account" section rows (organization row with the plan, and "Manage billing & subscription")
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud with an account that has a paid plan with a scheduled cancellation at period end.
Open the Command Palette and run Code: Account & Usage.

Look in the "AGI Cloud account" section for the organization row: its description reads "<plan name> plan · ends <date>" and its detail reads "Access remains active through <date>, then the plan ends".
Look at the "Manage billing & subscription" row: its description reads "Access ends <date>; review or resume the plan on Web" when the end date is known.
Compare with Expected: the cancellation is shown with its end date.
items.needs: a paid AGI Cloud account with a scheduled end-of-period cancellation (the tester cannot create this on demand; the account must already be in that state)
items.note: The date is formatted with the system locale (for example "Dec 31, 2026"). If the end date is not known the row shows "Review the scheduled cancellation on Web" instead of a date.

items.where: Settings (gear icon, title "Settings", at the top of the AGI Code panel) > General > Model preference > Choose. Also the command "Code: Select Model".
steps: Click the gear icon titled Settings at the top of the AGI Code panel.
Click General in the left list.
Under Model and reasoning, find Model preference and click Choose.
Pick a model from the list and confirm it.
Close Settings, open a new chat, and check that the model shown is the one you picked.
Compare with Expected: a new conversation should start with the chosen model.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Settings screen says "Auto chooses a model for the current session" and does not say "default for new conversations"; the VS Code setting agiWorkforce.model is described as "Default LLM model" in apps/extension-vscode/package.json. I did not verify that a new chat starts with the chosen model.

items.where: Settings (gear icon, title "Settings") > General > Reasoning effort. Also the slash command /effort in the composer.
steps: Click the gear icon titled Settings at the top of the AGI Code panel.
Click General in the left list.
Under Model and reasoning, find Reasoning effort and open its dropdown.
Pick a different level, for example High.
Close Settings, then reopen it and check that Reasoning effort still shows High.
Compare with Expected: the chosen level should be used for new turns.
items.needs: none
items.note: The Reasoning effort help text says "Used only by providers that expose an explicit reasoning-effort control", and the screen does not say "default for new turns". The levels are None, Minimal, Low, Medium, High, xHigh and Max. Whether a turn uses the chosen level depends on the provider, which I did not check.

items.where: Settings (gear icon, title "Settings") > General > Agent mode.
steps: Click the gear icon titled Settings at the top of the AGI Code panel.
Click General in the left list.
Under Model and reasoning, find Agent mode and open its dropdown.
Pick Plan from the list.
Close Settings, then reopen it and check that Agent mode still shows Plan.
Compare with Expected: the mode chosen should be the one new conversations start in.
items.needs: none
items.note: The modes in the code are Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass permissions. There is no chat versus agent choice, so the Expected wording "chat vs agent/work" is not what the screen offers. Bypass permissions needs a separate risk confirmation.

items.where: More (ellipsis icon, title "More", at the top of the AGI Code panel) > Help > Keyboard shortcuts. The item opens VS Code's own Keyboard Shortcuts editor filtered to AGI Code.
steps: Click the More icon (ellipsis) at the top of the AGI Code panel.
Click Help.
Click Keyboard shortcuts. VS Code's Keyboard Shortcuts tab opens filtered to AGI Code.
Pick an AGI command row and use the pencil icon or the right-click menu to change its key, or remove its key to disable it.
Compare with Expected: you should be able to view, rebind and disable AGI shortcuts.
items.needs: none
items.note: AGI's own Settings panel has no keyboard shortcut section, so rebinding and disabling happen in VS Code's editor. The row wording and menu items for changing or removing a key come from VS Code, not from this repository. The default key bindings are listed in apps/extension-vscode/package.json.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Account & Usage > AGI Cloud connected row > Edit your profile on Web
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud in the editor, then open the Command Palette and run "Code: Account & Usage".
Find the row "AGI Cloud connected" in the list that opens.
Click "Edit your profile on Web".
Your browser opens the account profile page on the AGI web app. Check that name, photo and email can be edited there and saved, and compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: In the editor, profile editing is only a link that opens /settings/profile in the browser; the extension itself has no name, photo or email editor.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Open Settings > Instructions & editor > Custom instructions
steps: Run "Code: Open Settings" from the Command Palette.
Click "Instructions & editor" in the left list.
In the "Custom instructions" card, type into the "Host default" box (or the workspace override box below it).

Click "Save host instructions" (or "Save workspace override"). Then start or open a developer chat and check that the instruction applies, and that clearing the box or changing it stops or changes it, as Expected says.
items.needs: none
items.note: The page says these instructions apply to developer sessions on this host; I did not find a separate on/off switch, only the text boxes, so switching off is presumably clearing the text, which I did not confirm.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts (also Add a memory fact and Turn account memory on or off)
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud, then run "Code: Memory" from the Command Palette.
Choose "Add a memory fact", type a fact, and confirm; then run "Code: Memory" again and choose "List & remove facts" to see it listed.
In the Memory list in the sidebar, hover a fact and use the edit icon (tooltip "Edit this fact") to change it, then use the trash icon (tooltip "Delete this fact") to remove one.

Run "Code: Memory" and choose "Turn account memory off" (it reads "Turn account memory on" when off), and check the placeholder line reads "Account memory off"/"on". Compare with Expected: memory on sends saved facts with chats, off stops them. The same switch is "Use saved memory facts" under Code: Open Settings > Instructions & editor > Memory.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The memory rows and edit/delete icons are sidebar row actions; I did not confirm the exact sidebar view name where they appear, and I did not verify that saved facts are used in chats beyond the code path.

items.needs: none
items.note: No crash-report or diagnostic-sharing choice found: a search for "crash" in apps/extension-vscode/src found nothing. Nearest controls: the Telemetry card in Settings ("Share usage events", apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/settingsWebviewContent.ts), which covers usage events only, and the manual "Code: Export Diagnostics" command (apps/extension-vscode/package.json), which creates a redacted report and is not a sharing choice. The cited line 1969 is the usage-events toggle, not crash reports.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Archived Sessions
steps: Run "Code: Archived Sessions" from the Command Palette. A list titled "Archived sessions" opens; if there are none, the message "Code: there are no archived sessions in this workspace." appears.

Select one or more sessions in the list, then click the "Restore" button (tooltip "Restore") or "Restore all listed sessions". Check that the session leaves the archived list and shows back in your sessions.
Select a session and click "Delete permanently" (the delete button), then confirm in the dialog. Check that the session is removed from the list and the message "Code: ... was deleted." appears.
Compare with Expected: list, restore and delete all work.
items.needs: a workspace with at least one archived chat
items.note: The same list is also reached from "Code: Show Sessions History" through its "Archived sessions" entry.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Remote Control (or type /remote-control in the chat box). The Remote Control panel shows Pair a phone, or Connected to {phone} with Disconnect phone.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and run Code: Remote Control. The panel titled Remote Control opens.
If a phone is paired, look for the line Connected to {phone} and the button Disconnect phone. If none is paired, you see Pair a phone and a QR code.
Click Disconnect phone. A dialog asks Disconnect {phone}? with the button Disconnect phone; confirm it.
Check that the panel no longer shows Connected to {phone} and returns to the pairing state, to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a paired phone (Mobile app) and a signed-in account; a second paired device is not shown in this panel
items.note: The VS Code panel lists only the one connected phone and offers Disconnect, not a list of all paired devices; browser-to-desktop pairing was not found in this feature. Web Settings > Account > Linked devices (Unlink device) covers linked CLI, VS Code, Chrome and desktop devices, not phones.

items.where: More actions (icon in the sidebar header) > Sign out, in the account row at the bottom of the menu. Also Command palette > Code: Sign Out of AGI Cloud.
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud from the sidebar so the account row shows your account.
Click the More actions button in the sidebar header.
Click Sign out in the menu, below the account name.
Look at the menu again: the account name should read Not signed in and the item should now read Sign in, to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account

labels.text: Code: Sign Out of AGI Cloud

items.note: Sign out runs at once with no confirmation dialog; if the AGI CLI on this machine stays signed in, a warning message appears.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Permissions (or type /permissions in the chat box). The picker opens with the title Saved approvals.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and run Code: Permissions, or type /permissions in the chat box.
Look for the picker titled Saved approvals with rows marked Always allowed or Always denied. If none are saved, the picker says No approvals are saved yet.
To have one to remove, first choose Always allow on an approval prompt in chat, then reopen Code: Permissions.
Click the remove action on a row and confirm Remove this saved approval?, then check the row is gone, to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a saved approval (made by choosing Always allow on an approval prompt) and a signed-in CLI
items.note: If the CLI offers permission rules, the picker title is Code, Permissions and shows a permissions view instead of Saved approvals, so the exact screen the tester sees may differ; the remove-confirmation wording was read from code only.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Choose Agent Mode, or Code: Open Settings > Agent mode. Mode names are Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass permissions.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P and run Code: Choose Agent Mode.
Pick Ask, then send a chat request that edits a file or runs a command.
Check the agent asks for approval before it acts.
Repeat with Auto (ordinary workspace edits run without prompting) and then Bypass permissions, which first asks for a risk confirmation; compare with Expected.
items.needs: a workspace folder open and trusted; Bypass permissions needs the separate risk confirmation
items.note: Expected says ask every time, auto-approve safe, autonomous; the code offers Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass permissions, and no mode is labelled autonomous, so the mapping is unknown.

items.where: Web app (not inside VS Code): Settings > Security > Turn on Advanced Account Security (panel titled Advanced Account Security).
steps: In the web app, sign in and open Settings, then the Security section.
Find the Advanced Account Security panel.
Click Turn on Advanced Account Security and follow its steps (passkeys or security keys, a code emailed to you, and recovery keys).
Once on, sign in again and check that a password or email code alone no longer gets you in, to compare with Expected.
items.needs: a web account with at least two passkeys or security keys and access to the email on the account
items.note: The VS Code app has no hardened-mode control; this is on the web account settings. The Settings > Security path comes from the support page apps/web/content/support/account-security.md, not from the navigation code, which was not verified.

items.where: Sidebar > onboarding screen > Permission docs
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and go to the onboarding screen that has the Permission docs link.
Click Permission docs.
Look at the browser that opens: it should be the docs page for permissions (URL contains topic=permissions), and the article should explain the permission settings shown on that screen.
items.needs: none (an internet connection to open the docs page)
items.note: This is the only per-screen help link found in the VS Code app. The Help menu's Documentation item opens the general docs page. The configuration and custom-instructions articles (apps/web/content/support) are not linked from the VS Code app. I did not check when the onboarding screen is shown.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Send Feedback > Report a Bug (also Sidebar > More actions > Help > Send feedback)
steps: Open the Command Palette and type Code: Send Feedback, or open the sidebar's More actions menu and choose Help > Send feedback.
Pick Report a Bug from the list.
Type a description in the box that reads Report a Bug: Describe your feedback, then press Enter.
Look for the notification that says your feedback reached the team. Compare with Expected: the form asks only for text, and the build and platform are sent with the report without being shown to you.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account (signed-out users get a Sign in prompt)
items.note: The sidebar More actions button was located from its markup (title More, aria-label More actions) but its visible position was not confirmed. The build and platform are added to the sent report silently, so the tester cannot see them in the UI.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Send Feedback > General Feedback
steps: Open the Command Palette and type Code: Send Feedback.
Pick General Feedback (description: Share thoughts about the extension).
Type a message in the box and press Enter.
Look for the notification that says your feedback reached the team. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The tester cannot see the stored record from inside the app; the code sends it to the server endpoint /api/feedback and labels it as general feedback.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Send Feedback > Feature Request
steps: Open the Command Palette and type Code: Send Feedback.
Pick Feature Request (description: Suggest a new feature or improvement).
Type the request in the box and press Enter.
Look for the notification that says your feedback reached the team. Compare with Expected.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The request is stored on the server as a feature-type report, which the tester cannot see from the app.

items.where: Command palette > Code: Export Diagnostics (also Sidebar > More actions > Help > Export diagnostics)
steps: Sign in to AGI Cloud (signed-out, the command shows a message and exports nothing).
Open the Command Palette and type Code: Export Diagnostics, or use Help > Export diagnostics from the sidebar's More actions menu.
Wait for the save dialog to open, then save the JSON file somewhere you choose.

Open the saved file and check its fields (for example collectedAt, surface, appVersion, platform, locale, recentEvents), then compare with Expected. Note the save dialog is the only point of choice: there is no preview in the app and no share-with-support button, so the tester attaches the file to support by hand. Cancelling the dialog writes nothing.
items.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account
items.note: The Expected line says the user can see what the bundle contains and choose to share it. The code only offers a save dialog after the server redacts the bundle; sharing with support is a manual step, and the Help item's description reads: A redacted report to attach when you contact support.

items.where: Sidebar chat > a message that fails > error message (the Reference: line)
steps: Send a chat message in the AGI Code sidebar.
Make the request fail (this cannot be set up on demand; it needs a failing request that the server answers with a typed failure).
Read the error message in the chat. It should end with Reference: followed by an id.
Copy the id and compare with Expected: the id must be one the user can quote to support.
items.needs: a request that fails with a server failure (not controllable from the app)
items.note: The reference is shown only when the failure carries a requestId and the turn failure is the typed kind. A failure without that id shows no reference. I did not confirm that the reference text can be copied, and I could not find a way to trigger a failure on demand.

items.where: Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P) > Code: Remote Control. The same command is also typed in the chat as /remote-control. The panel shows the Pair a phone link.
steps: Open a folder in VS Code and trust it (a trusted workspace is required), then sign in to your AGI account.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, type Code: Remote Control, and press Enter.
In the panel that opens, read the text that starts 'Open the Mobile app on your phone, choose Pair with Desktop, and scan this code' and check that a pairing code appears.

Click Pair a phone if no code is shown, then (with the phone) scan the code, confirm the phone in the dialog, and check that the status bar item shows 'Remote Control: waiting for your phone', then 'Remote Control: {phone}' once connected.
items.needs: a trusted folder open in VS Code, an AGI account signed in, and a phone with the AGI Mobile app signed in to the same account

labels.text: Remote Control: waiting for your phone

items.note: The phone-side pairing and watching/approving happen in the Mobile app, whose code is outside this folder, so only the desktop side was checked. The panel title was not confirmed in the code.

items.where: Chat panel > model button (shows Auto) > On this device group. Ollama and LM Studio status rows appear in that group.
steps: Make sure Ollama is not running (quit it), then open the AGI chat panel.
Click the model button that shows Auto, and look at the group named On this device.

Check for a row that reads 'Ollama is not running. Start it to use its models.' (the same shape shows 'LM Studio is not running' for LM Studio), and check that the reason text appears if the server does not respond ('Ollama is not responding: ...').
Start Ollama, reopen the model menu, and check that the row now reads 'Ollama is running · N models' (or 'Ollama is running with no models loaded') to compare with Expected.
items.needs: Ollama or LM Studio installed on this computer (to see the running state); with neither installed, the not-running row still appears

labels.text: {provider} is not running. Start it to use its models.

items.note: The health rows are shown inside the model menu only, not as a separate status indicator; the generic Code: Show Subsystem Health command (apps/extension-vscode/package.json) covers subsystems in general and was not confirmed to list the local runtime. The Auto label is the default text on the model button; the model button's hover title is Model. Whether the rows appear when the local runtime is not started at all (before the first model list loads) was not verified.

items.needs: none
items.note: The cited line apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:1880 is writer hand-off code (releaseWriter, takeOverWriter), not email. Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for gmail, email, mailbox and forwarded and found no email intake, matching the plan's 'not written yet'.

items.where: AGI Code panel > Sessions button in the panel header > Local tab > the row whose label reads Desktop
steps: Start a coding session in the desktop app for a folder, then open the same folder in VS Code.
Click the AGI Code icon in the activity bar, then click the Sessions button in the panel header.
On the Local tab, find the row labelled Desktop and click it.
Look: the earlier messages of the desktop session load in the chat, and you can send a new message that continues it.
items.needs: a session started in the desktop app in the same folder
items.note: The Desktop label comes from the session origin the runtime reports. Resuming refuses with 'The developer session workspace does not match its owning local runtime' if the folder differs (packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json). Whether a given desktop session is listed depends on the runtime, which was not checked.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Remote Control, then the Remote Control panel shows the pairing code; on the phone, the Mobile app > Pair with Desktop
steps: In VS Code open the Command Palette and run Code: Remote Control.
Read the Remote Control panel: it shows a pairing QR code and a Pairing code.
On the phone, open the Mobile app, choose Pair with Desktop, and scan the code.
When the warning box asks to allow the phone, click Allow this phone.
From the phone send a new request, then check that the approval prompts appear on this computer and the result shows on the phone.
items.needs: a phone with the Mobile app, signed in to the same account
items.note: The phone steps depend on the Mobile app, which was not checked. The pairing text is in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json (remote.howToPair). The cited code is in packages/platform/utils/src/remoteControl/codeRemoteController.ts and was not run.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Continue in the Cloud, or the chat command /cloud, or Sessions > Cloud tab > Continue in the cloud button
steps: Open a folder whose git remote is on GitHub and check out a branch that has been pushed to GitHub.
Open the AGI Code panel and run Code: Continue in the Cloud from the Command Palette, or type /cloud in the chat.
If the warning appears, read it: it asks you to check out a branch, push the branch, or open a GitHub folder.
Otherwise a cloud session opens; check that it names the repository and branch of this folder.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a folder on a pushed GitHub branch, and AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 (per the plan)
items.note: The Sessions button only shows the cloud button on the Cloud tab. The refusal texts are in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/continueInCloud.ts.

items.where: AGI Code panel > Sessions button > Cloud tab > click the cloud session row > Bring the branch in (or Command Palette > Code: Open AGI Code Session)
steps: Run a cloud coding session that works on a branch of a GitHub repository open in this window.
Click Sessions in the AGI Code panel header, then the Cloud tab, then click that session's row.
In the list that opens, choose the item labelled Bring the branch in; its description shows the branch name.
Look: the folder moves to that branch only after you choose it, and the checkout guard runs before it changes.
items.needs: a signed-in account, a cloud session with a working branch, and AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 (per the plan)
items.note: The item only appears when the session has a branch and a GitHub repository. The same text also appears in a message after a cloud handoff link is opened.

items.where: Command Palette > Code: Show Projects > click a project > Use in this chat
steps: Sign in and open Code: Show Projects from the Command Palette.
Click a project that has instructions or files, then choose Use in this chat in the list that opens.
Send a message in the AGI Code chat that the project's instructions cover.
Look: the reply follows the project's instructions, and the project is shown as in use; choosing Used in this chat again stops using it.
items.needs: a signed-in account and a project with instructions or files
items.note: The cited ChatStateManager.ts:5122 is the reference-attaching path, not the project path. The project is applied near apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:5354 (getActiveCloudProject). The CLI citation apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:875 was not checked.

items.where: AGI Code panel > chat: send a message when the account is at its usage limit > error card under the reply
steps: Use up the usage allowance on the account, then send a message in the AGI Code chat.
Read the error card: it says that you have reached a usage limit and when it resets, or how long to wait.
If the card shows Continue with {model}, click it and check that the reply continues on that model in the same turn.
Otherwise click Add credits, Compare plans or See your usage, which open a web page; or run Code: Upgrade Your Plan from the Command Palette.
items.needs: an account that has used up its usage allowance
items.note: The Continue with button appears only when the server names an eligible alternative model. The reset time text depends on the server, and the page the buttons open is set by the server reply.

items.where: AGI Code panel > chat: a card appears in the chat that says {server} needs you to sign in again > click Sign in and continue
steps: Connect an MCP server that uses a sign-in, then ask for a task that needs it.
Let that server's sign-in expire while the task is running.
When the card appears, click Sign in and continue and finish the sign-in in the browser.
Look: the card changes to Signed in to {server}. AGI is continuing., and the interrupted turn resumes with a continue message.
items.needs: an MCP server that needs a sign-in, a way to expire that sign-in, and an outside account

labels.text: {server} needs you to sign in again. AGI could not use it for this step.

items.note: The card appears only when the runtime sends an mcp/authRequired signal during a turn (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts). How to trigger that signal on demand was not confirmed.
